Major Update to v3.1.0: Deno Support and Status Command

  Overview

  This PR introduces full support for Deno 2.0+ as a first-class package manager and a new status command designed for
  CI/CD environments and advanced configuration inspection.

  Key Changes

  🦕 Deno Support

   - Full Integration: Added Deno as a supported package manager with comprehensive command translations (install, add,
     remove, task, test, publish).
   - Smart Detection: Enhanced the detection engine to prioritize deno.json and deno.jsonc files, ensuring correct
     environment identification in hybrid projects.
   - Version Handling: Implemented a specialized helper to parse and clean Deno's multi-line version output.

  📊 New status Command

   - Flexible Formatting: Introduced swpm status (alias s) with support for json and plain text outputs.
   - Property Filtering: Support for deep property access via paths (e.g., swpm status json:versions.node or swpm status
     plain:using).
   - CI Ready: Validated error handling for missing properties, returning clear error messages and appropriate exit
     codes for automation scripts.

  🛠 Technical Improvements

   - TypeScript Integrity: Performed a project-wide cleanup of strict typing issues, eliminating implicit any types and
     ensuring safe access to potentially undefined objects.
   - Unified Dev Environment: Simplified the contributor setup in DEVS.md with a single command for all global
     dependencies.

     scenarios.

   - Enhanced CHEATSHEET.md with a new column for Deno command comparisons.

     command formats.

body:
## Summary
Epic 3 PR B follow-up: closes the deferred half of PR B by extending `Supervisor.createAgent` to mint+register an Agent's pub identity when the source Identity declares a `pub:` block. Symmetrical with `cli.user.init` from PR B. Stacked on PR B (#20).

After this lands, the seed-team install flow is:
```
2200 daemon start
2200 pub create ops
2200 pub start ops
2200 user init --display-name "Doug"   # mints + registers user
2200 agent create poe --identity poe.identity.md   # mints + registers Agent
```
Both the user and Agent have pub identities provisioned end-to-end.

## What's in this PR
- **`writeIdentity()`** in `src/runtime/identity/loader.ts` — atomic write of an Identity file with schema validation. Mirrors `writeUserIdentity` from PR B.
- **`Supervisor.createAgent` extended** with optional `pub` and `identityClientFactory` opts. Routes through a private `provisionAgentPubIdentity` helper. No-op when the Identity has no `pub:` block (non-pub Agent). Skips mint when `pub.identity` is already non-empty (pre-provisioned, e.g., on supervisor restart).
- **`cli.agent.create` RPC** params extended with optional `pub`.
- **`2200 agent create` CLI** extended with `--pub <name>` for the multi-pub case.
- **Schema relaxation** on `AgentPubBlock.issuer_url`: removed `min(1)` so user-authored Identity templates can declare an empty `issuer_url` (means "to be provisioned"). The supervisor always writes a non-empty value back (`local://<host>:<port>` or `local://unregistered`).

## Tests
- **+8 tests, 375 total** (was 367 after PR B).
- `tests/runtime/supervisor/agent-pub-identity.test.ts`:
  - No `pub:` block in source → non-pub Agent (no credential file written, identity.md unchanged).
  - `pub:` block, no pub running → keypair minted + persisted, identity.md patched with empty `pub.identity` and `local://unregistered` issuer (deferred registration).
  - `pub:` block + running pub → full registration via fake `http.Server` mirroring v0.3.2 LOCAL_TRUST contract; `pub.identity` filled in with assigned UUID v7.
  - Multi-pub ambiguity → errors clearly when no `--pub` picked; respects `--pub` when given; rejects unknown pub names.
  - Raw YAML sanity check on the patched identity.md.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm verify` green locally (typecheck + lint + format + 375 tests + build).
- [x] Stacked on PR #20; merge after #20 lands.
- [ ] CI green.

## Note
v0.3.3 of `@openpub-ai/pub-server` shipped today (Doug + Poe bug-fix release). Pin stays at `0.3.1` per Doug's sequencing for PRs A/B/E; PR F bumps to whatever's current at smoke-test time.

body:
### Motivation
- Production startup previously depended on shell-based `.env` loading and missed critical PM2 runtime variables, so startup must be repeatable and shell-safe. 
- The `.env` file is not guaranteed to be shell-safe, so `set -a; . ./.env` is unreliable and must be replaced with `dotenv`-based loading. 
- The sessions table schema required a `token_hash` column and migration must be idempotent and safe to run multiple times even if it invalidates legacy sessions.

### Description
- Add `ecosystem.config.cjs` at repo root which loads the live `.env` via `dotenv`, fixes `cwd` to `/home/duc/ret2-member-portal`, sets `name: 'ret2-member-portal'`, `script: 'src/app.js'`, `instances: 1`, `autorestart: true`, `watch: false`, and `max_memory_restart: '512M'`, and supports `--env production` for repeatable PM2 start. 
- Harden `src/db.js` startup logic to compute `PRAGMA table_info(sessions)`, require the columns including `token_hash`, and if the schema is legacy/non-conformant, rebuild `sessions` and its indexes inside a transaction; code includes comments that legacy sessions are intentionally invalidated because older rows cannot be converted to `token_hash`. 
- Update `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` with production-safe PM2 start and restart commands (`pm2 start ecosystem.config.cjs --env production` and `pm2 restart ret2-member-portal --update-env`), health verification commands (`curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/health` and `curl -s https://mem.hanauda.online/health`), and an explicit warning not to source `.env` directly. 
- Files changed: `ecosystem.config.cjs`, `src/db.js`, and `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`.

- Ran `npm run check` and it completed successfully with no syntax errors.

author: talwgx
body:
## Why

Salvage of [#39](https://github.com/log-10x/log10x-mcp/pull/39), with the substantive scale/capability/coverage work ported through the `streamer→retriever` rename.

Five user-visible improvements that surfaced during dual-reviewer (Claude Opus + Grok-4) plan reviews against the otel-demo env:

1. **`doctor` scale block** — first call on an unfamiliar env now reports 7d volume, service count, pattern count, events-per-pattern compression. Agent sizes its strategy from this; without it, agents either over-poll or under-target on high-volume envs.

2. **`doctor` capability enumeration** — explicit list of question types the retriever unlocks when deployed, or that are out of reach when not. Tells the agent honestly whether to attempt a long-window historical query or route the user elsewhere.

3. **`services` top-N coverage** — "Top 3 services = 87% of volume" appended to the standard list. The number changes how the agent recommends drill-downs.

4. **`top_patterns` scope coverage** — "Top 10 = 18% of total volume in scope / 82% in the long tail" appended. At high volume this is load-bearing — Top-10 capturing 18% vs 92% changes the next-action recommendation entirely.

5. **`retrieverNotConfiguredMessage` upgrade** — replaces the plain "to enable, do X" list with three sections: what's out of reach, what the agent can do RIGHT NOW (deploy / rehydrate from cold tier / rescope to hot retention), and how to deploy later. Gives the agent immediate options instead of just a deployment guide.

## What changed in this salvage

Original PR was on `feat/capability-framing-and-scale-context` against pre-rename `streamer-*` files. This PR is a manual port:

- `isStreamerConfigured()` → `isRetrieverConfigured()`
- "Storage Streamer deployed" → "Retriever deployed"
- "log10x_streamer_query" references → not applicable (the salvage doesn't touch index.ts)
- File paths: `src/tools/streamer-query.ts` → `src/tools/retriever-query.ts`

## Deferred from the original PR

The full **server-instructions reframe** (`DIFFERENTIATORS` section, `SCOPE`, out-of-lane / SIEM-MCP escape valve, daily-habit row reorganization) — substantial 100+ line text rewrite to `src/index.ts` that needs careful integration with the rename. The capability enumeration in `doctor` (point 2 above) carries the most load-bearing piece; the rest is incremental polish that can ship later as a focused text-only PR.

## Tests

Existing suite green: 348 pass, 0 fail.

body:
## Summary

Audit cleanup before Stream A/B fan-out. Closes #11.

## Why

The audit before launching parallel agent sessions surfaced six issues. Each is small individually, but together they would have wasted 5-15 min per agent session and risked one real merge conflict (Codex's Firecrawl plan vs Stream B). This PR ships them as one bundle.

## Changes

- **B2 (op-run account):** Every documented `op run` uses `--account my.1password.com` so it picks the right vault. Without it, bash sessions either pick the wrong account or time out on biometric auth.
- **New bug found during audit (dotenv loads op refs):** `config.py` was using `load_dotenv(.env.local)` at import time, pushing the `op://` references into `os.environ` as literal strings. Downstream code treated those as real secrets (psycopg dialled `op://` as the DSN, live-db tests stopped skipping). Loader now uses `dotenv_values`, skips `op://` values, and only sets vars not already in the parent env.
- **C4 (Workflow auto-move):** `scripts/start_issue.sh` moves the Project card to `In Progress` via `gh project item-edit` on claim. Falls back to a print if the issue isn't on the board.
- **C5 (finish_issue grep):** `-B1` → `-B2` so the worktree-detection grep finds the matching directory line in `git worktree list --porcelain` output.
- **C2 (PROGRESS rule):** AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, PR template loosened to "milestones only" so parallel PRs don't serialise on conflicts in one file.
- **F3 (dead dep):** drop unused `responses` dev dep.

Plus one file reformatted under the current black version.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest -q` passes (88 pass, 2 skipped — live-db tests skip cleanly now thanks to the dotenv fix)
- [x] `ruff check .` passes
- [x] `black --check .` passes

- [x] Manual smoke: this PR was created from a worktree spawned by the new `start_issue.sh`, so the Workflow auto-move and the worktree path were dogfooded

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
The E2E tab-switching test in `runs-flow-runs.spec.ts` was failing with a 30s timeout when trying to click the "Go to next page" button.

### Root Cause

The test creates 6 flow runs (3 COMPLETED, 3 FAILED) and navigates with `limit=5`. After filtering to "Completed", only 3 runs remain — fitting on one page — so the next-page button becomes disabled. A race condition between the filter URL update and the data re-render caused `isEnabled()` to return `true` (stale unfiltered state), then `click()` hung on the now-disabled button until the test timeout.

### Fix

- Reduce `limit` from `5` to `2` so that even after filtering to Completed (3 runs), pagination is still needed (2 pages). The button stays enabled through the data transition, eliminating the race.
- Replace the racy `isEnabled()` guard with `toBeEnabled()` assertion that properly retries via Playwright's auto-waiting.

Failed workflow run: https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/actions/runs/24974563012

### Motivation
- Bring the Bilardo Shqip table footprint, pocket geometry and visible rail elements into parity with the reference Pool Royale table so gameplay spacing, visuals and aim feel match across billiards modes.
- Use the same placement logic for cue respot and rack anchor to ensure shots, rack positions and camera framing remain consistent with Pool Royale.
- Surface-level UI/visual parity (pockets, pocket radii, chalk blocks) improves onboarding and reduces mode-specific tuning differences.

### Description
- Updated `webapp/src/pages/Games/BilardoShqipGame.tsx` to change the table footprint and spacing: `CFG.tableW`/`CFG.tableL` and related rail/cushion parameters (e.g., `railW`, `railInset`, `cushionT`, `edgeMargin`).
- Replaced static respot/rack offsets with calculations derived from `CFG.tableL` by introducing `CUE_BALL_RESPOT` and moving the rack anchor to `-CFG.tableL * 0.215` so cue and rack scale with table size.

body:
## 概要

Book / BookAuthor モデルから UI・ロジックで参照されていない 6 項目を削除するリファクタ。

Closes #108

## 背景（Why）

リリース前の現状、Book モデルには UI/ロジックで一切参照されない飾りフィールドが複数存在していた。値の設定や検証ロジック（Cloud Functions / firestore.rules / テスト）が無駄なメンテ負担になっており、新規絵本追加時にも値の設定で都度判断が必要だった。リリース前で後方互換不要のため一括掃除する。必要になれば再追加は容易。

## 実装内容（What）

### 削除対象（6 項目）
- `BookCategory` enum + `Book.categoryId` — UI 露出ゼロ
- `Book.viewCount` — どこでもインクリメントされず UI 表示なし
- `Book.titleJa` / `Book.descriptionJa` getter — 完全未使用、`title.localized(...)` で代替済
- `BookAuthor.avatarUrl` — BookAuthor 経由では UI に表示されない
- `Book.pageCount` — `pages.length` で導出可能、viewer cover は `pages.length` に置換
- `Book.publishedAt` — 「最新公開順」未実装、recommended は `createdAt` を使用

### 保持
- `Book.updatedAt` — Cloud Functions の `submitBookForReview` が書き込む audit field
- `Book.authorUid` — `firestore.rules` の `resource.data.authorUid == request.auth.uid` で使用
- `User.avatarUrl` — User モデル側、BookAuthor とは別物

## 影響範囲

### Flutter (`lib/`)
- `features/book/domain/book.dart` — enum / フィールド / fromJson / toJson / == / hashCode 整理
- `features/book/data/mock_books.dart` — 9 冊から該当行除去
- `features/home/presentation/home_page.dart` — skeleton placeholder 更新
- `features/book/presentation/widgets/viewer_cover_page.dart` — `book.pageCount` → `book.pages.length` に置換

### Firestore / Cloud Functions
- `firestore.rules` — `categoryId` / `pageCount` / `viewCount` / `publishedAt` 不変チェック 4 行を削除
- `functions/src/books/createBook.ts` — `parseCategoryId` 関数 / `categoryId` 検証 / `viewCount=0` / `publishedAt=null` / `pageCount` 書込を削除、AuthorCopy から `avatarUrl` 削除
- `functions/src/books/submitBookForReview.ts` — `isCategoryId` 検証 / `pageCount === pages.length` 検証を削除
- `functions/src/books/types.ts` — `CATEGORY_IDS` / `CategoryId` 型を削除
- `functions/src/books/validators.ts` — `isCategoryId` 関数を削除

### テスト
- Flutter: `book_model_test.dart` / `widget_test.dart` / `book_viewer_page_test.dart` / `books_providers_test.dart` / `my_page_likes_grid_test.dart`
- Functions: `createBook.test.ts` / `submitBookForReview.test.ts`

### ドキュメント
- `document/01_事業計画書.md`
- `document/02_firestoreデータモデル設計書.md`
- `document/02_FDD/07_投稿・審査フロー機能設計書.md`
- `document/05_絵本制作ガイド.md`

### Sprint Contract / QA 評価
- `.harness/current-sprint.md` を Issue #108 用に更新
- `.harness/evaluations/2026-04-27-1145.md`（初回 FAIL: rules で `viewCount`/`publishedAt` 残存を検出）
- `.harness/evaluations/2026-04-27-1200.md`（修正後 PASS）

## テスト結果

- [x] `flutter analyze` — No issues
- [x] `flutter test` — 211/211 PASS
- [x] `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib test` — Clean
- [x] `npm --prefix functions run lint && build && test` — PASS（37/37）
- [x] QA Gate（Agent 独立評価）— PASS

## レビュー観点

1. **削除網羅性**: `BookCategory` / `categoryId` / `viewCount` / `titleJa` / `descriptionJa` / `BookAuthor.avatarUrl` / `pageCount` / `publishedAt` が `lib/`・`functions/`・`test/`・`firestore.rules`・`document/` 全層から漏れなく消えているか
2. **保持の正しさ**: `Book.updatedAt` / `Book.authorUid` / `BookAuthor.uid` / `BookAuthor.displayName` / `User.avatarUrl` が無傷か
3. **firestore.rules**: 不変チェック 4 行（`categoryId` / `pageCount` / `viewCount` / `publishedAt`）の削除のみで、`authorUid` / `author` / `likeCount` / `createdAt` / `submittedAt` / `updatedAt == request.time` は無傷か
4. **viewer cover**: 「全◯ページ」表示が `pages.length` で正しく出るか
5. **pageCount の l10n キー**: `lib/l10n/` の `pageCount` は `pageCount(int count)` 関数名（i18n キー）として残しており、`book.pageCount` フィールドとは別物。混同せず削除対象外として扱っている

body:
## Summary

Implements the items from the audit you selected: **6.1, 6.2, 6.3, 6.10, 6.11, 6.12, 6.13, 6.14, 6.15**. All changes are frontend-only.

**6.1 — Screenshot gallery no longer crops output.**
`ScreenshotGallery` switched from `object-cover` → `object-contain` on a checkered background so screenshots are letterboxed instead of cropped. Empty state was rebuilt as a real status card.
`frontend/src/components/ScreenshotGallery.tsx`

**6.2 — Friendly 409 handling on every wizard.**
- New typed error `RunRejectedError` parses the backend's `{reason: 'in_flight' | 'duplicate'}` body in `streamSse` and `postJson`.
- `useGenerate` now exposes `state.rejectedReason` and a human message (`"Another run is in progress…"` / `"Same payload submitted seconds ago…"`).
- Each wizard (TextToVideo, HtmlToVideo, ImageToVideo) renders a new `BackendRejectedBanner` with an "Open Processes" button instead of a raw `SSE request failed: 409 …` string.
`frontend/src/api/client.ts`, `frontend/src/hooks/useGenerate.ts`, `frontend/src/components/BackendRejectedBanner.tsx`, `frontend/src/pages/{TextToVideo,HtmlToVideo,ImageToVideo}.tsx`

**6.3 — Global ErrorBoundary.**
Top-level boundary wraps the entire `<App />`. Renders a recoverable card with reload / try-again / copy-details actions instead of a blank white screen.
`frontend/src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx`, `frontend/src/main.tsx`

**6.10 — A11y fixes on `Toggle` / `Section`.**
- `Toggle` is now a real `<input type="checkbox" role="switch">` with `htmlFor`/`aria-describedby` and visually-hidden focus.
- `Section` (collapsible cards in `SettingsPanel`) wires `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls` to the panel and gives the panel `role="region"` + `aria-labelledby`.
`frontend/src/components/Toggle.tsx`, `frontend/src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx`

**6.11 — Sidebar backend status is clickable.**
`SidebarFooter` is now a `NavLink` to `/settings`. When offline, the label turns rose and the title attribute hints "open Settings to ping or change the URL".
`frontend/src/components/Layout.tsx`

**6.12 — pptx/video output disabled upstream when backend isn't Windows.**
`OutputFormatPicker` (extracted from `ProjectStep`) calls `useBackendPlatform()`. On non-Windows backends the PowerPoint and MP4 buttons are greyed out, labelled "Windows", and show a tooltip explaining why. The existing `WindowsOnlyWarning` still renders for Windows hosts as a heads-up.
`frontend/src/pages/TextToVideo.tsx`

**6.13 — Recent-screenshots carousel on Home.**
A new horizontal-scroll strip ("Latest output / Fresh from your last runs") shows up to 12 thumbnails from successful runs, each linking back to its run on `/processes`. Hidden when no successful runs exist yet.

author: octaviantocan
body:
## What

Wires up the bot's self-introspection commands and ships the Docker
packaging needed to run relay in a container. All three commands are
fully implemented in `status.rs` — this PR connects them to the
Telegram command handler, captures `claude --version` at boot, and
adds the Dockerfile / compose / entrypoint / seed workspace.

## Commands

| Command | Output |
|---|---|
| `/status` | Uptime, model, current session ID, last activity, claude version |
| `/version` | Relay version (Cargo.toml), Claude CLI version (captured at boot) |
| `/whoami` | Owner ID, chat ID, user ID, workspace path |
| `/help` | Lists the four commands above + `/reset` |

## Sample output

```
/status
📊 relay status

model:         claude-opus-4-5
session id:    abc123…xyz
claude:        2.1.114 (Claude Code)
uptime:        3h 12m
last activity: 7m ago

/version
relay v0.2.0
claude 2.1.114 (Claude Code)

/whoami
owner id:  7424950903
chat id:   7424950903
user id:   7424950903
workspace: /workspace
```

## Scope (also includes)

This PR is intentionally bundled — the commands aren't useful on their
own; you need a container to introspect:

- **Docker setup**: `Dockerfile` (multi-stage rust build + claude CLI),
  `docker-compose.yml`, `docker/entrypoint.sh` (workspace seed on first
  run + auth sanity check), `.dockerignore`, `docker/README.md`
- **Workspace seed**: `workspace/.agent/{protocols,skills,memory}` —
  permissions, delegation rules, rust-test/ops/gbackup/debug skills,
  routing `MEMORY.md` + project/topic/people seed files
- **Doc rename**: `docs/openclaw-patterns.md` → properly attributed to
  Hermes (different system from OpenClaw)
- **Status plumbing**: `BotMeta` runtime state, duration formatters,
  `kill_on_drop` claude version probe with 5s timeout

## Testing

```
cargo test --all-targets         →  144 tests passing (114 + 6 + 24)
cargo clippy -- -D warnings      →  clean
```

## Review fixes applied
- `/status` snapshots before `touch_activity()` so idle reflects real
  gap, not 0s
- `command_handler` calls `touch_activity()` so command-only sessions
  don't read "never"
- SQLite errors on `/status` log via `warn!` instead of being silently
  flattened
- `claude --version` probe uses `kill_on_drop(true)` to prevent orphan
  processes if it hangs
- `to_string_lossy` on workspace path instead of allocating
  `display().to_string()`
- `.dockerignore` keeps tracked seed dirs (`people/`, `projects/`,
  `topics/`) so `MEMORY.md` references resolve in containers
- `bot.rs` has docstrings on every export and inline WHY comments

author: tim-chaplin
body:
## Summary
\`Best\`'s per-permutation Log copy was the dominant allocator in the eval hot path: \`snapshotCarry\`'s Log slice clone alone was ~22% of allocated bytes, called W times per chain × N chains × 10k turns. Yet 99.99% of those copies are throwaway — Log is only consumed when \`recordBestTurn\` fires (~13× per eval, when a turn becomes the new deck-level best).

Adds a \`SkipLog\` field on \`TurnState\`. \`appendLog\` still credits Value (the solver's tally is unchanged) but elides the Log slice append. The eval loop runs every turn with \`SkipLog=true\` via a new \`e.BestWithTriggersSkipLog\` entry point. When \`recordTurnStats\` reports a new deck-best, the loop replays that one turn with \`SkipLog=false\` to materialise the chain trace for the printout. \`Best\` is deterministic given inputs, so the replay reproduces the same Value / BestLine / CarryState plus a populated Log.

Refactors \`recordTurnStats\`: it returns whether \`stats.Best\` should be replaced, leaving the \`recordBestTurn\` clone to the caller so the SkipLog \`TurnSummary\` isn't cloned uselessly when the caller plans to overwrite with the replayed result.

## vs current main on \`BenchmarkEvalRealDeck\` (\`-benchtime=10x\`)
| metric | current main | + defer Log | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| ns/op | 21,429,573,430 | 19,529,685,370 | **−8.9%** |
| B/op | 10,788,091,385 | 7,989,342,200 | **−25.9%** |
| allocs/op | 125,849,522 | 97,236,654 | **−22.7%** |

## Sanity check
\`fabsim eval viserai_v4 -incoming 5 -deep-shuffles 10000\`: wall-clock 20.96s (matches the bench), printed best-turn chain trace is fully populated with the expected per-step lines and trigger sub-entries.

## Behavioural guarantees
- \`Best\` is deterministic given inputs. SkipLog and full-Log runs produce identical Value, BestLine, CarryState (excluding Log).
- \`hand.BestWithTriggers\` (existing public entry point) keeps populating Log — direct callers / tests that read \`State.Log\` are unaffected.
- The SkipLog-then-replay pattern lives entirely inside the deck-eval loop; no card-side changes needed.

## Test plan
- [x] \`go build ./...\`
- [x] \`go test ./...\`
- [x] Real \`fabsim eval\` printed output verified (chain trace, value, mean all match expectations).

author: ohah
body:
## 요약

- direct re-export barrel에서 사용되지 않은 source export body가 static import fanout을 살리는 문제를 줄였습니다.
- `export { x } from "./src"`의 export 관찰 가능성과 source module evaluation 필요성을 분리했습니다.
- source module 자체의 top-level side effect는 보존하되, dead export body 안에서만 참조되는 static import는 더 이상 전파하지 않습니다.
- unresolved direct re-export seeding은 전체 모듈 include fallback 대신 미해결로 둡니다.

## 변경 사항

- entry/context module만 초기 include하고, 일반 side-effectful module은 실제 evaluation dependency 경로에서 include되도록 변경했습니다.
- included module의 import record evaluation 전파를 정밀화했습니다.
  - `side_effect`, `re_export`, `require`, worker/glob/context 계열은 보수적으로 유지합니다.
  - `static_import`는 entry이거나 reachable statement에서 해당 binding이 실제 참조될 때만 source evaluation fanout을 유지합니다.
- reachable statement가 없는 included pure module의 import binding이 가짜 used export를 만들지 않도록 차단했습니다.
- direct re-export source side-effect와 dead export 내부 import 제거를 고정하는 output-level 회귀 테스트를 추가했습니다.

## Svelte smoke 영향

현재 브랜치 smoke 결과:

| Project | ZTS |
| --- | ---: |
| svelte | 1.5KB |
| svelte-mount | 77KB |
| svelte-mount-min | 35KB |
| svelte-full | 100KB |
| svelte-full-min | 47KB |

기존 관찰값 기준 `svelte-mount-min`은 44KB → 35KB로 감소했습니다. `svelte-full-min`은 47KB로 변화가 없어서, 남은 크기 차이는 direct re-export fanout과 별도 reachable path로 보입니다.

## 검증

- `zig build test -Dtest-filter="TreeShaking"`
- `zig build test -Dtest-filter="re-export"`
- `zig build test`
- `zig build`
- `cd tests/integration && bun test tests/tree-shake-precision.test.ts`
- `cd tests/benchmark && bun run smoke.ts --filter=svelte` (5/5 OK, 5/5 MATCH)
- pre-push hook 통과 (`zig fmt --check`, `zig build test`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`; oxlint는 기존 warning만, 0 errors)

body:
## Summary

Cleanup group **C10** from `.planning/trajectory/pr-comment-catalog/TRIAGE.md`. Addresses 14 review threads on PRs #102, #103, #107, #108 covering the cargo-mutants config layout, the mutants/dudect CI lanes, and the fuzz cocoverage script.

## Changes

### cargo-mutants config consolidation (PR #102)
- cargo-mutants 25.x only reads `.cargo/mutants.toml` at the workspace root; per-crate `crates/<name>/mutants.toml` files were inert. Even when loaded via `--config`, glob entries with path separators are matched relative to the source-tree root.
- Additionally, cargo-mutants discovers source files via `mod` declarations and does not expand `include!`. `chio-credentials/src/lib.rs` `include!`s 13 trust-boundary files (only `trust_tier` is a real `mod`); `chio-policy/src/evaluate.rs` `include!`s its `evaluate/{context,engine,matchers,outcomes,tests}.rs` siblings.
- Consolidate all per-crate scope into the workspace-root config with workspace-rooted globs. Mutate the umbrella file (`lib.rs` for credentials, `evaluate.rs` for policy) where `include!` is in play.
- Delete the four inert per-crate files. Update `docs/fuzzing/mutants.md`.

### mutants.yml gate flip + diff file (PR #103)
- Drop job-level `continue-on-error` from `mutants-pr` so `scripts/mutants-gate.sh`'s exit propagates, allowing the M02 P3 release-boundary `cycle_end_tag` flip to actually convert the lane from advisory to blocking. `mutants-nightly` keeps `continue-on-error: true` (dashboard-only, never gates a PR).
- `--in-diff` now receives a unified-diff text file path (captured via `git diff origin/<base>...HEAD > <file>`) rather than a git ref. cargo-mutants 25.x expects a file, not a ref.

### dudect.yml + threshold script (PR #107)
- `gh run list` in the correlate job now filters `status == "completed"` so an in-progress / queued / failed run cannot be selected as the prior baseline.
- `scripts/check-dudect-threshold.sh`:
  - `extract_max_abs_t` emits `%.17g` (round-trip f64) instead of `%.4f` so borderline values like `4.49996` are no longer rounded up to `4.5` and misclassified as FAIL. The verdict comparison itself was already done at full `awk + 0.0` precision; only the printed/returned value was being truncated.
  - Reject non-numeric / zero / negative `--threshold` via `is_positive_number` before the value gets coerced to `0` by `awk + 0.0` (which would otherwise misclassify almost every harness output as FAIL and fire spurious sustained-leak issues under the two-run rule).
  - Self-test now compares numerically rather than by string equality so the new round-trip representation does not break the dry-run gate.

### Cocoverage script (PR #108)
- Per-survivor replay now drives `cargo mutants` itself (`--file`/`--line` + `--test-tool` wrapper) so the fuzz corpus exercises the **mutated** binary prepared in cargo-mutants' temp tree, not the clean source tree (root cause of the cocoverage signal corruption).
- Drop per-target deduplication of survivors; two mutants in the same file may exercise disjoint paths and the corpus might catch one but not the other.
- jq path extraction now reads `.scenario.mutant.source_file.path` (it is an object with a `.path` sub-field per the cargo-mutants schema, matching `scripts/mutants-comment.sh`) plus `.scenario.mutant.span.start.line` for the per-mutant line argument.
- Non-jq fallback matches the literal `"MissedMutant"` tag cargo-mutants emits; the previous `"Missed"` pattern was never a substring because the next character is `M`, not `"`. Count-only path now states clearly that no mutated-binary replay happens without jq.

## Threads addressed

- PR #102: r3144127594, r3144132735, r3144132736
- PR #103: r3144137926, r3144146511, r3144146515
- PR #107: r3144173070, r3144173073, r3144182112
- PR #108: r3144171683, r3144171685, r3144180213, r3144180215, r3144180217

## Test plan

- [x] `actionlint .github/workflows/mutants.yml .github/workflows/dudect.yml` clean
- [x] `bash -n` and `shellcheck` clean on both scripts
- [x] `bash scripts/check-dudect-threshold.sh --dry-run` passes
- [x] Borderline 4.49996 now classifies as PASS (was FAIL); 61.61472 classifies as FAIL
- [x] `--threshold abc / -1 / 0` rejected with exit 2
- [x] No em-dashes (U+2014) in changed files
- [ ] cargo-mutants / cargo-fuzz lanes themselves require special toolchains and were not exercised in this PR; CI provides the live signal.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Medium risk because it changes CI gating behavior (mutants PR lane can become blocking via `scripts/mutants-gate.sh`) and alters how dudect baselines and cocoverage verdicts are computed, which could affect alerts and merge protection.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Mutation testing config is consolidated into a single workspace-root file.** `.cargo/mutants.toml` now explicitly scopes `examine_globs`/`exclude_globs` per crate (including `include!` umbrella files) and the per-crate `crates/*/mutants.toml` files are deleted; `docs/fuzzing/mutants.md` is updated to match.
> 
> **Mutants PR CI behavior is corrected and made gateable.** `mutants.yml` now captures a unified diff file for `--in-diff` (instead of passing a git ref) and removes job-level `continue-on-error` for `mutants-pr` so `scripts/mutants-gate.sh` can enforce advisory vs blocking based on `releases.toml`.
> 
> **Dudect and cocoverage correctness fixes.** `dudect.yml` only selects a prior run with `status==completed`, `check-dudect-threshold.sh` preserves full-precision t-stats and validates `--threshold`, and `mutants-fuzz-cocoverage.sh` replays the fuzz corpus against the *mutated* worktree via `cargo mutants --test-tool`, fixes survivor parsing for the 25.x JSON schema, and avoids deduplicating replays per target.

No breaking changes expected.

## Summary

Phase 2 of the v1.0 rewrite. Replaces the legacy 4-agent LangGraph pipeline with declarative deepagents subagents, wires the human-in-the-loop confirmation callback end-to-end, and deletes the v0.x agent classes (≈4000 LoC removed). The public surface \`from geoagent import GeoAgent; agent.chat(...)\` is preserved.

Six commits, each independently green:

1. \`feat: salvage v0.x agent prompts into core/prompts.py\` — distill the planner SYSTEM_PROMPT, analysis handler patterns (NDVI/EVI/SAVI, zonal stats, change detection, land_cover/elevation/water_mapping/fire_detection/snow_cover/surface_temperature/event_impact), context Q&A prompt, and routing heuristics into ten named prompt constants.
2. \`feat: add deepagents subagent specs in geoagent/agents/\` — planner / data / analysis / context / mapping / qgis / geoai / earthdata factories, plus \`default_subagents(ctx)\` that assembles the active list based on runtime state.
3. \`feat: wire default_subagents and MemorySaver into create_geo_agent\` — \`subagents=None\` now triggers the default list; \`checkpointer=None\` defaults to an in-memory \`MemorySaver\` so HITL works out of the box.
4. \`feat: rebuild GeoAgent facade on top of deepagents\` — 1075 → ~270 LoC. \`chat()\` invokes the graph, then loops on \`result["__interrupt__"]\` to bridge each pending tool call through the user's \`ConfirmCallback\` (approve / reject) and resume via \`Command(resume={"decisions": [...]})\`.
5. \`feat: add chat e2e and confirm-callback tests\` — \`tests/_fakes.py\` adds a \`ToolBindingFakeChatModel\` that no-ops \`bind_tools\` so deepagents middleware accepts it. Eight new tests cover happy-path chat, error propagation, search/analyze aliases, thread isolation, approve / reject / default-reject paths, and that safe tools never trigger a prompt.
6. \`chore: delete legacy 4-agent pipeline classes\` — removes \`core/{planner,data_agent,analysis_agent,viz_agent,context_agent,models}.py\` (4054 LoC). The canonical tool implementations under \`core/tools/*\` are kept; they back the new \`tools/*\` and \`tools/data/*\` factories.

- 75 tests passing (Phase 1's 67 + 8 new)
- pre-commit clean
- Net delta: +1k LoC new (prompts, agents, tests), -4k LoC deleted

body:
Promotes the `[Unreleased]` section in `CHANGELOG.md` to `[1.1.0] - 2026-04-27` and adds a fresh empty `[Unreleased]` above it. Updates the compare-link footnotes so `[Unreleased]` now compares `HEAD` against `v1.1.0` and the new `[1.1.0]` entry compares `v1.0.2...v1.1.0`.

## Why 1.1.0 (not 1.0.3 or 2.0.0)

Per [SemVer](https://semver.org), this is a **MINOR** bump from `1.0.x`:

- **Added** `cache_ttl` config field — backwards-compatible (omitting it preserves the new default behavior).
- **Security** change behavior — cache entries now expire (previously: never). This is the *intent* of fixing #3 and is the right opt-out-not-opt-in default for a tool in the authentication path; defaulting to `cache_ttl: 0` (= retain old behavior) would have shipped the security bug forever. Operators who actively want the old behavior can set `cache_ttl` to something very large.
- No public API removed; no breaking source-level change.

A 1.0.3 PATCH bump would understate the new feature (`cache_ttl`); a 2.0.0 MAJOR bump would overstate the disruption (no API was removed, just runtime behavior tightened in the security-correct direction).

## v1.1.0 contents

Already populated in `[Unreleased]` before this PR — this commit just renames the heading and updates compare links.

- **Added**: `cache_ttl` config field; `sha256` release-asset publication and `install.sh` verification; shellcheck CI.
- **Changed**: `install.sh` download path uses `curl -fLO` + checksum verification.
- **Fixed**: HTTP fetch errors no longer terminate the process.
- **Security**: cache entries now expire so revoked keys actually stop authenticating.

## What happens after this merges

The release workflow (`.github/workflows/go.yml`) triggers on `tags: v*`. Once this PR is on `main`, push the `v1.1.0` tag — the workflow builds, generates `ussher.sha256`, and uploads both as `v1.1.0` release assets with `CHANGELOG.md` as the release body. CLI for that step is in the chat reply that opened this PR.

body:
## Summary
This PR hardens path handling against directory traversal attacks, improves documentation clarity around tool limitations, and adds dependency vulnerability scanning to CI.

## Key Changes

**Security & Path Safety:**
- Added `_resolve_within()` helper function to validate that file paths don't escape their intended directory (prevents `../../etc/passwd` style attacks)
- Applied path validation in `eval_runner.py` to prompt/expected file resolution
- Applied path validation in `launch_validator.py` to IncludeLaunchDescription path checking
- Added email validation in `create_package.py` to reject characters that would break XML escaping

**Documentation & Clarity:**
- Rewrote `eval_runner.py` module docstring to clarify it performs *structural* checks only (validates fixtures exist and contain keywords), not model accuracy evaluation
- Added scope/limitations section to `skill_validate_hook.py` documenting that Bash dangerous-command checks are best-effort guards, not security boundaries
- Added distro stability notes to `tf2-urdf.md` and `lifecycle-components.md` referencing supported ROS 2 versions
- Updated C++ header includes in `tf2-urdf.md` from `.h` to `.hpp` (modern layout) with notes on backwards compatibility
- Added test case pinning documented behavior: docstrings mentioning anti-patterns trigger warnings (limitation of comment-skipping heuristic)

**CI & Dependencies:**
- Added `pip-audit` to GitHub Actions workflow for best-effort dependency vulnerability scanning (non-blocking)
- Improved error logging in `rosbag2_qos_checker.py` with debug-level exception details
- Reorganized imports in `rosbag2_qos_checker.py` for clarity

**Version Bump:**
- Updated marketplace.json version to 1.1.0

## Implementation Details

The `_resolve_within()` function uses `os.path.realpath()` to resolve symlinks and relative paths, then validates the resolved path stays within the base directory. This is applied consistently across path-handling code paths that accept user input from config files.

Error messages now distinguish between "path escapes directory" (security issue) and "file not found" (missing fixture) to aid debugging.

author: cristianxruvalcaba-coder
body:
## Summary

PR #150's wave-skip cache (skip wave evaluation when a recent ratio=1.00 pass is on file) **never fires in production** despite multiple consecutive runs that should trigger it (v7ad/v7ae/v7af on 2026-04-26/27 all passed wave 0+1 at 1.00, every kickoff re-evaluated from scratch). Diagnosed two compounding bugs in `SoulClient.recent_memories`; both are silent failures (no exception, no log).

## Diagnostic evidence

Live `GET /v1/memory/alfred-coo?limit=20` against the Oracle soul-svc shows the persisted wave-pass records (write path works):

```
2026-04-27T06:01:50  autonomous_build:wave_pass:8c1d8f69-...:wave_2  ratio=1.0
2026-04-27T06:01:39  autonomous_build:wave_pass:8c1d8f69-...:wave_1  ratio=1.0
2026-04-27T06:01:24  autonomous_build:wave_pass:8c1d8f69-...:wave_0  ratio=1.0
```

But `GET /v1/memory/recent?session_id=alfred-coo&topics=...` (what `SoulClient.recent_memories` was issuing) returns:

```json
{"memories": [], "count": 0, "session_id": "recent"}
```

Note `session_id: "recent"` in the response — the soul-svc OpenAPI surface has no `/v1/memory/recent` route. Path matching falls through to `/v1/memory/{session_id}` with `session_id="recent"` (a session id with zero stored memories), so every read returns empty regardless of the query string.

Verified directly:
```bash
curl /v1/memory/foobar?limit=5 → {"memories":[],"count":0,"session_id":"foobar"}
```

The `/v1/memory/recent` URL is structurally broken on soul-svc v2.0.0 and always has been — it has been silently masking the wave-skip cache (and `restore`, and PR #154's gate-ACK persistence) since each was shipped.

## Root cause (two compounding bugs)

1. **Wrong endpoint.** `recent_memories` called `GET /v1/memory/recent` (does not exist) instead of `GET /v1/memory/{session_id}` (does). PR #150 worked locally because the test fake `_FakeSoul.recent_memories` filtered an in-memory list with no HTTP involved.

2. **Wrong field name.** Real soul-svc returns each memory's payload under `full_context` (plus a `topic_id` and optional `topics` list); `lookup_wave_pass` reads `mem.get("content")`. Even with (1) fixed, every record would be silently discarded.

## The fix

`SoulClient.recent_memories` now:
- Calls `GET /v1/memory/{session_id}` with `self.session_id` (the actually-existing endpoint).
- When a topic filter is active, fetches with `limit >= 200` so the client-side filter has enough headroom (the session's tail is dense with state snapshots between wave_pass entries).
- Normalises each returned record so callers continue to read `content` (mapped from `full_context`) and `topics` (merged with `topic_id`).

Collateral wins: the same fix unblocks `state.restore` (cross-restart orchestrator state) and `lookup_gate_ack` (PR #154 SS-08 ACK persistence) — both had the same silent-empty failure mode.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_soul_client_recent.py` — **6/6 green** (new regression tests using an `httpx.AsyncBaseTransport` soul-svc stub that mirrors the real response shape; pre-fix this file fails 5/6).
- [x] `pytest tests/test_wave_skip_and_stale_sweep.py` — **13/13 green** (PR #150's tests still pass; their fakes match the new normalised shape).
- [x] `pytest tests/test_autonomous_build_state.py tests/test_autonomous_build_dry_run.py tests/test_autonomous_build_ss08_gate.py tests/test_autonomous_build_review_loop.py` — **68/68 green**.
- [x] Full repo suite (excluding pre-existing main failures: `target_hints_entry_count_unchanged`, fleet_gateway/memory_push/infisical/mcctl/reconcile + collection errors in aletheia/test_pricing_loader/test_fleet_memory_pull) — green and identical to main.
- [x] `ruff check src/alfred_coo/soul.py` — 1 fewer error than main (one legacy bare-`except` retired as part of the rewrite; the other two are pre-existing and out of scope).
- [x] Live verification: `GET /v1/memory/alfred-coo` shows the wave_pass records; the new client retrieves and normalises them.

## APE/V Acceptance (machine-checkable)

- [x] **A · Authorship**: branch `fix/wave-skip-not-firing` carries one coherent commit (`2d1d63d`) co-authored by Claude (Saluca harness).
- [x] **P · Provenance**: diagnosis grounded in (a) live `GET /v1/memory/alfred-coo` against soul-svc Oracle (records present), (b) `GET /openapi.json` (no `/v1/memory/recent` route), and (c) `curl /v1/memory/foobar` confirming literal-session_id path-routing. Linked in commit message.
- [x] **E · Evidence**: regression test `tests/test_soul_client_recent.py::test_recent_memories_finds_wave_pass_record_against_real_endpoint` reproduces the exact production scenario (project `8c1d8f69-...`, wave_0, ratio=1.0) end-to-end and asserts on the URL that goes out (must be `/v1/memory/{session_id}`, must NOT be `/v1/memory/recent`).
- [x] **V · Verification (CI-checkable on this PR)**:
  - `pytest tests/test_soul_client_recent.py -v` → 6 passed
  - `pytest tests/test_wave_skip_and_stale_sweep.py -v` → 13 passed
  - `python -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('src/alfred_coo/soul.py').read())"` → exits 0
  - Pre-fix bisect: `git stash && pytest tests/test_soul_client_recent.py` (against main) → 5/6 fail with the broken URL/shape, proving the regression is real and the test is load-bearing.

## Out of scope (follow-ups recommended)

- The two remaining bare-`except` blocks in `write_memory` and `search_memories` should be tightened separately (was not load-bearing for this fix).
- `state.lookup_gate_ack` and `state.restore` are now functional via the same client fix; if any production data drifted while they were silently no-op'ing, a one-time soul-memory audit may be warranted.

Cristian self-merges after review. Do not auto-merge.

body:
## TLDR

When specifying an openai-base-url and an openai-api-key via CLI args, the CLI silently falls back to the default model, regardless of what model is specified using --model. This is fixed here, by using --model.

## Dive Deeper

Appearently, it is possible to specify all OpenAI API parameters using Environment variables, but this is undocumented. --help shows that --openai-api-key and --openai-base-url are supported as CLI parameters. Thus it would seem natural that the model is specified via --model. It turns out that it is entirely impossible to specify the model used when specifying openai-api-key etc and instead the code tries to infer the model from environment variables (`OPENAI_MODEL`) or falls back to the default model.

Another way to fix this would be to not provide a path through the CLI arguments to control OpenAI API usage but only through environment variables, and to adequately document this option.

author: lestrrat
body:
`KeyAlgorithmFrom("X")` used to walk three independent registries — `SignatureAlgorithm` → `KeyEncryptionAlgorithm` → `ContentEncryptionAlgorithm` — and return the first hit. There was no cross-registry uniqueness, so an extension could register the same name in two kinds and `KeyAlgorithmFrom` would silently flip resolution with import order. Failure landed deep in `jws.Sign` / `jwe.Encrypt` with confusing messages far from the misconfiguration.

This change funnels all three KeyAlgorithm-implementing kinds through a single shared `algRegistry` (hand-written in `jwa/jwa.go`). Per-kind `Register*` / `Lookup*` / `Unregister*` / `<Kind>s()` become thin wrappers around five private helpers (`registerAlgorithm`, `markBuiltin`, `unregisterAlgorithm`, `lookupAlgorithm`, `listAlgorithmsByKind`) emitted by the generator. Cross-kind name reuse becomes a structured error from `Register*` at the conflicting init() call site, which existing `panicOnRegistrationError` wrappers turn into a startup crash.

Bundles JWA-002: `KeyAlgorithmFrom` typed arms now reject zero-value typed algorithms (`String() == ""`) with `ErrInvalidKeyAlgorithm`.

Preserved:
- Same-kind idempotent re-registration (`RegisterSignatureAlgorithm(ES256())` twice is a no-op).
- Per-kind built-in protection ("reserved for a built-in value").
- Same-kind, non-builtin overwrite (separate UX concern, not flagged).

Out of scope:
- `KeyType`, `EllipticCurveAlgorithm`, `CompressionAlgorithm` — they don't dispatch through `KeyAlgorithmFrom` and don't have JWA-001's collision shape.
- v3 backport — separate follow-up via the older `tools/cmd/genjwa/` generator.

Tests added at `jwa/cross_kind_test.go`: cross-kind collision (3 directions), unambiguous lookup, zero-value rejection (3 typed kinds + `EmptySignatureAlgorithm()`), idempotent re-register. mldsa companion smoke against the unified registry passes.

author: wcypierre
body:
## Root cause

Inspecting the live site at deluge.i.wcyp.ru with AOT mode revealed a hidden breakage: `p-accordionTab` was **silently ignored** in JIT mode (unknown elements render as empty), but causes a hard `NG8001` build error in AOT mode. PrimeNG 21 replaced the single `p-accordionTab` with a composite structure: `p-accordion-panel` + `p-accordion-header` + `p-accordion-content`. This means the **Add Torrent → Torrent Options** accordion panel in the config dialog was completely blank.

## Why AOT was disabled

`aot: false` was set earlier because `ngx-filesize v2` and `ngx-moment v5` used Angular 13 ViewEngine metadata (NG6002 errors). Since the dependency update:
- `ngx-filesize v3` declares peer deps `@angular/core >= 14 < 22` — Ivy compatible ✓
- `ngx-moment v6` uses `ɵɵngDeclarePipe` (partial declaration, linker-compatible) ✓

AOT is now safe to enable.

## Changes

1. **`angular.json`**: `aot: false` → `true`; `buildOptimizer: false` → `true` (was forced off because buildOptimizer requires AOT)
2. **`add-torrent-config.component.html`**: Migrate accordion from old API to PrimeNG 21:
   - `<p-accordionTab header="..." [selected]="false">` + `<ng-template pTemplate="content">` →
   - `<p-accordion-panel value="0">` + `<p-accordion-header>` + `<p-accordion-content>`

## Impact

| Metric | Before (JIT) | After (AOT) |
|--------|-------------|-------------|
| main.js bundle | 2.08 MB | 1.43 MB |
| Gzipped | ~530 KB | ~278 KB |
| Build budget warning | ⚠️ exceeds 2 MB | ✅ under budget |
| Template errors caught | at runtime (silent) | at build time |

author: tomeido
body:
💡 **What:** The `secp256k1` elliptic curve instantiation was moved from inside the `generateWallet` function to a lazily-initialized module-level variable `_cachedEc`.

🎯 **Why:** Instantiating the elliptic curve (`new elliptic.ec('secp256k1')`) is a moderately expensive operation. By reusing the instance, we can significantly speed up the key derivation step, enhancing the overall wallet generation speed without side effects, as the object preserves only curve definitions without state.

📊 **Measured Improvement:**
A baseline Playwright performance benchmark running `generateWallet()` purely (bypassing timeouts) showed average generation time dropping from **53.79 ms** to **46.63 ms** across 50 iterations.
Zooming into just the derivation process, time per derivation fell from **1.03 ms** to **0.84 ms**.

author: aarora79
body:
## Summary

Resolves #891

- Skip CSRF validation in `verify_csrf_token_flexible` when no session cookie is present (non-browser clients)
- Add CSRF dependency to virtual server toggle endpoint for consistency across all user-facing toggle endpoints
- Add 7 unit tests covering both the bypass path and enforcement path

## Problem

OAuth M2M Bearer token clients could register agents and skills but could not enable them, because the toggle endpoints required a CSRF token bound to a session cookie that Bearer clients do not have. This blocked any programmatic registration pipeline.

## Fix

Move the session cookie check to the top of `verify_csrf_token_flexible`. If no session cookie is present, the request is from a non-browser client and CSRF protection does not apply (CSRF attacks require a browser session with automatic cookie attachment). Browser/SPA sessions retain full CSRF enforcement.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `registry/auth/csrf.py` | Early return when no session cookie (core fix) |
| `registry/api/virtual_server_routes.py` | Add CSRF dependency for consistency |
| `tests/unit/auth/test_csrf.py` | 7 new unit tests |

## CSRF Coverage After Fix

| Endpoint | CSRF Depends | Bearer Token Works |
|----------|-------------|-------------------|
| `POST /api/toggle/{service_path}` | Yes | Yes (bypass) |
| `POST /api/servers/toggle` | No | Yes (no CSRF) |
| `POST /api/internal/toggle` | No | N/A (internal auth) |
| `POST /api/agents/{path}/toggle` | Yes | Yes (bypass) |
| `POST /api/skills/{path}/toggle` | Yes | Yes (bypass) |
| `POST /api/virtual-servers/{vs_path}/toggle` | Yes (new) | Yes (bypass) |

## Design Documents

Full design documentation in `.scratchpad/issue-891/`:
- [LLD](.scratchpad/issue-891/lld.md)
- [Expert Review](.scratchpad/issue-891/review.md)
- [Testing Plan](.scratchpad/issue-891/testing.md)

## Test plan

- [x] Full test suite passes (2522 passed, 67 skipped, 47.80% coverage)

- [ ] Verify Bearer token toggle works for skills on a live instance
- [ ] Verify browser UI toggle still works (CSRF enforced with session cookie)
- [ ] Verify virtual server toggle works for both Bearer and browser clients

author: tas50
body:
## Summary

Output of a deep evaluation of the Azure provider for logic errors, nil handling, pagination, N+1 problems, and typos.

After verification, the Azure-specific findings reduce to **four N+1 patterns** in lazy-loaded resource methods. None of them have an Azure-side batch endpoint, so the cheapest correct fix is bounded-concurrency parallelization — same shape applied four times (`errgroup.SetLimit(10)`).

Result: each call collapses from O(N) sequential round-trips to ~O(N/10).

## Findings & fixes

### 1. `keyvault.go` `autorotation()` — per-key `GetKeyRotationPolicy`

The `KeyVaultServiceVault.autorotation()` method paginated through keys and, for each key, called `client.GetKeyRotationPolicy` serially. A vault with 200 keys cost 200 sequential round-trips before any resource was yielded.

**Fix:** Within each page, fan out `GetKeyRotationPolicy` calls concurrently into a `kid -> bool` map (bounded errgroup, limit 10). The subsequent `CreateResource` loop simply reads from the map. Errors are still tolerated (best-effort), matching the previous `if err == nil` swallow.

### 2. `compute.go` `dataDisks()` — per-disk `DisksClient.Get`

`VM.dataDisks()` looped over `properties.StorageProfile.DataDisks` and issued one `DisksClient.Get` per disk. A VM with N data disks cost N sequential round-trips.

**Fix:** Collect the disks to fetch, run `DisksClient.Get` concurrently, then map into MQL. Also adds a nil guard on `dd.ManagedDisk` / `dd.ManagedDisk.ID` (the SDK exposes both as pointers — a malformed VM-properties payload could have panicked the unchecked deref).

### 3. `compute.go` `publicIpAddresses()` — nested per-NIC + per-IP `Get` (most impactful)

This was a two-level N+1: for each NIC on a VM, `InterfacesClient.Get`; then for each IP config in that NIC, `PublicIPAddressesClient.Get`. Worst case for `M` NICs × `K` IP configs each, you paid `M + M·K` sequential round-trips.

**Fix:** Two phases, both parallelized:
1. Fetch all NICs concurrently into a `[]network.Interface`.
2. Walk every NIC's IP configs to collect public-IP fetch targets, then fetch all in parallel.

Also adds nil guards on `iface.ID`, `ni.Properties`, `config.Properties`, and `config.Properties.PublicIPAddress.ID` — the original code dereferenced through these without checking.

### 4. `network.go` `ApplicationFirewallPolicy.gateways()` — per-gateway `Get`

For each gateway ID listed in the policy's `applicationGateways` property, the code did `ApplicationGatewaysClient.Get` serially.

**Fix:** Same parallelization shape. Also replaces the panic-on-bad-input `id.(string)` cast with the comma-ok form (a malformed property payload would otherwise crash the resource).

## Audit findings that turned out to be false positives

For transparency:

- All `tags[*t.Key] = *t.Value` style sites in the Azure provider — already wrapped in `if t.Key != nil && t.Value != nil` guards.
- All `pager.More() / pager.NextPage()` paginated list operations — every site I traced consumes all pages, no early-break bugs.
- No `CreateResource`/`NewResource` resource-name typos found.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` in `providers/azure` clean.
- [x] `go vet ./...` in `providers/azure` clean.
- [x] `go test ./resources/...` in `providers/azure` passes.
- [x] `gofmt -w` on all changed files.
- [x] `go mod tidy` (errgroup promoted from indirect → direct).
- [ ] Manual verification on a real Azure tenant with VMs that have multiple data disks and NICs, and a vault with several keys (deferring to reviewer with a real Azure env).

## Related

- AWS provider got the same treatment for Lambda's `ListTags` N+1 in #7407.

## Summary

T3.2 — pure-math service computing the per-answer grounding confidence score that T3.5 will expose to the FE. Formula codified in plan §2434:

```
confidence = 100 * (
    0.40 * mean_top_k_similarity +    // strongest signal
    0.20 * threshold_margin +          // safety vs refusal threshold
    0.20 * chunk_diversity +           // distinct docs / total chunks
    0.20 * citation_density            // cites per ~100-word segment
)
```

## Design choices (codified in L18)

- **Weights as `private const`**, not config — they're part of the v3.0 grounding contract, not a tunable. Reviewers see the formula in code; tuning is a deliberate code change with test updates.
- **Producer-side clamp at the very end** — `(int) round(max(0, min(100, $score)))`. The schema column has no CHECK constraint (per L17), so this method is the load-bearing invariant. Each sub-calc also clamps to [0,1] via `clamp01()` for defense-in-depth.
- **Boundary carve-outs**, each with a dedicated named test:
  - 0 chunks → 0 (defense vs caller forgetting refusal short-circuit)
  - threshold === min_used → margin component = 0
  - 0 answer words → density forced to 1 (refusal path neutrality, not punitive)
  - threshold === 1.0 → margin = 0 safely (no division-by-zero throw)
- **Polymorphic chunk input** — `fieldOf()` accepts both object and array shapes. KbSearchService emits stdClass, fixtures use arrays; the calculator stays refactor-safe.

## Verification Gate (all green)

- [x] PHPUnit: **11 cases / 23 assertions / 71ms** — pure unit, no Laravel boot.
- [x] Coverage: every formula component + every boundary carve-out has a dedicated test.

## Test plan

- [ ] Integration with T3.5 (response shape) covered in T3.5 PR

author: bingqinglyu
body:
### Description: 

This PR enhances the SEATBELT profile resolution logic to support both project-local and global user profiles. Specifically, the resolver now: 

* First checks for profile files in the project’s .qwen/ directory.
* If not found, falls back to the user’s global .qwen/ directory (~/.qwen/ by default).
     
This change enables users to define and reuse global SEATBELT sandbox profiles across multiple projects — eliminating the need to duplicate profile files in every project directory. 

### Background: 

Currently, SEATBELT supports the following predefined profiles: 

-    permissive-closed
-    permissive-open
-    permissive-proxied
-    restrictive-closed
-    restrictive-proxied
     
As documented in `docs/sandbox.md`, users may also define custom profiles via the `SEATBELT_PROFILE` environment variable. However, the system previously only looked for custom profile files (e.g., `sandbox-macos-<profile>.sb`) within `<project>/.qwen/name.sb`. If the file was absent, resolution would fail — even if a valid profile existed in the user’s global settings directory. 

### Impact: 

With this change, users can now place commonly used sandbox profiles in their global `~/.qwen/` directory and reference them from any project — streamlining setup and reducing redundancy. 

## Reviewer Test Plan

This only applies to macOS (because Seatbelt).

- Write a seatbelt profile in your `~/.qwen`. You may copy and modify one e.g. `packages/cli/src/utils/sandbox-macos-permissive-open.sb` into `~/.qwen/sandbox-macos-custom.sb`,
- Launch qwen with `SEATBELT_PROFILE=custom qwen -s`,
- It should now show `macOS Seatbelt (custom)` in the status.

Fixes #559

💡 What: Replaced Mongoose `lean({ virtuals: true })` overhead with a streamlined `.select()` and plain `.lean()` query, manually computing the required virtual fields. Also excluded non-essential large fields like `locationPoint`, `__v`, and specific image metadata.

author: iamdarshg
body:
This PR addresses the physical grounding and accuracy issues in the LBM solver (Issue #16). 

Key changes:
1. **Vectorized MRT Solver**: Replaced the simple BGK operator in `D3Q27Solver` with a sophisticated Multiple Relaxation Time (MRT) collision model. This improves simulation stability and allows for higher Reynolds number runs by relaxing different moments (energy, shear, higher-order) independently.
2. **Physical Force Scaling**: Refactored `_scale_momentum_exchange_force` to follow a rigorous derivation based on the speed of sound ratio between the physical world and the lattice. This ensures that the reported drag and lift coefficients are physically meaningful and grid-independent.
3. **Mach Consistency**: Updated `_estimate_lattice_freestream_velocity` to use the correct D3Q27 sound speed ($c_s = 1/\sqrt{3}$), ensuring the lattice velocity correctly represents the configured physical Mach number.
4. **Optimized Boundaries**: Re-implemented domain boundary conditions (equilibrium inlet, Neumann outlet) using efficient PyTorch slicing and masking, avoiding performance degradation while improving flow physics.
5. **Standalone Logic Preservation**: Ensured that all existing diagnostic metrics (vorticity, Q-criterion, etc.) and the standalone STL voxelization/simulation path remain fully functional.

Validation:
- Ran internal benchmarks on multiple STLs. The drag coefficient for a unit cube is now approximately 1.09, closely matching the OpenFOAM baseline (~1.05).
- All 35 tests in the suite pass without regressions.
- Verified that the implementation uses high-performance vectorized operations.

### Motivation
- Docker image builds were failing when pip attempted to compile scientific or audio packages from source and when shared audio libraries were missing in the final slim image.
- The change aims to reduce CI/docker build flakiness by ensuring required build tools and runtime libraries are present and by preferring binary wheels where available.

### Description
- Updated `Dockerfile` builder stage to install additional build dependencies: `cmake`, `pkg-config`, and `libsndfile1-dev` to support building scientific/audio packages.
- Changed the pip install step to use `--prefer-binary` when installing `-r requirements.txt` to favor prebuilt wheels and avoid source builds where possible.
- Added `libsndfile1` to the runtime stage so audio packages (e.g., `soundfile`/`librosa`) have the required shared library at runtime.
- Kept the multi-stage venv approach and existing healthcheck/entrypoint behavior unchanged.

body:
## Summary

Adds `deadlock-tracker/` — a personal Deadlock stat tracking website similar to tracklock.gg.

**Backend**: Python FastAPI proxying `api.deadlock-api.com` (free, no API key required) with 5-min in-memory cache.

**Frontend**: React + Vite + TypeScript using react-query and recharts.

## Features

- **Player search** — Steam display name, Steam64 ID, or 32-bit account ID
- **Match history** — paginated table with W/L color, KDA, hero, net worth, duration
- **Rank/MMR chart** — recharts line chart of player score over last ~100 games
- **Hero stats** — sortable win rate, avg KDA, games played per hero
- **Live match banner** — polls every 60s, shows green banner when player is in-game

## How the data pipeline works

Valve has no public Deadlock API. Data comes from the community-run api.deadlock-api.com. Steam caches replay URLs encoding match_id + salt; the open-source deadlock-api-ingest Rust binary reads those and submits them. Running it locally ensures your own matches are always captured. See `deadlock-tracker/docs/DATA_PIPELINE.md`.

## How to run

```bash
# Backend
cd deadlock-tracker/backend && pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m uvicorn app.main:app --reload

# Frontend
cd deadlock-tracker/frontend && npm install && npm run dev
```

Search any player at http://localhost:5173.

## Test plan

- [ ] Search by name (e.g. `shroud`) resolves to player profile with match history
- [ ] W/L color coding correct, KDA and hero names display accurately
- [ ] Rank History tab renders MMR line chart
- [ ] Heroes tab sorts by win rate / KDA
- [ ] `npm run build` passes with no TypeScript errors
- [ ] `python -c "from app.main import app"` succeeds

author: khaeransori
body:
## What changed
- New workflow `.github/workflows/perf-budgets.yml` with two parallel jobs:
  - **lighthouse** (PR + workflow_dispatch) — builds apps/pos, runs `vite preview` on `127.0.0.1:4173`, executes `treosh/lighthouse-ci-action@1b0e7c33` (v11.4.0 SHA — last Lighthouse line that scores PWA, kept so we can keep the PWA ≥ 90 contract from the acceptance instead of swapping to per-audit checks against Lighthouse 12).
  - **bundle-size** (PR + push:main + workflow_dispatch) — builds apps/pos and runs `size-limit` against `apps/pos/.size-limit.json`.
- `apps/pos/lighthouserc.json` — mobile preset, simulated slow-4G, median of 3 runs. Asserts `performance ≥ 0.90`, `accessibility ≥ 0.95`, `best-practices ≥ 0.95`, `pwa ≥ 0.90`, `LCP ≤ 2500 ms`, `TBT ≤ 200 ms`, `CLS ≤ 0.1`.
- `apps/pos/.size-limit.json` — `200 KB gzip` initial route (main JS + main CSS), `350 KB gzip` total route-loaded JS.
- `apps/pos/package.json` + `pnpm-lock.yaml` — add `size-limit` and `@size-limit/file` dev deps and a `size:check` script.
- `docs/CI-CD.md` §8 — new section documenting the budgets, the per-audit rationale, the informational→blocking flip procedure, and the budget-bump procedure (PO sign-off + SLO impact note).

## Why
The cross-milestone Performance budgets track in `ROADMAP.md` commits to `Bundle size, Lighthouse, and Web Vitals gates enforced in CI`. None were wired today — `ci.yml` runs lint/build/typecheck/test only. Without these gates a PR can silently push the cold-start cost past the point where catalog browse feels laggy on the entry-level Android tablets that pilot merchants run on slow-4G; we'd only find out in pilot week.

## Posture: informational at first
Both jobs ship with `continue-on-error: true`. The current apps/pos initial bundle is **206.23 KB gzip** (vs. the 200 KB target — over by ~6 KB), so the lighthouse + bundle-size gates would flap red on every PR until the code-splitting work brings it back under. The acceptance explicitly anticipates this: *"informational on first regression, blocking after baseline lands."*

Flip to blocking once either:
1. Two consecutive `push: main` runs land at or under every budget, or
2. The budget itself is raised via the PO-sign-off procedure documented in `docs/CI-CD.md` §8.4.

Mechanism: delete the `continue-on-error: true` line from the relevant job. No restructuring.

## Wall-clock impact
Both jobs run **in parallel** with `ci.yml` (no `needs:`), so they don't extend the critical-path PR latency. Each job: checkout (~5 s) + pnpm install --frozen-lockfile (~20 s with cache) + apps/pos build (~15 s) + gate (~30–60 s) ≈ ~2 min per job. Acceptance budget was ≤ 2 min added; since they're parallel the wall-clock added is the difference between perf-job runtime and `ci.yml` runtime, which is roughly zero.

## How to test
- [ ] CI runs `lighthouse` and `bundle-size` jobs on this PR (visible as separate checks).
- [ ] Bundle-size step fails with an over-budget message for "POS initial route" (~206 KB vs. 200 KB) — but the job is marked succeeded because of `continue-on-error: true`.
- [ ] Lighthouse step uploads a temporary public-storage URL (link in the action's logs) where the report is browseable.
- [ ] After merge, `bundle-size` runs on `push: main` and records the trendline (informational).
- [ ] `gh workflow run perf-budgets.yml` triggers a manual run successfully.

## Out of scope
- Real-device perf on physical Android/iOS hardware — `KASA-131` (v1).
- Real-user Web Vitals (RUM) — no Sentry/GA performance SDK changes here.
- `apps/back-office` budget — owner-side app, separate SLO.
- Code-splitting work to bring the initial bundle under 200 KB — separate ticket; this PR ships the gate so the regression signal is visible.

## Related
Closes [KASA-141](https://app.paperclip.dev/companies/53dd6c47-dd4d-4125-b940-93bca28d8c3c/projects/dfe07b76-95c0-49d9-8ec8-42b8dc958cc2/issues/KASA-141)

author: tttol
body:
## Summary
See also: https://github.com/tttol/dotfiles/blob/neovim-0.12.2/adr/ADR-0001-migration-to-neovim-0.12.2.md

Neovim 0.12.2 への移行に合わせて、Treesitter 周りの設定を Neovim 本体機能中心の構成へ更新しました。

`nvim-treesitter.configs` による highlight 有効化をやめ、Neovim 本体の `vim.treesitter.start()` と `vim.treesitter.foldexpr()` を使う形に変更しています。外部プラグインは parser/query 管理や、Neovim 本体にない UX 機能に限定します。

## Background
Neovim 0.11.x では、`nvim-treesitter` が highlight などの Treesitter 機能を有効化する中心的な役割を持っていました。一方、Neovim 0.12.2 では highlight や fold は Neovim 本体 API で扱えるため、plugin の責務を parser/query 管理へ寄せる方針にしています。

今回の構成では、Neovim 本体が parser/query を使って highlight や fold を実行し、`nvim-treesitter` が parser/query の install/update を担当します。Parser build には `tree-sitter` CLI が必要なため、README に `cargo install tree-sitter-cli` の手順も追加しました。

  |  | Neovim 0.11.x | Neovim 0.12.2 |
  |---|---|---|
  | Highlight 有効化 | 主に nvim-treesitter.configs の highlight.enable = true |vim.treesitter.start() |
  | Fold 有効化 | nvim-treesitter 設定や手動設定 | vim.wo.foldexpr ="v:lua.vim.treesitter.foldexpr()" |
  | Parser 管理 | 旧 nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter が中心 | 新 neovim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter などで管理 |
  | Query 管理 | 旧 plugin に多く同梱 | parser/query registry から取得する方向 |
  | Plugin の役割 | highlight/indent/incremental selection なども含む大きな統合plugin | parser/query 管理が中心 |
  | Neovim 本体の役割 | Treesitter API はあるが、実運用は plugin 依存が多い |highlight/fold などを本体 API で直接使う |
  | tree-sitter CLI | 旧 plugin でも parser install/update には実質必要 | 新plugin では明確な要件 |
  | 設定スタイル | require("nvim-treesitter.configs").setup({...}) |vim.treesitter.start() を FileType autocmd で呼ぶ |

### Tree-sitter
Tree-sitter は、ソースコードを「ただの文字列」ではなく「意味のある構造」として解析するための仕組みです。

parser はこれを読んで、だいたいこういう tree を作ります。
例:
```lua
  local message = "hello"
```

```yml
  chunk
    local_variable_declaration
      variable_list
        identifier: message
      expression_list
        string: "hello"
```

この構造があることで、Neovim は正確な syntax highlight、fold、Markdown の code block 内の別言語 highlight などを実現できます。

### Parser
Parser は、特定の言語のコードを Tree-sitter の構文木に変換する部品です。

Lua には Lua parser、Python には Python parser、Markdown には Markdown parser が必要です。Neovim が `README.md` を開いたときに Markdown の見出しや code block を理解できるのは、Markdown parser がファイルの中身を構文木に変換しているためです。

Parser は言語ごとに必要なので、`lua`, `python`, `typescript`, `markdown` など、使う言語ごとに install/update する必要があります。今回追加した `tree-sitter-cli` は、この parser を build するために使われます。

### Query
Query は、parser が作った構文木の「どの部分をどう使うか」を決めるルールです。

Parser はコードを構造化しますが、それだけでは「どの部分を青くするか」「どこを fold するか」は決まりません。Query が `function name` を function として highlight する、Markdown の heading を fold 対象にする、code block の中身を別言語として扱う、といった判断を定義します。

代表的な query には、syntax highlight 用の `highlights.scm`、fold 用の `folds.scm`、埋め込み言語検出用の `injections.scm` があります。Neovim は parser と query の両方を使って、Treesitter ベースの表示や編集機能を提供します。

author: yu-zh
body:
- Related issues: https://github.com/moonbitlang/moon/pull/1366
- PR kind: Bugfix

## Summary

Previously, `libbacktrace.a` was appended to `c_flags`, and `c_flags` was passed as `user_cc_flags` into `make_cc_command_pure`. That helper intentionally skips default optimization flags like -O2 whenever user compiler flags are present, so the backtrace library accidentally disabled release optimization.

  Changes made:

  - Added `make_cc_command_with_link_flags_pure(...)` in `moonutil::compiler_flags`.
  - Kept `make_cc_command_pure(...)` as a wrapper for existing callers.
  - Added `link_flags` to `MakeExecutableInfo`.
  - Changed Rupes Recta planning so:
      - `cc-flags` go into `c_flags`
      - `cc-link-flags`, propagated link config, and `libbacktrace.a` go into `link_flags`
  - Changed native executable lowering to pass `c_flags` and `link_flags` separately.

  Result: `libbacktrace.a` is still passed to `cc`, but it no longer counts as a user compiler flag, so release native builds now get -O2. I also updated the native release snapshots and added unit tests covering this behavior.

author: rsnodgrass
body:
## Summary Fixes the **ox-qqka** leak: when `ValidateSummaryContent` rejected an LLM's output, the daemon was writing the validator's error string (`"Summary failed content validation: title too short"`) into `meta.summary`. The api-go list handler returned it; the web UI rendered it as the row title. The audit on the SageOx Internal ledger found 14 sessions affected. This PR ships the producer-side fix, a writer-side invariant guard, structured lifecycle fields so consumers stop sniffing for sentinel strings, the sticky-tombstone fix that prevented successful regen from overwriting stale failure stubs, the test infrastructure that makes the whole class of bug visible at PR-time, and a one-shot retro-cleanup tool for existing ledgers. Closes bd `ox-lo29`, `ox-qqka`, `ox-wstd`, `ox-4ggw`, `ox-l4mj`. ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph before["Before (broken)"] b1["LLM output rejected by validator"] b2["session_finalize.go:744
summaryResp.Summary = 'Summary failed...'"] b3["writeMetaAndUploadLFS
meta.Summary = summaryResp.Summary"] b4["api-go list handler
returns meta.Summary"] b5["web UI displays
'Summary failed content validation:...' as row title"] b1 --> b2 --> b3 --> b4 --> b5 style b5 fill:#ffe1e1 end subgraph after["After (this PR)"] a1["LLM output rejected by validator"] a2["session_finalize.go
ValidationError = diagnostic
SummaryStatus = 'failed_validation'
Title and Summary stay empty"] a3["writeMetaAndUploadLFS
meta gets all four fields verbatim"] a4["lfs.WriteSessionMetaOnly
Validate() rejects any leak in user-visible fields"] a5["UI: empty title/summary plus
structured summary_status signal"] a1 --> a2 --> a3 --> a4 --> a5 style a4 fill:#e1f5ff style a5 fill:#e1ffe1 end ``` ## What changed ### Schema (ox-lo29) — additive, omitempty everywhere | Type | New fields | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `pkg/sessionsummary.SummarizeResponse` | `SummaryStatus`, `ValidationError` | Structured signal + ops-facing diagnostic | | `internal/lfs.SessionMeta` | Same two | Mirrored so meta.json is the contract for backend/UI | Constants: `SummaryStatusOK`, `SummaryStatusPending`, `SummaryStatusFailedValidation`, `SummaryStatusUnrecoverable`. Older readers (and older meta.json on disk) keep working without migration — empty `SummaryStatus` reads as "unknown / pre-status" per the doc comment. ### The fix (ox-qqka) Three failure-stub sites in `internal/daemon/agentwork/session_finalize.go` reworked. None of them write the diagnostic into `Summary` anymore; all populate `ValidationError` + `SummaryStatus = "failed_validation"` instead. `ScoreReason` continues to carry the diagnostic for existing log-based ops tooling. `writeMetaAndUploadLFS` now propagates the new fields into `meta.json`. ### Sticky guard (ox-wstd) `cmd/ox/session_push_summary.go` no longer gates `UpdateMetaSummary` on `summaryObj.Title != ""`. A successful regen can now overwrite a stale failure stub. `lfs.UpdateMetaSummary` additionally clears `ValidationError` and stamps `SummaryStatus=ok` on success — the success path is now the canonical "everything is fine again" transition. ### Tests (ox-4ggw) The bug slipped because per-layer tests were green but no test asserted the **cross-layer invariant** "user-visible fields never carry an internal error message". This PR adds: 1. **Schema-level guard** — `internal/lfs/meta_validate.go` defines `LeakySummaryPrefixes`, `IsLeakySummaryString`, and `ValidateUserVisible(meta)`. `WriteSessionMetaOnly` calls `meta.Validate()` before persisting; any meta with a leak in `Title`/`Summary` hard-errors at write time. 2. **Cross-layer property test** — `TestFinalize_ValidationFailure_LeavesUserVisibleFieldsEmpty` drives `ProcessResult` end-to-end with a deliberately-too-short title and asserts (a) `summary.json` and `meta.json` both have empty user-visible fields, (b) both carry the structured failure status, (c) the diagnostic survives in `ValidationError`. 3. **Sticky-tombstone regression** — `TestUpdateMetaSummary_FailedThenSucceeded_NoStickyTombstone` exercises the failed→succeeded flow at the `lfs.UpdateMetaSummary` boundary. 4. **Existing fixture refactor** — `session_finalize_reverify_test.go:53`, `session_finalize_summary_test.go:163`, and `internal/session/artifacts_stub_test.go` no longer bake the leak in as expected behavior. New shape: empty `summary` + populated `validation_error` + `summary_status: "failed_validation"`. The tests' **intent** is preserved (failure markers must persist; stubs must NOT be detected as skip-write candidates). Tests assert intent (the user-visible invariant), not call-site internals — fixture shape changes won't churn them. ### Retro fixer (ox-l4mj) `ox session repair-meta-summary [--dry-run] [--ledger ]` walks the ledger: | Detected state | Action | |---|---| | `meta.title` or `meta.summary` is leaky AND `summary.json` has a clean title | Recover the title, mark `SummaryStatus=ok`, clear `ValidationError` | | Leaky AND no clean replacement available | Clear user-visible fields, mark `SummaryStatus=failed_validation`, preserve diagnostic in `ValidationError` | | Already clean | Skip — meta.json is NOT rewritten (idempotency contract: avoids ledger-mtime churn) | | `meta.Files` (OID manifest) | **Always preserved verbatim** — repair never touches LFS | Idempotent: a second run is a no-op. Designed to be invokable from anti-entropy (follow-up). ### Render-time mitigation hardened `cmd/ox/session_list.go:480` was already filtering one prefix; now uses the centralized `lfs.IsLeakySummaryString` helper so it catches all known leak shapes for ledgers that haven't been retro-cleaned yet. ## Test plan - [x] `go test ./pkg/sessionsummary/... ./internal/lfs/... ./internal/session/... ./internal/daemon/agentwork/... ./cmd/ox/...` — all pass - [x] `go run ./cmd/ox session repair-meta-summary --help` shows correctly - [x] New `TestFinalize_ValidationFailure_LeavesUserVisibleFieldsEmpty` fails without the producer-side fix; passes with it - [x] New `TestWriteSessionMetaOnly_RejectsLeakyMeta` proves the writer-side invariant guard hard-errors on a regression - [x] New `TestUpdateMetaSummary_FailedThenSucceeded_NoStickyTombstone` proves a successful regen overwrites stale state - [x] New `TestRepairMetaSummary_*` covers recovery from clean summary.json, no-summary-json clearing, dry-run, idempotency, manifest preservation The pre-existing flaky `TestCodeDBMaintainerNilManager` in `internal/daemon/` fails under the full suite but passes in isolation; unrelated to these changes. ## Manual verification (recommended for reviewer) 1. `git checkout ryan/sticky-validation-leak` 2. Find a session on the SageOx Internal ledger that still has the leak in meta.summary 3. `ox session repair-meta-summary --dry-run --ledger ` — review the report 4. `ox session repair-meta-summary --ledger ` — apply 5. Confirm the web UI now renders the recovered title (not the diagnostic) ## Notes for reviewer - Format-only churn from `make format` (~130 unrelated files) intentionally excluded. - All five bd issues closed in the same commit. - The `LeakySummaryPrefixes` list in `internal/lfs/meta_validate.go` is the canonical source of truth — both the writer's reject-list and the retro-cleanup tool's detect-list go through it. New leak shapes get appended in one place. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added a CLI to repair session metadata and a sanitizer that strips leaked validator strings from titles/summaries. * Introduced structured summary lifecycle fields (summary_status, validation_error) to represent validation outcomes. * **Bug Fixes** * Prevented validator-error sentinel text from appearing in user-visible title/summary fields. * Ensured summary writes overwrite stale or failed prior values
