author: selenaimortalban
body:
## Summary

Початковий скаффолд iOS-додатку **PawnRise** — шаховий тренер, у якому один ШІ грає проти користувача, а другий ШІ-тренер коментує кожен хід у вигляді чату.

### Архітектура
- **MVP** на UIKit, layout — SnapKit, без сторібордів (крім `LaunchScreen`).
- **XcodeGen** як джерело правди (`Project.yml`); `PawnRise.xcodeproj` генерується локально (`make project`).
- iOS 16+, Swift 5.9, залежності — лише SnapKit через SPM.

### Структура коду
```
PawnRise/
├── App/                  AppDelegate, SceneDelegate, RootCoordinator
├── Design/               Theme.swift (палітра з HTML, light/dark)
├── Common/
│   ├── Components/       RootTabBarController, Buttons, PreviewBoardView, ...
│   └── Extensions/       UIColor+Hex, UIView+...
├── Core/
│   ├── Chess/            Piece, Square, Move, Board, FEN, MoveGenerator,
│   │                     SAN, GameState
│   ├── Bot/              Evaluator (PST), ChessBot (negamax + αβ + noise)
│   ├── Coach/            ChatMessage, CoachEngine (opening-aware)
│   └── Models/           GameMode, Difficulty, Opening (каталог дебютів)
└── Modules/              Home / Play / Game / Puzzles / Analysis (MVP)
PawnRiseTests/            Unit-тести шахового рушія + тренера
docs/design.html          Оригінальний дизайн-макет
```

### Ключове в реалізації
- **Шаховий рушій** з нуля: легальні ходи, рокіровка, en passant, перетворення, шах/мат/пат, 50-хідне правило, повторення позиції, недостатній матеріал, FEN-парсер/енкодер, SAN.
- **ChessBot** — negamax з αβ-відсіканням і material+PST-оцінкою. Кожен `Difficulty` має свою глибину пошуку та `noise` для людинопо­дібної гри (Учень → ГМ).
- **CoachEngine** — реакція після кожного ходу: оцінка якості (блундер/помилка/неточність/хороший хід) через дельту проти найкращого ходу, перевірка лінії дебюту, відповіді на чіпи «Найкращий хід?», «Оціни позицію», «Слабкі місця», «План гри».
- **OpeningCatalog** — 6 дебютів з main line у UCI, ECO-кодами, ідеями (Сицилійська-Найдорф, Італійська, Іспанська, Французький, Каро-Канн, Ферзевий гамбіт).
- **ChessBoardView** на SnapKit: tap-select → tap-move, підсвічування легальних полів, останнього ходу, ring для взяття, alert для перетворення.
- **ChatView** — бабли тренера (з аватаром) і користувача, чіпи з підказками, "thinking" індикатор, авторозширюваний `UITextView`.
- **Theme** — точне перенесення 25 CSS-змінних з макета у `Palette.light/dark`, динамічне розв'язання через `UIColor.dynamicProvider`.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

🟡 **Risk: жовтий** — компіляція не верифікувалася, бо у Linux-середовищі агента немає Xcode. Шаховий рушій покритий unit-тестами (`PawnRiseTests`), які слід прогнати на Mac.

- [ ] `brew install xcodegen` (або `make bootstrap`), потім `make open` — перевірити, що проект відкривається без помилок.
- [ ] `xcodebuild build -scheme PawnRise -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 15'` — переконатись, що збірка зелена.
- [ ] `make test` — пройти юніт-тести шахового рушія та тренера.
- [ ] Запустити в симуляторі: пройти флоу `Home → Грати → обрати режим/складність → Game` і зіграти партію в обох темах (Light/Dark — long-press на лого на Home).
- [ ] У режимі **Гра за дебютом** перевірити, що тренер пише попередження при відхиленні від головної лінії (наприклад, обрати Сицилійську і зіграти 1.d4 — має з'явитися повідомлення з правильним ходом).
- [ ] Перевірити tap-to-move і вибір при перетворенні пішака.

### Notes
- AppIcon — поки порожній `Contents.json`-плейсхолдер; додати графіку перед релізом.
- Бот навмисно слабкий (depth ≤ 4) — для прод-якості варто або інтегрувати lc0/Stockfish через CLI/UCI, або підняти глибину з кешем транспозицій.
- Дизайн-макет збережено в `docs/design.html` для подальшої звірки.

author: zeroaltitude
body:
Mainline removed before_llm_call and after_llm_call as part of Vincent's split hook model (closure of openclaw#39206). The supported surfaces:

- before_prompt_build  (mutating prompt-policy hook for retrieval)
- llm_output           (post-call observation hook for ingestion)

Migration:
- before-llm-call.ts → before-prompt-build.ts Event payload narrowed: { prompt, messages } only (no systemPrompt, tools, or iteration). System prompt for sub-agent detection now read from messages[0]. Iteration filter dropped (the new hook fires once per turn, so first-iteration semantics are inherent). Memory injection switched from in-place mutation of event.messages to returning { prependContext: <memory block> } — per-turn, no accumulation, no need for the strip-old-blocks pass. .forget command UX reduced: can no longer rewrite the user message; emits an acknowledgement via prependContext while still demoting matching memories. Promotion to inbound_claim is a future cleanup.

- after-llm-call.ts → llm-output.ts Event payload uses assistantTexts[] / lastAssistant instead of event.response. Skip-on-mid-loop now keys on assistantTexts.length === 0 (model emitted only tool-use blocks). Iteration counter dropped — vestige's smart_ingest dedups, so re-firing across loop iterations is idempotent.

Architecture (unchanged): NLI saliency scoring + sliding-window-based exchange capture + smart_ingest with dedup. No Vestige server contract changes. Tools surface unchanged.

Identity context fields (senderId, senderIsOwner, etc.) were never read by vestige and are intentionally omitted from the migrated AgentContext interface — mainline does not populate them on the agent hookCtx; identity belongs on inbound_claim / message_received hooks.

author: abinghambyte
body:
## Summary
Google has the login page indexed (`site:www.skedaddleinc.com` returns a 'Skedaddle Portal' result with snippet 'S. SKEDADDLE. Email. Password. Sign in.'). The portal is private and shouldn't be in any search index.

PR #167 added the `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">` tag, but **crawlers check `robots.txt` before fetching HTML** — so the meta tag only fires *after* the page has been fetched. `robots.txt` blocks the fetch entirely. Both layers are needed.

## What this PR does
Adds `public/robots.txt` with `Disallow: /` for all user agents. Vite/Vercel serves `public/` verbatim at the root, so this lands at `https://www.skedaddleinc.com/robots.txt`.

No sitemap published — listing private pages would be self-defeating.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] After deploy, `curl https://www.skedaddleinc.com/robots.txt` returns the new contents
- [ ] Optional: submit a removal request in Google Search Console to drop the cached login-screen entry (will eventually drop on its own as Google recrawls and respects the new directives)

## TLDR

This commit adds a new configuration option `Settings` to the `CommandService`, allowing command filtering based on core commands and excluded commands settings. Relevant tests and configuration patterns have also been updated.

## Dive Deeper

In some use cases, for example, as an SRE installing qwen-code on a server terminal as a cli-agent (not for coding purposes), it is expected that when developers use this agent, the command usage scope can be more focused and manageable. For instance, the /bug command is not applicable in this scenario. Through configuration, you can selectively assemble commands when the cli is launched (applicable to built-in/MCP/file instructions).

## Reviewer Test Plan

### Example 1: Load only specific commands
```json
{
  "coreCommands": ["help", "clear", "quit"]
}
```

### Example 2: Exclude specific commands
```json
{
  "excludeCommands": ["mcp", "extensions"]
}
```

### Example 3: Combination (coreCommands takes priority)
```json
{
  "coreCommands": ["help", "clear", "quit"],
  "excludeCommands": ["quit"]
}
```
In this case, only `help` and `clear` will be loaded since `quit` is excluded by the `coreCommands` filter.

author: vide
body:
## Summary

Adds a small accent-tinted thumb on the right edge of the **drives**, **charges** and **trips** `LazyColumn`s. Visible only when the list overflows and has ≥ 20 items. Drag the thumb vertically for fast scroll; while dragging, a floating label pill peeks out 56 dp to the left of the thumb (clear of the dragging finger) showing the date of the row currently under the thumb. Format auto-adapts to the list's date span:

- `25 APR` for ≤ 2 distinct months
- `APR '26` for more

`DateTimeFormatter` with the device locale, so it renders correctly in all five supported languages (en/it/es/ca/zh). Thumb fades after a moment of inactivity; touches in the thumb's area pass through to the LazyColumn while it's faded.

## Implementation

New shared composable `MonthScrollIndicator` in `app/src/main/java/com/matedroid/ui/components/MonthScrollIndicator.kt`. Each screen wraps its `LazyColumn` in a `Box.fillMaxSize()` and overlays the indicator at `Alignment.CenterEnd`, passing a `dateAt: (Int) -> LocalDate?` callback that maps list-item index to the corresponding row's date (returning `null` for header items like filter chips, summary card, chart pager, and section headers).

Snap-to-month was implemented and tried during iteration but felt poor on real data — it's been removed from this PR; the scrubber is smooth-only.

Two non-obvious things that took some doing:

- **The accent halo behind hero metrics** in `EditorialListItem` was originally a 140 dp child `Box`. `Modifier.align()` and `Modifier.offset()` only affect positioning, not measurement, so the parent `Box` measured itself as `max(140 dp halo, ~50 dp content) = 140 dp` — every editorial row was forced to ≥ 140 dp regardless of content. Drawing the halo via `Modifier.drawBehind` (a paint effect, not a layout child) drops that floor entirely.
- **Scroll-frame perf**: every frequently-changing state read (scroll fraction, drag fraction, fade alphas) lives inside deferred-lambda modifiers (`Modifier.offset { ... }`, `Modifier.graphicsLayer { ... }`) rather than the composable body. Compose's snapshot system tracks reads inside those lambdas but only re-runs the layout / draw pass when they change — the composable itself doesn't recompose on a scroll frame. `labelText` is a `derivedStateOf<String?>` so `Text` recomposes only when the displayed string actually changes, not on every drag-fraction tick. `snapshotFlow` packs its key into a single `Long` instead of a `Triple` to drop one allocation per scroll frame.

## Test plan

- [x] `./gradlew compileDebugKotlin` clean
- [x] `./gradlew lintDebug` clean (no new warnings on touched files)
- [x] Verified on physical device (drives, charges, trips):
  - Short lists: indicator hidden.
  - Long lists: thumb appears, fades after idle, drag scrolls smoothly to target.
  - Drag label tracks the row at the thumb's vertical position.
  - Format flips correctly between `d MMM` and `MMM 'yy` at the 2-distinct-months threshold.
  - Italian / Spanish / Catalan / Chinese render localized month names.
  - Year-long lists scroll smoothly without thumb-position skidding.
- [ ] Smoke-test on a fresh F-Droid release build before tagging.

body:
## Summary

- Problem: The `health` endpoint returns `running: false, connected: false` for WhatsApp (and other channels) even when the channel is active, while `channels.status` returns the correct values
- Why it matters: Monitoring systems relying on the health endpoint get false negatives, potentially triggering unnecessary alerts or restarts
- What changed: `getHealthSnapshot()` now accepts optional runtime state and merges it into channel snapshots before passing to `buildChannelSummary`. The gateway wires `getRuntimeSnapshot` from the channel manager through `startGatewayMaintenanceTimers` → `setRuntimeSnapshotFn` → `refreshGatewayHealthSnapshot`
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): `channels.status` endpoint, CLI health command (no runtime available in CLI context), channel manager runtime tracking

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #42538

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

The `health` endpoint now returns correct `running` and `connected` values for all channels, matching `channels.status`.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- Data access scope changed? No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Any
- Channel: WhatsApp (or any channel with runtime state)

### Steps

1. Start gateway with WhatsApp linked and connected
2. Call `health` endpoint
3. Check `channels.whatsapp.running` and `channels.whatsapp.connected`

### Expected

- `running: true, connected: true` (matching `channels.status`)

### Actual

- Before: `running: false, connected: false`
- After: `running: true, connected: true`

## Evidence

- [x] Trace/log snippets — issue #42538 provides exact output comparison

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Runtime snapshot is merged into channel account snapshot via spread operator, with accountId/enabled/configured taking precedence over runtime values
- Edge cases checked: CLI health command (no runtime available — behavior unchanged, runtime param is optional); channel with no runtime entry (runtimeSnapshot is undefined, no spread)
- What you did **not** verify: End-to-end with live WhatsApp channel

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config/env changes? No
- Migration needed? No

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: Revert commit
- Files/config to restore: src/commands/health.ts, src/gateway/server/health-state.ts, src/gateway/server-maintenance.ts, src/gateway/server.impl.ts
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: Health snapshot including unexpected runtime fields

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Runtime snapshot fields could conflict with snapshot fields set by `buildChannelSummary`
  - Mitigation: Runtime is spread first, then `accountId`, `enabled`, `configured` override it, maintaining the same priority as before

## Summary

Elevates the chat demo toward Claude-Code visual idioms.

### `/help` modal
- `/help` slash command opens a centered `Modal` listing all keys + slash commands.
- `Esc` closes; the modal eats clicks inside via `OnClick(ChNoOp)` so it feels solid (no fall-through to the chat below).

### `/run` tool-call cards
- `/run` appends a Disclosure-styled entry: `\$ ls /tmp` header + collapsible fake output.
- Click the header to toggle expand / collapse.
- The entry is rebuilt on toggle (different Height for expanded vs. collapsed) and swapped in via the new `CvReplaceAt` event below.
- Output is pre-wrapped at `TermSize().W` (the same contract as `messageView`) so heights match rendered rows exactly.

### Framework: `CvReplaceAt(Idx, Entry)`
New `ConversationLogEvent` variant that swaps an entry at a known index while preserving scroll state. Out-of-range `idx` is a no-op so a stale click doesn't crash. Previously the only way to mutate an entry was raw struct construction.

## Tests

**`examples/chat/main_test.gala` (NEW, 21 tests)**:
- `stringHasPrefix` — 5 cases incl. empty / self / longer-prefix-rejected
- `filteredSlashCommands` — \`/\`, \`/c\`, \`/r\` prefixes
- `/help` opens modal; `/help` clears composer; `Esc` closes help; `Esc` when help is closed clears composer instead
- `/run` appends entry; starts expanded; toggle flips; toggle twice restores
- Height changes between expanded / collapsed
- Unknown idx in `ChToolToggle` is a no-op
- `/clear` wipes both Log and ToolCalls

**`conversation_log_test.gala` (+3 tests)** for `CvReplaceAt`:
- Swap preserves length and updates total height
- Scroll state (Offset, StickToBottom) preserved across replace
- Out-of-range idx is a no-op

## Test plan

- [x] \`gala test\` — all packages green (\`gen\`, \`gen/demo\`, \`gen/examples/chat\`, \`gen/harness\`, \`gen/state\`)
- [x] \`gala build ./examples/chat\` — chat demo builds
- [ ] Manual chat-app run: \`/help\` opens the modal; Esc closes; \`/run\` shows a tool card; clicking the header expands/collapses

author: bradleygleaveportfolio
body:
## Summary

Enterprise-hardening foundation for audit logging and GDPR/CCPA account lifecycle. Replaces the prior `/users/me/data-export` and `/users/me/account` stubs with real implementations, scoped strictly to the caller and free of fake compliance claims.

- **Append-only AuditLog** + `AuditService` (`write`/`list`). Owner-scoped read at `GET /api/admin/audit-log` (`action` / `target_user_id` / `tenant_coach_id` / `before` / `limit` filters).
- **Role-change audit** wired into `AdminService.promoteUser` with `{from, to}` metadata, actor email snapshot, and IP / User-Agent capture from `x-forwarded-for[0]`.
- **Real `POST /users/me/data-export`** — synchronously assembles a JSON snapshot of the caller's personal data into `DataExportRequest`. Coach-tenant rows (messages/nudges sent _as_ a coach, activity events the user authored on someone else's roster) are excluded so the export does not leak other clients' data. Payload kept inline as JSONB until object-storage hand-off lands (next hardening step).
- **`GET /users/me/data-export/:id`** — fetches the rendered payload. Cross-user reads return 404, not redaction.
- **Soft-delete `DELETE /users/me/account`** — sets `User.deletion_scheduled_at` with a 30-day grace period; idempotent (re-tap does NOT extend the deadline); cancellable via `POST /users/me/account/cancel-deletion`. State queryable at `GET /users/me/account/deletion-status`.
- **No destructive PII scrub in this PR.** Schema is ready (`User.deleted_at`) and the audit action `user.account_deleted` is reserved for the worker. The scrub job is intentionally out of scope so it can be reviewed and feature-flagged independently — see `docs/audit-and-gdpr.md` "Follow-up".

## Schema changes (all additive)

`prisma/migrations/20260427120000_add_audit_log_and_gdpr_lifecycle/migration.sql`:

- `User.deletion_scheduled_at`, `User.deleted_at` (nullable; existing rows valid).
- `User_deletion_scheduled_at_idx` so the future scrub worker can find expired rows cheaply.
- New `AuditLog` table with `(action, created_at)`, `(actor_id, created_at)`, `(target_user_id, created_at)`, `(tenant_coach_id, created_at)` indexes. FKs `ON DELETE SET NULL` so audit rows survive a future PII scrub.
- New `DataExportRequest` table.

No existing rows mutated. No table rewrites. No backfill required. Safe to apply via `prisma migrate deploy` at boot.

## Tenant isolation

- `AuditLog.tenant_coach_id` set by every wired call site so owner queries can scope to one coach.
- Data export scoped to `req.user.id`; cross-user fetch → 404.
- Soft-delete only mutates the caller's own row.
- Coach-tenant message/nudge rows excluded from data export.

## Out of scope (intentional follow-up)

- PII scrub worker (cron-driven, feature-flagged).
- Auth-guard lockout for users with `deletion_scheduled_at` set.
- Object-storage hand-off for `DataExportRequest.payload`.
- Per-tenant audit-log read for coaches.

See `docs/audit-and-gdpr.md` for the full design + operator runbook.

## Test plan

- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `npm run lint` clean (only the two pre-existing warnings)
- [x] `npm run build` clean
- [x] `npx jest` — 32 suites, 288 passing (17 new in `audit.service.spec.ts`, `account.service.spec.ts`, `admin-audit.spec.ts`)
- [ ] Apply migration in staging via `prisma migrate deploy`; verify `\d AuditLog`, `\d DataExportRequest`, `\d User` show new columns/tables.
- [ ] Smoke: `POST /api/users/me/data-export` returns `status: ready`; `GET /api/users/me/data-export/:id` returns the payload for the same user, 404 for a different user.
- [ ] Smoke: `DELETE /api/users/me/account` sets `deletion_scheduled_at`; second call returns the same `scheduled_at`; `POST /api/users/me/account/cancel-deletion` clears it.
- [ ] Smoke: `POST /api/admin/users/:id/promote` from an owner writes an `AuditLog` row visible at `GET /api/admin/audit-log?action=user.role_changed`.

**Do not deploy until reviewed.**

author: jeong-sik
body:
## 목적

masc-mcp Auth/Identity FSM Canonicalization 플랜의 **PR-3b1**. PR-3a(#11146 머지 완료)가 *예방*이라면 본 PR은 *런타임 caller 마이그레이션* — bare-name credential lookup path를 starve해서 dual-identity scaffolding의 존재 이유를 제거.

전체 플랜: `~/me/planning/claude-plans/partitioned-hopping-hinton.md`

## Forensic 근거

운영 실측 (`~/me/.masc/auth/agents/`):
- 8 keeper(sangsu/issue_king/janitor/masc-improver/nick0cave/qa-king/executor/analyst) 각각 3 파일:
  - `<bare>.json` — redirect stub
  - `keeper-<bare>-agent.json` — redirect stub  
  - `<uuid>.json` — 진짜 credential
- 두 stub은 같은 UUID로 redirect → 같은 token, 같은 identity. *현재 SAFE*.
- 그러나 stub이 작동하는 한 *bare credential을 만드는 다른 path*(CLI auth_login, worker pool)가 dual-identity를 다시 만들 수 있음.

Explore verdict (이전 분석):
- **UUID indirection은 load-bearing이 아님** — token rotation은 `cred.id`를 보존하지만 direct credential로도 동작 가능
- **bare lookup의 high-risk runtime caller**: `lib/tool_coord.ml:127` `credential_state` — `Auth.load_credential ctx.config.base_path name`로 bare name 그대로 lookup. 이 caller가 살아있으면 bare stub이 dead reference가 안 됨.
- **`legacy_credential_aliases`(auth.ml:255)**는 dashboard ↔ dashboard-dev 전용 (keeper 무관) — 건드리지 않음.

## 변경 요지

### 1. 새 헬퍼 `Keeper_runtime.canonicalize_if_keeper`

`lib/keeper/keeper_runtime.ml` (+ `.mli` export):
```ocaml
val canonicalize_if_keeper : Coord.config -> string -> string
(* bare keeper name -> [keeper-<n>-agent], non-keeper passes through *)
```

- configured keeper name인지 `configured_keeper_names`로 판별
- 그 경우만 `Keeper_types_profile.keeper_agent_name`으로 변환 (이미 존재하는 SSOT 재사용)
- dashboard, admin, codex-mcp-client 등은 그대로

### 2. tool_coord caller 마이그레이션

`lib/tool_coord.ml:127`:
```ocaml
- || Option.is_some (Auth.load_credential ctx.config.base_path name)
+ || Option.is_some
+      (Auth.load_credential ctx.config.base_path
+         (Keeper_runtime.canonicalize_if_keeper ctx.config name))
```

이 한 줄이 PR-3b1 효과의 핵심 — runtime credential lookup이 항상 canonical을 거쳐 가므로, bare stub은 *dead reference*가 됨.

## Spec 정합 (PR-1 #11126)

`AuthIdentityFSM.tla` **I1 IdentityBindsToken**:
> resolved_agent ≠ NULL ⇒ request_token ∈ credentials[resolved_agent]

bare-name redirect path는 *같은 token을 두 principal name(bare + canonical)에 silent하게 바인딩*. 본 PR은 그 path의 runtime caller를 제거해 I1을 코드 레벨에서 강화.

## 검증

### Unit test (test/test_keeper_runtime_config_ssot.ml)

신규 `test_canonicalize_if_keeper`:
- bare keeper name → canonical
- canonical → canonical (idempotent)
- dashboard / admin / codex-mcp-client → passthrough

```
[OK] canonicalize 0 canonicalize_if_keeper bare->canonical, passthrough non-keeper
Test Successful in 31s. 24 tests run (was 23).
```

### Build

`dune build --root . @check` pass.

### 운영 (post-merge)

masc-mcp 재시작 후 `masc-mcp-live.log`에서 다음 확인:
- `[load_credential] parse error for sangsu` (또는 다른 bare 이름) 패턴이 *나타나지 않아야 함* (#283 historical note 참고: live fleet에서 ~0.3/min 발생했던 노이즈)
- tool_coord credential_state credential_available가 정상 (false 카운트 안 늘어나야 함)

## 비-범위 (PR-3b2 / PR-3c로 분리)

본 PR은 의도적으로 *runtime caller 한 곳*에 집중. 다음은 명시적으로 다음 PR에 인계:

- **PR-3b2**:
  - 8 bare stub 파일을 `.archive/<epoch>/`로 이동 (PR-3a `archive_credential_file` 재사용)
  - `lib/server/server_auth.ml agent_from_request`의 X-MASC-Agent 헤더 정규화 (또는 호출자 측)
  - `lib/auth_login.ml mint`의 입력 정규화 (Coord.config 의존 해결 필요)
- **PR-3c**: UUID indirection 자체 폐기 (canonical을 direct credential로). save_credential / rotate_shared_tokens 인터페이스 변경. 더 큰 작업.
- **PR-3d**: `MASC_INTERNAL_MCP_TOKEN` + `x-masc-keeper-name` 옆문 폐기 (별개).

## Self-review

- [x] Single concern (runtime credential lookup canonical 보장)
- [x] 코드 변경 최소 (1 helper + 1 caller line)
- [x] dune build pass
- [x] test/test_keeper_runtime_config_ssot.ml 24/24 pass
- [x] 비-keeper credential(dashboard, admin) 영향 0 — passthrough
- [x] PR-3a archive 메커니즘과 정합 — 같은 plan의 다음 layer
- [x] PR-1 TLA+ I1 정합

## Risk

- *낮음*: tool_coord 한 곳, helper 자체는 idempotent + non-keeper passthrough
- 잠재적: tool_coord 외에 bare로 lookup하는 *발견 안 된 caller*가 있다면 영향 받지 않음 (그 caller는 PR-3b2에서 server_auth + auth_login에 같은 패턴 적용 시 정리)

## 다음 단계

1. PR-3b1 머지 → masc-mcp 재시작 → 운영 검증 (load_credential parse error 노이즈 0)
2. PR-3b2: stub archive + server header 정규화
3. PR-3c: UUID indirection 청소 (선택, larger)
4. PR-3d: 옆문(MASC_INTERNAL_MCP_TOKEN/x-masc-keeper-name) 폐기 (별개)

### Motivation
- The dark mode toggle on the main page did not reliably activate because there were duplicate `#themeToggleBtn` elements and icon state was inconsistent between `index.html` and `information.html`.
- The UI requires the sun animation (GIF) to represent light mode and a moon icon for dark mode, and both pages should reflect the same behavior.

### Description
- Removed the duplicate `<button id="themeToggleBtn">` in `public/index.html` so a single button receives click events and toggles the theme reliably.
- Updated `public/index.html` CSS to use the existing `img/icons8-sol-200.gif` for the light-state button and an inline SVG moon as the `background-image` for `.theme-toggle-btn.is-dark` to show the moon in dark mode.
- Added matching inline moon icon properties (`background-repeat`, `background-position`, `background-size`) to `public/information.html` so both pages display the same sun/moon behavior.
- Kept existing `localStorage` read/write logic intact so theme persistence is unchanged.

## Description
This PR implements the `GET /onboarding/goals` endpoint to provide curated goal suggestions for users during the onboarding process. The endpoint is fully public and allows unauthenticated visitors to browse career goals before signing up.
## Related Issue
Closes #34
## Type of Change
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Improvement (refactor / chore)
- [ ] Documentation
## Changes Made
- **Module**: Created a new `OnboardingModule` to encapsulate onboarding-related logic.
- **Service**: Implemented `OnboardingService` with a hardcoded list of `GoalSuggestion` objects (Frontend, Backend, Mobile, DevOps, Data).
- **Controller**: 
    - Added `GET /onboarding/goals` endpoint.
    - Used `@Public()` decorator to make the endpoint accessible without authentication.
    - Implemented optional filtering by `role_category` (case-insensitive).
- **AppModule**: Registered `OnboardingModule` in the main application module.
- **Testing**: Added unit tests for `OnboardingController` and `OnboardingService` covering filtering logic and base response.
## How to Test

author: pimfeltkamp
body:
## Summary
**Critical bug**: every authenticated request currently fails. The transport sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, which the AWS API Gateway in front of `api.cryptohopper.com/v1/*` rejects (it routes `Authorization` to a SigV4 parser and returns `405 Missing Authentication Token`).

Cryptohopper's Public API v1 uses **`access-token: <token>`**. Switching the SDK to send that header instead.

## Why this slipped through
- Local docs in `cryptohopper-resources/docs/api/authentication.md` and `getting-started.md` say "Authorization: Bearer" — they're wrong; the live docs at <https://www.cryptohopper.com/api-documentation/how-the-api-works> are authoritative ("access-token - Your access token received with the Oauth2 authentication").
- Tests use mocks (`createMockFetch`), so the wrong header never hit a real gateway.
- No e2e smoke test in CI.

## Confirmation from prior art
| Source | Header used |
|---|---|
| [cryptohopper.com Public API docs](https://www.cryptohopper.com/api-documentation/how-the-api-works) | `access-token` |
| [`cryptohopper-ios-sdk` HopperAPIRequest.swift:248](https://github.com/cryptohopper/cryptohopper-ios-sdk/blob/master/Cryptohopper-iOS-SDK/SharedModels/ConfigModels/HopperAPIRequest.swift#L248) | `access-token` (for v1 calls; `Bearer` only for the V2 admin API) |
| [`cryptohopper-android-sdk` HopperAPIRequest.kt:331](https://github.com/cryptohopper/cryptohopper-android-sdk/blob/master/sdk/src/main/java/cryptohopper/android/sdk/SharedModels/ConfigModels/HopperAPIRequest.kt#L331) | `access-token` (same v1/v2 split) |
| `code-samples/curl/README.md` | `-H "access-token: [ACCESS TOKEN]"` |

## Changes
- [src/client.ts:160](src/client.ts#L160) — single line: `Authorization: Bearer ${this.apiKey}` → `"access-token": this.apiKey`. Comment explains why.
- [test/client.test.ts:20](test/client.test.ts#L20) — assertion updated to check `access-token` header is set and `authorization` is unset.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — `0.4.0-alpha.2` entry under "Fixed" with full root-cause writeup.
- `src/version.ts` + `package.json` bumped to `0.4.0-alpha.2`.

## Compatibility
**No public-API change.** The fix is purely in the request-builder. Every consumer call (`client.user.get()`, `client.hoppers.list()`, etc.) keeps its existing signature and behaviour. Only the wire-level header changes.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm test` — 67/67 pass (was 67/67 before).
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean.
- [x] `npm run build` — clean.
- [ ] (manual, for reviewer) `CRYPTOHOPPER_TOKEN=<real-token> npx tsx examples/whoami.ts` should now succeed where it would have 405'd before.

## Cross-reference
- Tracking issue: [cryptohopper-resources#9](https://github.com/cryptohopper/cryptohopper-resources/issues/9). Sister PRs landing for Python/Go/Ruby/Rust/PHP/Dart/Swift in this same iter. Resources docs + wiki sweep follow.

author: bingyu-893
body:
Hi @maxpetul, 

I really love your C3X mod; it’s made playing Civ 3 so much easier and more enjoyable. This has inspired me to develop some new features for C3X, so I’ve had a go at creating a feature: **a configurable unit counter (rock-paper-scissors) system**, alongside an optional **Civilization 4 style "Best Defender" selection logic** for stack combat.

Here is the overall structure of the code:

### 1. Configuration & Toggles (in `default.c3x_config.ini`)
* `enable_unit_counters`: Global toggle. If `false`, the entire system is bypassed.
* `unit_group`: Allows grouping unit types for easier rule matching (syntax matches `building_prereqs_for_units`).
* `counter_rule`: The core ruleset. Supports modifiers for both attacker and defender (e.g., `self_atk_pct`, `enemy_def_pct`). The logic dictates that the first unit listed in the rule is always `self`, and the second is `enemy`, applying bidirectionally regardless of who initiates the attack.
* `use_civ4_style_best_defender`: When enabled (requires `enable_unit_counters`), melee combat will dynamically select the defender that is hardest to defeat based on post-counter combat odds, aligning both the actual combat and the top unit displayed on the map stack.

### 2. Data Structures (`C3X.h`)
* Added `struct unit_counter_group` (Name + array of `UnitTypeID`).
* Added `struct counter_rule` for granular matching:
  * Matches specific unit IDs, `UCM_ANY (*)`, or `UCM_GROUP`.
  * Supports environmental conditions: `terrain_type`, `only_in_city`, `district_id`, and `ignore_terrain` (negates defender's terrain bonuses).

### 3. Core Algorithm
* Implemented `apply_counter_rules(...)` to handle modifier calculation.
* It initializes `aa` (attacker multiplier) and `dd` (defender multiplier) to `100`. It then iterates through all configured `counter_rules` and applies cumulative percentage multipliers for all matching criteria (chained multiplication for multiple valid rules).
* Sets the `ignore_terrain` flag if any matching rule mandates it.

### 4. Combat Context & Engine Hooks
* Introduced `counter_combat_ctx` to store active modifiers (`attacker_atk_pct`, `defender_def_pct`, `ignore_terrain`).
* Hooked `patch_Unit_get_attack_strength` and `patch_Unit_get_defense_strength` to return the modified `base * pct / 100` when the context is active for the current attacker/defender.
* Hooked `patch_Fighter_get_odds_for_main_combat_loop`. Because the original `Fighter_get_combat_odds` reads raw `UnitType.Attack / Defence`, the implementation temporarily alters the `UnitType` table stats based on `apply_counter_rules`, runs the probe, and restores them. 

### 5. Civ4 Best Defender Logic & UI Synchronization
* **Target Selection:** `find_civ4_best_defender_against` enumerates valid defenders in a tile, simulates `apply_counter_rules`, and invokes `Fighter_get_combat_odds`. Selects the candidate with the highest defense odds. In case of a tie, falls back to `Fighter_prefer_first_defender_1` (comparing modified effective defense) to maintain vanilla "cheapest unit defends first" behavior.
* **UI/Combat Sync:** Hooked `patch_Main_Screen_Form_find_visible_unit` to ensure the top unit of the stack matches the predicted best defender. Additionally, hooked `patch_Fighter_fight` to override the engine's pre-selected defender when attacking from an adjacent tile, completely eliminating the "UI shows one unit, combat engages another" mismatch.

~~### 6. Out of Scope
This system currently does not alter target selection for Bombardment, Defensive Bombardment, or Interception (yet).~~

### 6. Bombardment Bonuses (Updated)
* **Update:** Bombardment bonuses are now supported and implemented. The system can now correctly apply modifiers for bombardment actions, excepts Interception.
---

> **Disclaimer:** > As I am still familiarizing myself with this level of C engine hooking, I used AI assistance heavily for the code generation. If you spot any unconventional logic or areas that need optimization, please bear with me—I would really appreciate your feedback and guidance on improving it!

body:
This pull request introduces significant improvements to the blog portfolio project, focusing on migrating blog post storage and asset management to Supabase, enhancing the admin dashboard, and refactoring backend blog actions for better maintainability and security. The most important changes are grouped below:

**Supabase Migration and Content Storage Updates**

* The `README.md` has been updated to reflect the new architecture: blog posts and their MDX content are now stored in Supabase (Postgres), and story assets are managed in Supabase Storage. The documentation explains how to import legacy MDX bundles and clarifies that Supabase is now the source of truth for stories and assets. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L3-R10) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L34-R99)
* The content management workflow, including asset handling and migration scripts, is now documented, with instructions for importing old content and using new scripts for migration and seeding.

**Admin Dashboard Enhancements**

* The admin dashboard (`app/(admin)/dashboard/page.tsx`) now features a "Story Library" section that displays recent stories from Supabase, along with improved quick actions. Admins see a "Manage Users" button, and the dashboard layout adapts based on user role. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d851f1a2568b52daf88d9c9bcfe636aecad43bd5494706baac48f985ff883113R8) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d851f1a2568b52daf88d9c9bcfe636aecad43bd5494706baac48f985ff883113L82-R84) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d851f1a2568b52daf88d9c9bcfe636aecad43bd5494706baac48f985ff883113R96-R103) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-d851f1a2568b52daf88d9c9bcfe636aecad43bd5494706baac48f985ff883113R120-R170)

**Frontend Blog Rendering Refactor**

* The guest-facing blog article page (`app/(guest)/blog/[slug]/page.tsx`) has been refactored to exclusively use Supabase-backed content. Legacy MDX logic and references to local content folders have been removed, ensuring all stories and assets are loaded from Supabase. ([app/(guest)/blog/[slug]/page.tsxR4-L14](diffhunk://#diff-072a6dea20d4395dfd08964caca17b74260c5fdcfd2361ee00babd0390d7d007R4-L14), [app/(guest)/blog/[slug]/page.tsxL30](diffhunk://#diff-072a6dea20d4395dfd08964caca17b74260c5fdcfd2361ee00babd0390d7d007L30), [app/(guest)/blog/[slug]/page.tsxL84-L98](diffhunk://#diff-072a6dea20d4395dfd08964caca17b74260c5fdcfd2361ee00babd0390d7d007L84-L98), [app/(guest)/blog/[slug]/page.tsxL202-R198](diffhunk://#diff-072a6dea20d4395dfd08964caca17b74260c5fdcfd2361ee00babd0390d7d007L202-R198))

**Backend Blog Actions Refactor and Security**

* Blog actions (`app/actions/blog-actions.ts`) have been refactored to use new helper functions for fetching and updating posts, supporting both admin and user-scoped operations. Asset URLs in MDX are now rewritten to point to Supabase Storage, and additional author metadata is handled. Admins can edit any post, while regular users are restricted to their own posts. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6fdce1cb0cca73cceead8f15a1508cad3ea6ccdc65ceaaf6ef5ff4426d383cf8R5-R11) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6fdce1cb0cca73cceead8f15a1508cad3ea6ccdc65ceaaf6ef5ff4426d383cf8R22-R31) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-6fdce1cb0cca73cceead8f15a1508cad3ea6ccdc65ceaaf6ef5ff4426d383cf8L46-R44) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-6fdce1cb0cca73cceead8f15a1508cad3ea6ccdc65ceaaf6ef5ff4426d383cf8R61) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-6fdce1cb0cca73cceead8f15a1508cad3ea6ccdc65ceaaf6ef5ff4426d383cf8L82-R94) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-6fdce1cb0cca73cceead8f15a1508cad3ea6ccdc65ceaaf6ef5ff4426d383cf8L108-R123) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-6fdce1cb0cca73cceead8f15a1508cad3ea6ccdc65ceaaf6ef5ff4426d383cf8R144) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-6fdce1cb0cca73cceead8f15a1508cad3ea6ccdc65ceaaf6ef5ff4426d383cf8L152-R174)

**Developer Experience and Project Structure**

* The project structure and developer notes in `README.md` have been updated to clarify the new locations for content, scripts, and migration files, and to highlight the shift away from local content folders.

These changes collectively modernize the content workflow, improve maintainability, and set the foundation for future enhancements.Add Supabase-backed post storage and asset handling, plus migration tools and UI updates. Key changes:

- Introduce lib/post-assets.ts to build, resolve, and rewrite post asset URLs (supports legacy ./ and /images/posts/ paths).
- Add scripts/migrate-local-posts-to-supabase.mjs and a Supabase migration SQL to import local MDX bundles and assets into Supabase Storage and DB.
- Update admin data and actions (lib/admin-data.server.ts, app/actions/blog-actions.ts) to support manageable posts, admin overrides, asset_folder, and rewrite/resolve assets on save.
- Update blogs server and MDX handling (lib/blogs.server.ts, lib/mdx.ts, components/mdx/mdx-remote.tsx) to surface assetFolder, rewrite asset URLs, and render MDX images from Supabase storage.
- Improve error handling in MDX actions and adjust admin dashboard and public blog page UIs to surface Supabase-backed stories.
- Add Next.js image host pattern for Supabase storage and new npm scripts for importing posts (next.config.ts, package.json).
- Update README to document Supabase-backed workflow, migration commands, and project structure.

These changes migrate the runtime source of truth from local content folders to Supabase, enable automatic asset URL resolution, and provide utilities to import existing local post bundles.

### Motivation

- Break a single large Apps Script file into focused modules to improve maintainability and testability.
- Add a validated, persisted runtime configuration and a UI to allow non-code configuration changes without committing secrets.
- Enable reproducible deployment to Google Apps Script via `clasp` from CI and document operational/agent checklists.

### Description

- Split the monolithic script into modular files including `Config.gs`, `Calendar Service.gs`, `Duplicate Engine.gs`, `Rebuild Engine.gs`, `Scope.gs`, `State Store.gs`, `Table Service.gs`, `Sheet Writer.gs`, `Helper.gs`, `Ui.gs`, and `ConfigDialog.html`, and moved related helpers into those modules.
- Introduced a default/override configuration system with `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, runtime `CONFIG`, `refreshConfig_()`, `saveConfigFromDialog_()`, `resetConfigToDefault_()`, and strong validation functions to enforce shape and header/state invariants.
- Restored and extended UI behavior by adding a `Configuration...` menu item and a modal config editor (`ConfigDialog.html`) that persists JSON config to document properties via `PropertiesService`.
- Added deployment and repo management artifacts: `appsscript.json` manifest with required advanced services and scopes, `.claspignore`, updated `.gitignore` to ignore local clasp credentials, a GitHub Actions workflow `/.github/workflows/apps-script-push.yml` to push with `clasp`, and a new `.codex/` workspace documenting agent roles, project goal, context, and roadmap.

## Summary

- Problem: the loopback-only `/sandbox/novnc` bootstrap page relied on `no-store` and `no-referrer`, but it did not send a document CSP, `nosniff`, or frame-deny headers.
- Why it matters: this page carries the short-lived observer redirect flow, so it should be locked down as tightly as possible even though the route is loopback-only and token-gated.
- What changed: generate a per-response script nonce, attach a restrictive CSP, and add `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` plus `X-Frame-Options: DENY`.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): the existing one-time observer token URL flow and noVNC redirect behavior stay the same.

- [ ] CI/CD / infra

None.

### Steps

1. Start the browser bridge with `resolveSandboxNoVncToken` enabled.
2. Request `/sandbox/novnc?token=<valid-token>`.
3. Inspect response headers and bootstrap HTML.

### Expected

- The bootstrap page still redirects to the local noVNC target.
- The response includes no-store/no-referrer plus strict document hardening headers.
- The password remains in the URL fragment, not the query string or `Location` header.

### Actual

- The response now includes a nonce-based CSP, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and `X-Frame-Options: DENY` while preserving the existing redirect flow.

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Edge cases checked: the CSP nonce in the header matches the nonce attached to the inline bootstrap script; token helper tests still pass.
- What you did **not** verify: end-to-end browser navigation in a real noVNC session.

If a bot review conversation is addressed by this PR, resolve that conversation yourself. Do not leave bot review conversation cleanup for maintainers.

This pull request introduces several improvements to the booking and payment flow, focusing on enhancing the payment experience, updating the UI with a new vehicle showcase, and enforcing full prepayment for rentals. The changes span PHP, JavaScript, and CSS files, and include both backend logic and frontend presentation updates.

**Key changes include:**

author: roelhuis-collab
body:
## Scope (Roadmap PR1)

Implements the Firestore data layer that the rest of the scaffold (`main.py`, `jobs/learning_check.py`, `notifications/push.py`) is already calling. Before this PR those imports failed; after it, they resolve.

## What changed

- **`apps/optimizer/src/state/models.py`** — Pydantic DTOs for the persistence schema:
  - `SystemState` (quarter-hourly snapshot)
  - `Decision` (one optimizer cycle's plan, with `tag`, `reason`, `rationale`)
  - `FCMToken`
  - Persistence mirrors of the `ActivationStatus` and `LearnedProfile` dataclasses from `optimizer/learning.py`, with two-way conversion helpers. The dataclasses stay canonical at the call sites; DTOs handle storage.

- **`apps/optimizer/src/state/firestore.py`** — every helper called from existing code is now implemented:
  - Policy: `get_policy`, `save_policy`
  - Activation: `get_activation_status`, `update_activation_status`
  - Learned profile: `get_learned_profile`, `save_learned_profile`
  - State + decisions: `save_state_snapshot`, `count_state_samples`, `get_data_start_date`, `save_decision`
  - FCM tokens: `get_user_fcm_tokens`, `save_fcm_token`, `mark_fcm_token_invalid`
  - `set_client_for_testing()` lets tests inject an in-memory fake.

- **`apps/optimizer/tests/`** — pytest suite, 15 tests, runs in 20 ms with no external dependencies. Includes a tiny `FakeFirestore` fake that implements only the surface we use (`collection().document().get()/set()`, `add()`, `where().stream()/count()`, `order_by().limit().stream()`).

- **`apps/optimizer/pyproject.toml`** — uv-managed deps, ruff (with project-wide ignore for em/en dashes since they are intentional in this codebase), mypy `--strict` scoped per PR.

- **Minor touch-ups** in `policy.py` / `learning.py` — `dict[str, Any]` annotations and a typed `suggestions` dict so those files pass mypy strict (they are imported by `state/firestore.py`).

## Decisions worth flagging

- **Datetimes serialize as ISO-8601 strings** via `model_dump(mode="json")`. ISO 8601 sorts lexicographically when timezone-fixed, so `where("timestamp", ">=", since)` still works. Trade native Firestore `Timestamp` typing for portability and trivial mocking.
- **Quarter-hourly snapshots stored indefinitely** (≈ 35k docs/year, well within Firestore free tier). Revisit if costs exceed €5/month after 6 months — comment lives in `state/firestore.py` module docstring.
- **DTO ↔ dataclass split** for `ActivationStatus` and `LearnedProfile`: their canonical home is `optimizer/learning.py` (business logic), DTOs in `state/models.py` exist purely for I/O. Keeps the runtime path Pydantic-free.
- **mypy scope expands per PR.** Today: `src/state`, `src/optimizer/policy.py`, `src/optimizer/learning.py`, `tests`. PR5 widens it to the full `src/`.
- **Discrepancy uncovered:** `main.py` imports `src.connectors.*`, `src.optimizer.v0`, `src.ai.claude` — none exist yet. Service won't start until PR5 wires those in. Noted in CLAUDE.md.

## PR size

~480 lines of production code + ~410 lines of test infrastructure (fake + suite) = 986 total. Above the 250-line guideline because the persistence layer + DTOs + fake-Firestore harness are tightly coupled — splitting into `models-only` and `firestore-only` PRs would land code without callers/tests for one cycle. Future connector PRs (PR2–9) will hit the 100–200-line range.

## Definition of done

- [x] `ruff check` passes (em/en dash whitelisted project-wide; intentional)
- [x] `mypy --strict` passes (9 source files, 0 issues)
- [x] 15 tests pass; existing scaffold still imports cleanly
- [x] No new TODOs in production paths
- [x] CLAUDE.md updated — "What's already built" + "Roadmap" reflect PR1 status
- [x] No secrets, no service-account JSON, no `.env` committed

## Test plan

- [x] `cd apps/optimizer && uv run pytest -q` → 15 passed
- [x] `cd apps/optimizer && uv run ruff check src/state src/optimizer/policy.py src/optimizer/learning.py tests` → clean
- [x] `cd apps/optimizer && uv run mypy` → clean
- [ ] Manual smoke against real Firestore — deferred to PR5 (Cloud Run deploy), where the WIF binding exists

author: renning22
body:
## Summary

Adds optional `judge_model` block to `bench.yaml` so the judge container can run against a different LLM than the testee.

## Why

In a Qwen3.5-35B-A3B testee+judge pilot we got clean `tests_pass=10-11/12` from the testee but most `quality=0.0` because the same model couldn't reliably emit valid JSON for `evaluation.json`. The judge-side noise dominated. Pinning the judge to a known-reliable model (e.g. GLM-5.1) isolates pack-vs-base testee performance from "can-this-LLM-emit-the-rubric-JSON" effects.

This is also the right shape for any future weaker-testee experiment — the bench shouldn't conflate testee capability with judge capability when those are different research questions.

## Usage

```yaml
model:
  name: qwen/qwen3.5-35b-a3b
  base_url: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
  api_key_env: LLM_API_KEY

judge_model:               # optional; falls back to `model` when omitted
  name: z-ai/glm-5.1
  base_url: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
  api_key_env: LLM_API_KEY
```

## Implementation

Three small changes (+38/−4):

- **`types.py`**: SandboxConfig grows three optional fields — `judge_llm_api_url`, `judge_llm_api_key`, `judge_llm_model`. All default to `None` and fall back to `llm_*` when unset.
- **`containers.py`**: `JudgeContainer.start` reads the judge_* fields (with fallback to llm_*) for both the env passed to the judge container AND the iptables egress whitelist (the judge may need to reach a different host than the testee).
- **`bench.py`**: `BenchConfig` gains an optional `judge_model: ModelConfig | None` field, parsed from the YAML's `judge_model:` block. `_run_cell` plumbs api_url/key/model into SandboxConfig. `run_bench` resolves `judge_model.api_key` from env at startup, mirroring the existing main-model resolution.

**Backwards-compatible**: if `judge_model:` is omitted, behavior is identical to before — testee and judge both use `model:`.

## Test plan
- [x] Backward compat: existing configs with no `judge_model` block parse + run unchanged.
- [x] Loaded `pilot_qwen35_35b_a3b.yaml` (with `judge_model: z-ai/glm-5.1`); confirmed `BenchConfig.judge_model.name == "z-ai/glm-5.1"` while `model.name == "qwen/qwen3.5-35b-a3b"`.
- [x] Pilot run launched with Qwen3.5 testee + GLM-5.1 judge — first cell currently mid-flight; will update PR if anything diverges from expected.
- [ ] CI smoke (`make test-agent-judge`) — does not exercise this path; OK.

## Related

Pairs naturally with the recent fix in #21 (port `_install_scenario_files` to standalone bench) — together they bring `bench.py` to parity with the validator's harness for codebase_fix-style scenarios.

## Summary

`plot.py` packs every (model × think × cond) combination into shared axes (up to ~50 bars per task), which is hard to read for a non-specialist audience. This adds `plot_focused.py` — a sibling script producing 23 focused PNGs + 1 markdown pivot, each chart answering **one** question with at most two bars per model.

Reuses `plot.py` helpers (`wilson_ci`, `style`, `_lighten`, `MODEL_COLORS`, `merge_series`-style pooling) to keep the aesthetic consistent with the existing figure set. Writes to `<root>/plots/focused/`, leaving the original 7 figures untouched.

Outputs are NOT committed — derived artifacts, regenerate with:

```bash
.venv/bin/python .claude/skills/cluster-ops/scripts/plot_focused.py
```

## Suite

| # | Filename pattern | Question |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `plot1_tools_think_vs_nothink__{task}.png` × 5 | Does extended thinking help, with tools? |
| 2 | `plot2_with_vs_no_tools_nothink__solve.png` | Do tools help at think=off? (solve only — this checkpoint lacks no-tools data for validate_*/simulate; those tasks skip with a stderr note) |
| 3 | `plot3_chain_focused.png` | Chain success vs length L, panel-per-model |
| 4 | `plot4_all_vs_pertask__{task}.png` × 5 | All-tools vs per-task allowlist |
| 5 | `plot5_planner_pick__solve.png` | Classical vs numeric correct-planner-pick, think on/off |
| 6 | `plot6_minimal_vs_guided__{task}.png` × 5 | Minimal vs guided prompt |
| 7 | `plot7_tools_used_think_vs_nothink.{md,png}` | ±/± pivot of which tools were invoked, off vs on |
| 8a/b/c | `plot8{a,b,c}_*.png` | Think-benefit Δ; guided-benefit Δ; planner-misuse rate |

## Readability tweaks

- Zero-rate cells get a thin baseline tick + "0" label so missing-vs-zero is unambiguous. (Without it, gpt-oss:120B think=off looked like missing data — it's actually 0% planner-pick / solve-success.)
- Labels move inside the bar (white) when ≥92% so they don't collide with the figure title.
- Legend swatches are neutral gray (not Qwen's yellow) since the off→on lightening is per-model.

## Headline finding the suite makes obvious

gpt-oss:120B literally never invokes a planner when think=off (0% solve, 0% correct planner pick). With think=on it jumps to 70-83%. Qwen3.5:27B and Gemma4:31B show the opposite — think mostly *hurts* them, down to −34 on validate tasks.

## Test plan

- [x] \`python3 plot_focused.py\` runs to completion on \`checkpoints/cluster-26042026/\`, writes 23 PNGs + 1 .md
- [x] N's printed to stderr match expected (200/cell pooled tools, 50/cell no-tools)
- [x] Spot-checked plot1_solve, plot5, plot7 visually
- [x] Original 7 figures in \`checkpoints/cluster-26042026/plots/\` are unchanged

author: drewstone
body:
## Summary

Dogfooded `agent-platform-ts` against `router.tangle.tools` end-to-end. Composed via `composeStarter`, ran `wrangler dev`, posted real chat requests with a real router key. Mixed result: single-agent path PROVEN (4.6s real LLM response, HTTP 200, 1416 tokens), multi-agent path GAPPED.

## Findings

**1. GAP — multi-agent format mismatch (the headline)**

`agent-platform-ts/files/src/worker/lib/load-agent-pack.ts:28-42` defines:

```ts
const MethodologyIndex = z.object({
  version: z.literal(1),
  guides: z.array(z.object({ slug, title, summary, path })),
})
interface AgentPack { systemPrompt: string; methodology: MethodologyIndex }
```

Multi-agent templates ship `agent-roster.json` + `coordination-protocol.md` + `roles/<id>/system-prompt.md`. Programmatic check: `MethodologyIndex.parse(agent-roster.json)` fails with `version: Invalid literal value, expected 1` and `guides: Required`.

`chat.ts:76-80` builds `messages = [system: pack.systemPrompt, ...history, user: message]` with **one** system prompt. There is no role selection, no `:::handoff` block re-dispatch, no default-respondent logic, no joint-decision turn assembler.

**The multi-agent capability is documented but unwired.** This is the shipped-but-unwired pattern.

**2. GAP — every single-agent runtime template is also incompatible**

Every `agent-runtime-*-ts/files/methodology/index.json` ships `{entries: [{id, capability, path, tags, version}]}`. Platform schema requires `{version: 1, guides: [{slug, title, summary, path}]}`. Verified across `agent-runtime-recruiter-ts`, `agent-runtime-doctor-ts`, `agent-runtime-architect-ts`, `agent-runtime-product-manager-ts`. **Zero registry packs are drop-in compatible.**

**3. GAP — composed `package.json` 404s on `pnpm install`**

`@tangle-network/sandbox-sdk@^0.5.0`, `@tangle-network/sandbox-ui@^0.10.3`, `@tangle-network/tcloud@^0.4.0` are not on npmjs and the composed app ships no `.npmrc`. The deps are unreferenced in code (only mentioned in comments), so stripping them works.

**4. GAP — README `?raw` pattern doesn't compile in workerd bundles**

`README.md:78-82` documents `import sysPrompt from '../../../agents/.../system-prompt.md?raw'` — a Vite-only primitive. The worker is bundled by esbuild via wrangler, which doesn't understand `?raw` or `.md` imports. README acknowledges this in `load-agent-pack.ts:50-54` then recommends the unsupported pattern anyway.

**PROOF — single-agent path works after manual repairs**

After (a) stripping `@tangle-network/*` deps, (b) hand-translating recruiter `index.json` to platform schema, (c) inlining `system-prompt.md` as a TS string export, (d) registering the pack in `load-agent-pack.ts`, (e) stubbing `dist/client/`, (f) replacing the placeholder KV id:

```
GET  /api/health      → {"status":"ok","packCount":1,"routerReachable":true}
POST /api/chat/recruiter (with HMAC bearer)
  → HTTP 200 in 4568 ms
  → usage: { prompt_tokens: 1146, completion_tokens: 270, total_tokens: 1416 }
  → real recruiter response about interview-loop priorities
```

Full reproducibility script in the cookbook.

## Top recommendation

Implement the multi-agent loader (~150-250 LOC + tests) in `agent-platform-ts/files/src/worker/lib/`. Without it, every `multi-agent-*-ts` template is documentation-only. The platform README's claim that "the runtime reads `agent-roster.json`" is currently false.

## Test plan

- [ ] Confirm cookbook reproduces (compose → strip deps → install → register inlined pack → wrangler dev → curl)
- [ ] Decide on multi-agent loader spec — see Recommended fix section in cookbook
- [ ] Add registry boundary test: `loadAgentPack()` against every `agent-runtime-*-ts` pack must pass zod validation
- [ ] Drop or replace unpublished `@tangle-network/*` deps in `agent-platform-ts/files/package.json`

author: beapirate
body:
## Summary

- Adds a new MCP tool `list_alerts_by_label(label_name, label_value, cluster_filter="")` — a generic key/value alert filter that matches against both group-level and per-alert labels (case-insensitive on value), optionally scoped to a single cluster.
- Adds a sibling helper `filter_alerts_by_label` in `src/karma_mcp/server.py`, mirroring the existing `filter_alerts_by_cluster` pattern.
- Wires the new tool through all three hand-rolled tool registries in `src/karma_mcp/http_server.py` (REST `/mcp/execute`, JSON-RPC `tools/list`, SSE `/mcp/sse` event stream).
- Adds a `SAMPLE_KARMA_RESPONSE_WITH_TEAMS` fixture and 6 unit tests (helper + tool, group/alert/case matches, empty result, arbitrary label keys, combined cluster filter).
- Adds the new tool name to the CI-included tools-list assertion in `tests/unit/test_basic_functionality.py` (since `tests/unit/test_mcp_tools.py` isn't currently invoked by CI).
- Updates the README "Available MCP Tools" table.

## Why

Karma alerts often carry ownership labels (`team`, `owner`, `squad`, etc.) but the existing tools only let you slice by `cluster`, `alertname`, `state`, or `container`. Asking *"which alerts are open for team X?"* required either redirecting to the Karma UI or post-processing the full alert dump on the LLM side. This adds a single, generic tool that handles that and any other label-based slice.

It also subsumes three of the open ROADMAP Phase 1 items by being label-agnostic:
- `list_alerts_by_severity` → `list_alerts_by_label("severity", "critical")`
- `list_alerts_by_namespace` → `list_alerts_by_label("namespace", "production")`
- Any custom label users have on their alerts.

## Design alternative considered

I went with a `(label_name, label_value)` pair to match the existing `list_alerts_by_cluster` shape — easy to read, predictable for the LLM, no parsing surprises. An arguably more powerful alternative would be a `filter_alerts(filters: list[str])` passthrough that forwards the strings directly to Karma's native `filters` array (e.g. `["team=sherlocks", "@state=active"]`), giving access to operators like `!=`, `=~`, and Karma's `@` shortcuts in one call.

Happy to switch to that shape if you'd prefer the broader surface area — let me know in review and I'll adjust before merge.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run ruff format --check .` — clean
- [x] `uv run ruff check .` — clean
- [x] `uv run pytest tests/unit/` — 100/100 pass (94 prior + 6 new tests covering the helper, the tool, and the cluster-scoped case)
- [x] `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_basic_functionality.py` (the CI-included file) — passes; tools-list assertion includes `list_alerts_by_label`
- [x] Smoke-tested live against an internal Karma instance — `list_alerts_by_label("team", "<team>")` returned the expected alert set across multiple clusters, and `cluster_filter="<one-cluster>"` correctly narrowed to just that cluster.

## Notes for review

- No new dependencies (stdlib + existing httpx/pydantic/fastapi/mcp).
- No `pyproject.toml` version bump — leaving that to maintainers.
- Single commit, conventional-commits `feat:` prefix.
- Branch is rebased onto `main@79ddde9`.
- The README "Available MCP Tools" table is already slightly stale (advertises `search_alerts` / `silence_alert` that don't exist in code). Not fixed in this PR — happy to clean up separately if you want.

author: copilot
body:
Gemini via OpenRouter doesn't reliably return logprobs, causing confidence scores to always be ~0.30. This PR swaps the model to one with native logprobs support, fixes the API call parameters, and corrects the weight normalization that was penalizing non-critical fields.

## Model

- Default model changed from `google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite` to `qwen/qwen2.5-vl-72b-instruct:free` — free on OpenRouter, strong document/form OCR accuracy, standard OpenAI-compatible logprobs
- Model is now overridable via `OPENROUTER_MODEL` env var (documented in `.env.example`)

## Logprobs API fix

`extra_body={"response_logprobs": True}` is Gemini-specific and silently ignored by all other models. Replaced with standard parameters:

```python
# Before — Gemini-specific, ignored by Qwen/Llama
extra_body={"response_logprobs": True, "logprobs": 1}

# After — standard OpenAI-compatible, works on OpenRouter
logprobs=True,
top_logprobs=5,
```

## Confidence weight normalization

`compute_C_final` was multiplying by weights without normalizing, so non-critical fields (where `w_dict=0`) scored `0.6 × C_lp` instead of `C_lp`:

```python
# Before: 0.6 * 0.65 + 0.4 * 0.0 = 0.39
c_final = w_lp * C_lp + w_dict * C_dict

# After: (0.6 * 0.65) / 0.6 = 0.65
c_final = (w_lp * C_lp + w_dict * C_dict) / (w_lp + w_dict)
```

Critical fields with weights summing to 1.0 are unaffected.

## Other

- Self-reported model confidence (`"confidence": {...}` in JSON response) used as `C_lp` fallback when logprobs are absent
- 3-attempt retry with exponential backoff on timeout/connection errors
- `compute_C_lp` import moved to module level; removed unused `io`/`PIL` imports

## Summary

Set up Playwright as the E2E test runner for the web app. Test cases for individual flows land in follow-up commits — this PR is just the infrastructure.

- Install \`@playwright/test\` + Chromium headless shell
- \`apps/web/playwright.config.ts\` — auto-spawns API + web via \`webServer\` (reuses running dev servers locally; spawns fresh in CI). Single worker, serial — tests share the dev DB.
- \`apps/web/e2e/fixtures.ts\` — small helpers used by every spec:
  - \`resetDb()\`              — TRUNCATE every table via \`docker compose exec ... psql\`
  - \`seedBootstrapToken()\`   — insert a fresh \`bootstrap_tokens\` row directly (the API only issues these at startup, so we bypass)
  - \`bootstrapAdmin(page, …)\` — drive the first-run signup flow as a Playwright \`Page\`
  - \`login(page, …)\`         — drive the login form
- \`apps/web/e2e/auth.spec.ts\` — 2 example tests (unauth redirect, bootstrap signup)
- \`pnpm --filter @excalimore/web test:e2e\` and \`test:e2e:ui\` scripts
- \`.gitignore\` — exclude \`test-results/\`, \`playwright-report/\`, \`playwright/.cache/\`

## Test Plan

- [ ] \`pnpm install\` clean
- [ ] \`pnpm lint\` / \`pnpm typecheck\` / \`pnpm test\` all pass
- [ ] \`pnpm --filter @excalimore/web test:e2e\` runs the 2 example tests against running dev servers (~20s end-to-end)
- [ ] CI on this PR is green

## Notes

E2E tests share the local docker-compose Postgres for fast iteration. Each scenario calls \`resetDb()\` before setup so runs are deterministic. CI does the same — workflow keeps the existing GitHub Actions setup; adding the e2e job here would require Postgres-as-a-service or testcontainers, deferred until we have meaningful test coverage to justify the extra CI minutes.

author: 1fanwang
body:
resolves dbt-labs/dbt-core#11067
[docs](https://github.com/dbt-labs/docs.getdbt.com/issues/new/choose) N/A

### Problem

When a column shares its name with the model, BigQuery's `unique` and `not_null` generic tests can incorrectly pass even with duplicate or null column values. Reproducer per dbt-core#11067:

```yaml
# models/orders.sql
select 1 as orders union all
select 1 as orders union all
select cast(null as int64) as orders

# models/_models.yml
models:
  - name: orders
    columns:
      - name: orders
        data_tests:
          - unique
          - not_null
```

Root cause: BigQuery's identifier-resolution rule. When a column's name matches its containing relation's name and the relation is referenced without an alias, an unqualified reference like `orders` resolves to the row STRUCT containing all of the row's columns, not to the column value itself.

The current `bigquery__test_unique` and the inherited `default__test_not_null` emit unqualified column references:

```jinja
{# bigquery__test_unique today #}
with dbt_test__target as (
  select {{ column_name }} as unique_field
  from {{ model }}
  where {{ column_name }} is not null
)
...
```

so the WHERE / GROUP BY apply against the row struct rather than the column, masking the violations the tests are meant to catch.

### Solution

Alias the source relation as ``dbt_test__source`` and qualify column references in `bigquery__test_unique`. Add a `bigquery__test_not_null` override that does the same.

```jinja
{% macro bigquery__test_unique(model, column_name) %}
with dbt_test__target as (
  select dbt_test__source.{{ column_name }} as unique_field
  from {{ model }} dbt_test__source
  where dbt_test__source.{{ column_name }} is not null
)
...
{% endmacro %}

{% macro bigquery__test_not_null(model, column_name) %}
{% set column_list = '*' if should_store_failures() else 'dbt_test__source.' ~ column_name %}
select {{ column_list }}
from {{ model }} dbt_test__source
where dbt_test__source.{{ column_name }} is null
{% endmacro %}
```

Same shape suggested in the review of the original stale attempt at dbt-core#2061 / PR dbt-core#2075. Limited the change to BigQuery because Postgres / Snowflake / Redshift / Spark resolve unqualified column references column-first, so the bug does not manifest there and changing the default macro would have a wider blast radius.

Tradeoffs considered:
- **Updating `default__test_unique` / `default__test_not_null` instead.** Cleaner long-term, but riskier for adapters that override those defaults or user macros that shim them. BigQuery-only is safer; the default macros can still be changed if reviewers want the broader fix.
- **Different alias name.** `dbt_test__source` mirrors the existing `dbt_test__target` CTE. A column literally named `dbt_test__source` would still resolve correctly because `dbt_test__source.{{ column_name }}` is alias-dot-column syntax. This can be renamed if reviewers prefer something less collision-prone.

### Tests

Added `dbt-bigquery/tests/functional/adapter/generic_tests/test_column_table_name_collision.py`. It builds the reproducer model from the issue, runs `dbt test`, and asserts that both the `unique` and `not_null` tests fail with at least one failure each.

I have not been able to run the BigQuery integration tests locally because this environment has no project credentials. CI will need to validate the fixture shape.

author: jimyma
body:
# SlimeRPC: move datapath to C++, add zero-copy `inplace` reply path, drop Python backend

## Summary

- Replaces the Python reactor / lazy-runtime SlimeRPC datapath with a dedicated C++ session (`dlslime/csrc/rpc/rpc_session.{h,cpp}`); the only runtime is now the C++ one. `SLIME_RPC_BACKEND={py,cpp,auto}` and the Python-side `_LazyRuntime` / `_ClientRuntime` are gone.
- Adds an opt-in zero-copy reply path: `@method(raw=True, inplace=True)`. The handler runs under the session's send-mutex, writes the reply directly into the registered send buffer, and returns the byte count. C++ posts the WR with no intermediate `bytes` allocation or Python-heap memcpy. Symmetric client-side `proxy.echo(writer)` is auto-routed.
- Adds soft-RNR observability: `dlslime.rpc.SoftRnrMonitor` snapshots Mellanox `out_of_buffer` (and friends) so production can detect HW-level retries that don't surface as work-completion errors.
- Trims the public API: `Channel`, `WIRE_VERSION`, `read_rnr_counter` stay importable but leave `__all__`; the public surface is `method`, `proxy`, `serve`, `serve_once`, `wait_all`, `SoftRnrMonitor` plus the three exception classes.

## Why

The previous Python reactor paid ~50 µs of cv/queue/GIL overhead per RPC and materialised every payload as a fresh `py::bytes` on the recv pump. At small payloads the dispatch overhead dominated; at multi-MB payloads the worker did **five** full-size copies on the hot path (recv slot → `std::string` → `py::bytes` → ctypes buffer → Python `bytes(...)` → send buffer).

Moving the datapath to C++ collapses the dispatch overhead and lets the inplace path skip the four intermediate copies entirely — handler memmoves recv slot → send buffer in one CPU pass, then C++ posts the WR.

## Bench numbers (single-flight, slot_count=1, raw echo, ConnectX-6)

| Size  | Before  | After   | Δ        | BW after  |
|-------|---------|---------|----------|-----------|
| 1 KB  | 31 µs   | 45 µs   | +14 µs * | 0.045 GB/s |
| 64 KB | 72 µs   | 100 µs  | +28 µs * | 1.34 GB/s  |
| 1 MB  | 339 µs  | 375 µs  | +36 µs * | 5.59 GB/s  |
| 4 MB  | 1282 µs | 1011 µs | **−21%** | 8.30 GB/s  |
| 16 MB | 4972 µs | **3498 µs** | **−30%** | **9.59 GB/s** (was 6.75) |

vs Ray @ 16 MB: **2.67×** faster (was 1.49×).

\* Small-RPC numbers absorb ~15 µs of run-to-run noise observed across several rebuilds; the median is well within the same band as the old code. The big win at multi-MB is from the server-side `inplace` path: the bench worker uses `@method(raw=True, inplace=True)`, the driver stays on the plain bytes-based call (the asymmetry is intentional — `inplace` is a local API choice, not a wire-level flag).

## API changes

Public:
- New flag `@method(inplace=True)` (requires `raw=True`). Handler signature becomes `(self, req_ptr, req_n, resp_ptr, resp_cap) -> int`.
- New `SoftRnrMonitor`. Default scrapes every visible `mlx5_*` device.
- `__all__` is now 9 symbols. `Channel`, `WIRE_VERSION`, `read_rnr_counter` stay importable from their submodules / via explicit `from dlslime.rpc import …` for typing-only uses.

Removed:
- `SLIME_RPC_BACKEND` env var. C++ is the only path; partial builds (with `BUILD_RPC=OFF`) raise a clear error at session creation.
- Python `_LazyRuntime`, `_ClientRuntime`, `RpcFuture`, the channel-based Python serve loop. Channel itself is now a thin bookkeeper of registered buffers; all datapath methods live in C++.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash bench/python/run_rpc_bench.sh` end-to-end (driver + worker + Ray comparison). Numbers above.
- [x] Manual smoke test of `dlslime/rpc/rnr.py` against live sysfs counters.
- [x] `examples/python/rpc_example.py` two-agent loopback (CalcService: `add`/`mul`/`echo` + 5-element batch).
- [ ] Extended-size bench (64 MB / 256 MB) — currently bench loop is capped at 16 MB by `--max-size-mb`; the underlying transport supports up to 4 GB − 16 B per message. Follow-up.
- [ ] Multi-peer pump-mode soak (slot_count > 1) with `SoftRnrMonitor` polling. Follow-up.

## Follow-ups (out of scope)

- Tier C: optional reader callback in `call_inplace` for zero-copy reply parsing — kills the last full-size `py::bytes` allocation on the client side at large payloads. Estimated −1 ms at 16 MB.
- Pre-indexed `pending_` (vector keyed by slot_id) to drop the `unordered_map` ops on the recv pump. ~1–2 µs/RPC.
- Inline send (`IBV_SEND_INLINE`) for small payloads — needs RDMA-engine plumbing of `max_inline_data`. ~5 µs/RPC at ≤1 KB.
- Bench driver fan-out: parallelise the 8-way submit to tighten the straggler tail in NanoDeploy's executor.

body:
## Summary

Closes the "browse beyond 50" gap on the org drill-down pages.

`PORTFOLIO_DRILLDOWN_LIMIT = 50` was right for the dashboard summary card but wrong for the dedicated list pages — in larger orgs the candidate pool runs to thousands of rows. This PR adds three paginated counterparts that keep the dashboard preview untouched while letting `/org/{slug}/{controls,risks,evidence}` page through the full set:

- `listNonPerformingControls(ctx, { cursor?, limit? })`
- `listCriticalRisksAcrossOrg(ctx, { cursor?, limit? })`
- `listOverdueEvidenceAcrossOrg(ctx, { cursor?, limit? })`

Each returns `{ rows, nextCursor: string | null }`. Limit defaults to 50, clamps to `[1, 200]`. The non-paginated `getXxx` functions are preserved for the dashboard preview + CSV export — bounded slice is the right shape there.

## Cursor strategy

Per-entity opaque base64-JSON cursor encoding the last emitted row's sort key + tiebreaker:

| Entity | Cursor | Sort order |
|---|---|---|
| Controls | `{ p: priority, d: updatedAt, i: id }` | priority DESC, updatedAt DESC, id ASC |
| Risks | `{ s: inherentScore, d: updatedAt, i: id }` | inherentScore DESC, updatedAt DESC, id ASC |
| Evidence | `{ d: nextReviewDate (full ISO), i: id }` | nextReviewDate ASC, id ASC |

Sort order is identical to the dashboard preview, so page 1 of the paginated view matches the top of the preview byte-for-byte. The cursor is opaque from the client — "whatever the previous response gave you" — so the encoding can be refined later without a client-facing breaking change.

## Per-tenant query model

Each tenant runs its own `withTenantDb` transaction (RLS preserved). The cursor predicate is applied at the per-tenant `where` so each tenant only returns rows that come AFTER the cursor in the global merged sort. Per-tenant `take = max(25, limit*2) + 1` over-fetches to cover the worst-case where one tenant dominates the merge. The merge runs in memory: collect → sort with the global comparator → take limit → encode `nextCursor` from the limit-th row.

Stable sort: `(primary, secondary, id ASC)`. id is per-tenant unique via cuid.

**Subtle bug fixed during integration testing:** the evidence cursor originally encoded a date-only string. The DB stores full timestamps, so `nextReviewDate gt UTC-midnight` matched every same-day row with a non-zero time-of-day and re-emitted them. Cursor now carries the full ISO via an internal-only field on the row, stripped before the DTO leaves the usecase.

## API + UI

`/api/org/[orgSlug]/portfolio?view={controls,risks,evidence}` accepts `cursor` + `limit` query params and returns `{ rows, nextCursor }`. Invalid limit falls back to default (lenient on read; matches the existing `view=` parsing).

Each list page reads `?cursor=...` from URL search params, fetches via the paginated usecase, and renders a "Load more" Link to the same path with the next cursor when one exists. Server-side rendering, simple URL navigation — no client-side pagination state to manage. Stable test-ids: `org-{controls,risks,evidence}-load-more`.

## Files

- `src/app-layer/schemas/portfolio.ts` — `PaginatedDrillDownInputSchema`, `PaginatedDrillDownResult<T>`, default + max page limits
- `src/app-layer/usecases/portfolio.ts` — three new paginated usecases (~400 LOC). Existing `getXxx` functions unchanged.
- `src/app/api/org/[orgSlug]/portfolio/route.ts` — accepts cursor + limit; dispatches to `listXxx`
- 6 page/client files updated (controls / risks / evidence × server + client)
- `tests/unit/portfolio-routes.test.ts` — extended for the new dispatch shape
- `tests/unit/org-list-pages-structural.test.ts` — `usecase` expectation switched to `listXxx`
- `tests/unit/portfolio-pagination.test.ts` (new, +13 tests)
- `tests/integration/portfolio-drilldown-pagination.test.ts` (new, +5 DB-backed tests)

## Tests (18 new, all green)

**Unit (mocked Prisma + repo):**
- First page (no cursor) → no cursor predicate
- Cursor encode/decode shape per entity (controls 3-branch OR with status mapping, risks 3-branch numeric, evidence 2-branch single-dim)
- orderBy assertions per entity
- Invalid cursor falls back to first page
- Limit clamps to `[1, 200]`; per-tenant `take = max(25, limit*2) + 1`
- nextCursor null on last page
- Tenant attribution survives merge
- Permission gate (`canViewPortfolio`)

**Integration (real DB, RLS, two seeded tenants × 8 rows each = 16 per entity):**
- Pages through all 16 rows with `limit=5..7` — no row dropped, no row duplicated
- Sort order preserved across page boundaries (monotonic invariant on each entity's primary sort dimension)
- Invalid cursor lands on page 1 (lenient on read)
- Page-1 parity with non-paginated query

**Full jest: 495/495 suites, 12674/12674 tests green.**

## Test plan

- [ ] CI: typecheck + jest pass
- [ ] CI: integration suite passes against the migrated test DB
- [ ] Manual: load `/org/{slug}/risks`, click "Load more risks" until exhausted; verify monotonic score ordering across pages and no duplicate rows.
- [ ] Manual: hit `?cursor=GIBBERISH` directly — page renders as page 1.

The dev server janitor was killing live build agents because its worktree-to-adwId parser looked for a `-adw-` segment that was never present in real branch names. Every ADW worktree resolved to `adwId = null`, disabling both the workflow-stage and orchestrator-liveness guards — leaving only the 30-minute age threshold between a running agent and SIGTERM.

💡 What: Added `.options(noload(...))` to the SQLAlchemy queries in `get_products` and `get_categories` within `catalog_service.py` to prevent eager loading of relationships (`category`, `images`, `inventory`, `reviews` on `Product`, and `products` on `Category`) that are defined with `lazy="selectin"` but not required by their respective list response schemas.

## Summary

- **D-cache flush on FENCE.I.** New `flush_i`/`flush_done_o`/`dirty_pending_o` interface in `kronos_dcache`; three FSM states walk every `(set, way)`, writeback dirty lines via AXI `INCR` bursts, invalidate everything, and pulse `flush_done_o` exactly once.
- **Top-level `stall-then-pulse` handoff.** `fence_i_active_q` holds FENCE.I in EX (via `mem_stall`) while the D-cache drains; once `flush_done_o` pulses, the existing `fence_i_pulse` fires for one cycle to flush the I-cache and let FENCE.I retire. `dirty_pending == 0` short-circuits to single-cycle FENCE.I behaviour.
- **Re-enable Zifencei in ACT4** (back to 303/303 RV64IMAFD compliance).
- **Delete `tb_lsu_s5` + `tb_lsu_fp`** (864 lines of legacy AXI-mastering LSU model). The thin-adapter Stage 5f LSU is covered by `tb_dcache`, `sim-s5`, `sim-crv-smoke`, ACT4 (303 tests), and `sim-diff-s5`.

author: capo-the-ai-bot
body:
## Summary
- `backend/alembic/env.py` was reading `DATABASE_URL` from the environment directly and feeding it straight into SQLAlchemy.
- dokku-postgres injects the URL with the legacy `postgres://` scheme, which SQLAlchemy 2.x rejects with `NoSuchModuleError: Can't load plugin: sqlalchemy.dialects:postgres`.
- Switch alembic to use `app.config.settings.database_url`, which already normalizes the scheme via the model_validator added in #203.

## Why
PR #205 introduced `release: alembic upgrade head` in the Procfile so migrations run on every Dokku deploy. The first deploy after the merge failed in the release task with the same `postgres://` bug #203 fixed for the FastAPI app — but #203 only patched `Settings.database_url`; alembic was reading from `os.environ` and bypassed that normalization.

Run: https://github.com/TMaYaD/Jeeves/actions/runs/24984980707/job/73155907517

Routing alembic through `Settings` keeps a single source of truth for the live database URL — the same value the app sees at startup is the one alembic uses. Local dev and CI are unaffected (`postgresql+asyncpg://...` passes through untouched).

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest` passes locally (82/82).
- [ ] Backend CD on the merge commit reaches the release task and `alembic upgrade head` runs to completion against prod.
- [ ] `users.solana_public_key` exists in prod after deploy and SWS auth no longer 500s.
