author: naroam1
body:
## Summary

Reintroduces the work from #2119 (Dockerfile fix + scheduler-side prefix-cache tracker), but with the tracker **auto-disabled when an L2 backend is configured**. Matches the architectural constraint @DwyaneShi flagged in his revert rationale (#2119 (comment)) and preserves the upstream worker-reconciliation model bit-for-bit for L1+L2 deployments.

@DwyaneShi pre-approved this direction in #2119 (comment).

## Motivation

@DwyaneShi's revert (#2132) correctly identified that a scheduler-side tracker assumes exclusive ownership of the external cache — valid for L1 local but not for L2 distributed (shared across engines). This follow-up makes the tracker opt-out-by-default for L2 users:

- The scheduler auto-detects L2 presence via `AIBRIX_KV_CACHE_OL_L2_CACHE_BACKEND` and disables its tracker when L2 is configured, yielding the full upstream worker-reconciliation model unchanged.
- L1-only deployments (common for single-engine setups) regain the `vllm:external_prefix_cache_hits_total` visibility and the warm-TTFT speedup we measured originally.

The Dockerfile fix from #2119 is included here per @DwyaneShi's note that *"the Dockerfile improvement for handling missing patch files across newer vLLM versions is useful and can be kept separately in a follow-up PR"* — bundling for one-shot review.

## Change

### `aibrix_offloading_connector_type1.py`

- `AIBrixOffloadingConnectorScheduler.__init__` computes `self._tracker_enabled = not bool(aibrix_kvcache.envs.AIBRIX_KV_CACHE_OL_L2_CACHE_BACKEND)`. When True (L1-only), the scheduler maintains `_cached_block_hashes`, `_request_block_hashes`, and `_request_external_tokens`. When False (L2-backed), all tracker entry points short-circuit to no-ops.
- `get_num_new_matched_tokens`, `update_state_after_alloc`, and `receive_connector_worker_meta` all gate on `_tracker_enabled`. When disabled they return early — equivalent to the current upstream behavior introduced by the revert.
- `_cached_block_hashes` is now a bounded `OrderedDict` (cap `_MAX_CACHED_BLOCK_HASHES = 100_000`), addressing the unbounded-growth concern @varungup90 raised in the original review.
- `AIBrixWorkerMeta` carries `saved_tokens` and `failed_load_tokens`. `aggregate()` uses intersection + min() for `saved_tokens` and union + max() for `failed_load_tokens` for TP correctness.
- Worker `_newly_saved_tokens` / `_newly_failed_load_tokens` are populated unconditionally in `_send_kv_sync_impl` / `_recv_kv_sync_impl`. The scheduler discards these reports when its tracker is disabled — safe to always populate.

### `kv_connector/__init__.py`

- Reuses the simplified monkey-patch from #2119 (`start_load_kv_before_update` + `wait_for_save` with metadata re-bind), which works in tandem with the scheduler-side tracker via vLLM's `get_num_new_matched_tokens` path.

### `Dockerfile.vllm`

- Conditional patch step: skip the source patch when no patch file exists for the current `VLLM_VERSION` (e.g., `v0.19.0`). Adds `apt-get update` before debug tool install. Defaults `VLLM_VERSION=v0.19.0`.

### Tests

- `tests/test_connector_inheritance.py` gains a fourth AST-based assertion verifying that `Scheduler.__init__` assigns `_tracker_enabled` and that the gate is driven by `AIBRIX_KV_CACHE_OL_L2_CACHE_BACKEND`.

## Untouched

- `BaseKVCacheManager` public API: no changes.
- L1Cache callback mechanism: no changes (the existing `_l2_ingestion_callback` slot is preserved).
- Type2/Type1 inheritance scaffolding from #2125: already on `main`, untouched.

## Testing

Smoke-tested on an L4 GPU with Qwen3-4B-AWQ in L1-only configuration (`AIBRIX_KV_CACHE_OL_L1_CACHE_ENABLED=1`, no L2 backend), 500-prompt flood pattern (same harness as #2119):

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| `vllm:external_prefix_cache_hits_total` | **1280** |
| Warm TTFT avg (10 refs) | **0.146 s** |
| Cold TTFT avg (excl warmup) | 0.213 s |
| Speedup | **-31%** |

AST-based structural tests pass on Python 3.11 + 3.12, no vLLM / GPU dependency required.

L2-backed deployments path: not exercised in our cluster (no L2 backend available), but the gate's no-op behavior is mechanical — when `_tracker_enabled = False`, all entry points return early and the connector reduces back to the current upstream code path.

Closes the regression introduced by the revert of #2119, keeping @DwyaneShi's L2-safe semantics intact.

### Motivation
- Prevent a privilege-escalation where AdminView's in-memory authenticated state persists across consecutive users in the same browser tab so the next user could access admin without re-entering the PIN.

### Description
- Add `AdminView.resetAuth()` which clears the in-memory `isAuthenticated` flag, clears the PIN input and login error, and forces the admin UI back to the locked/login section.
- Call `AdminView.resetAuth()` from `App.handleUserLogout()` so logout clears both the user session and any unlocked admin state in the same tab.
- Refactor `admin.js` so `handleLogout()` delegates to `resetAuth()` and export `resetAuth` as part of the `AdminView` API for testability.
- Update `frontend/tests/app.test.js` to include a `resetAuth` mock on `AdminView` and assert it is invoked when a user logs out.

### Testing
- Ran `cd frontend && npm test -- --run tests/app.test.js tests/admin.test.js` and both test files passed (2 files, 16 tests total passed).

author: pmatos
body:
## Summary
- Replace `JsObjectData.properties: HashMap<String, PropertyDescriptor>` with a hybrid `PropertyMap`: `SmallVec<[(String, PropertyDescriptor); 4]>` inline (linear-scanned, no heap alloc) → randomised `HashMap` once exceeded.
- `INLINE_CAP = 4`. Issue #68 suggested 8, but a `mem::size_of::<JsObjectData>` unit-test tripwire fired at 3520 bytes with 8 inline slots; 4 covers the motivating splay-node case (`{key, value, left, right}`) while keeping the struct under 3 KB.
- Spill is **one-way** — deletes never collapse back to inline. Removes a timing side-channel at the inline/spill boundary.
- The spilled `HashMap` continues to use the std default randomised SipHasher, preserving the DoS mitigation from #111.
- `property_order` is untouched: it still drives `Object.keys` / `for...in` order. `PropertyMap::iter()` / `keys()` / `values()` are deliberately order-unspecified; verified no caller relies on `HashMap` iteration order.
- The new API is a strict subset of `HashMap`'s (`contains_key, get, get_mut, insert, remove, iter, keys, values`), so all ~100 call sites compiled unchanged. Two pre-existing clippy auto-deref nits in `eval.rs` and `helpers.rs` are cleaned up where the new `&str`-typed `get` signature exposed them.
- Promotes `smallvec` from a transitive dep (already in `Cargo.lock` via `icu`) to a direct dep.

Closes #68.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo build --release`
- [x] `./scripts/lint.sh` (rustfmt + clippy clean)
- [x] `cargo test --release` — 70/70 pass, including 9 new `PropertyMap` unit tests covering inline get/insert, spill on overflow, duplicate-insert, remove-after-spill, iter visits all in both modes, `get_mut` mutation in both modes, Symbol-key enumeration in both modes, and a `mem::size_of::<JsObjectData>()` tripwire
- [x] `uv run python scripts/run-test262.py -j 100` — 98,426 / 98,426 (100.00%), 0 regressions vs `origin/main` baseline, 64 new passes
- [x] Manual smoke: 4-prop object (inline) → 11-prop object (spilled) → delete-after-spill keeps insertion order

author: bingqinglyu
body:
## Summary

Adds optional `pairingMessage` config to iMessage and Telegram channel configs, allowing operators to customize or suppress OpenClaw branding in pairing challenge messages sent to unknown senders.

Fixes #41058

## Problem

When `dmPolicy: pairing` is set, every unknown sender receives a hardcoded message exposing:
1. The OpenClaw brand name
2. The channel platform ("Your iMessage sender id:" / "Your Telegram user id:")
3. The full CLI invocation syntax (`openclaw pairing approve imessage CODE`)

No config option exists to override any part of this. The only workaround is patching compiled dist bundles after every update — not sustainable for white-label or privacy-conscious deployments.

## What changed

- `src/pairing/pairing-messages.ts`: Add `PairingMessageConfig` type with optional fields (`header`, `senderIdLabel`, `codeLabel`, `footer`, `showCliHint`). Update `buildPairingReply` to use config when provided.
- `src/config/types.imessage.ts`: Add `pairingMessage?: PairingMessageConfig`
- `src/config/types.telegram.ts`: Add `pairingMessage?: PairingMessageConfig`
- `src/config/zod-schema.providers-core.ts`: Add `PairingMessageConfigSchema`, wire into `IMessageAccountSchemaBase` and `TelegramAccountSchemaBase`
- `src/imessage/monitor/monitor-provider.ts`: Wire `pairingMessage` config into `issuePairingChallenge` via existing `buildReplyText` hook
- `src/telegram/dm-access.ts`: Pass `pairingMessage` through `enforceTelegramDmAccess`, wire into `issuePairingChallenge`
- `src/pairing/pairing-messages.test.ts`: Add tests for all config overrides and backward compat

## Fully backward compatible

All `PairingMessageConfig` fields are optional. Existing deployments with no `pairingMessage` config see zero behavior change.

## Example config

```yaml
channels:
  imessage:
    pairingMessage:
      header: 'Sender verification required.'
      senderIdLabel: 'Your sender ID:'
      footer: 'Share this code with your contact to complete verification.'
      showCliHint: false
```

## Notes

Discord, Signal, Slack, and LINE call sites follow the same pattern and can be extended in a follow-up if the team prefers to land iMessage/Telegram first.

## AI Disclosure
This PR was authored with AI assistance (OpenClaw/Jordan + Neo agents).
Testing: Fully tested — unit tests in `pairing-messages.test.ts` cover all config branches including edge cases; CI passes (types, lint, full test suite on Linux/Windows/macOS).
The authors have reviewed and understand all code changes in this PR.

## What this PR does / why we need it:

PR #24201 moved Query_INSERT table locking off the pre-pipeline path. LOAD DATA is also planned as Query_INSERT and always carries a table-locking LockOp, so TPCH 1T load started taking that path too and the nightly load phase regressed noticeably after b79773d551.

This patch keeps the #24201 behavior for regular INSERT statements, but restores the pre-pipeline table lock for LOAD DATA only. That keeps the fix scope narrow and avoids changing unrelated INSERT paths again.

author: dynnamitt
body:
Closes #36.

## Summary

- **`HGridLayout::hex_face_tris()`** — center-fan flat-top tris (6 per hex, hard-coded fan).
- **`HGridLayout::all_tris()`** — unified triangle stream: gap quads split along the canonical `[v0, v2]` diagonal, gap junction tris, hex face tris. Diagonal choice now owned in rust, not on the JS client.
- **`crates/hex-grid/src/serialize.rs`** (new) — `SerializeGeo` trait with four implementors:
  - `SvgPlain` / `SvgRich` — existing SVG variants
  - `JsonV1` — gen1 payload, byte-compatible with consumers of `hex-grid.json` (hexes / edges / quads / tris)
  - `JsonV2` — gen2 payload `{ version: 2, tris: [...] }` from `all_tris()`
- **Example renamed** `svg.rs` → `geo_export.rs`, now a thin CLI wrapper dispatching by `--format <svg|svg-rich|json-v1|json-v2>`. `--rich` and `--json` kept as backward-compat aliases.
- **Makefile** — all targets switched to `--example geo_export`; new `svg-json-v2` target emits `hex-terrain.json`; included in `svg-preview` deps.
- **`web/hex-terrain.html`** — fetches `hex-terrain.json` (v2), feeds the unified `tris` field directly to `weldedMesh`. The per-source toggles (hex faces / gap quads / gap tris) collapse — only filled / wireframe / flat-shading remain, since the per-source split no longer exists client-side.
- **`web/hex-terrain.js`** — drops unused `hexFaceQuads` / `hexFaceTris` helpers (their work moved to rust).
- **`crates/hex-grid/README.md`** — documents the rename, the `--format` flag, and the new `JsonV2` variant.

`web/svg-preview.html` continues to consume v1 (`hex-grid.json`) — gen1 stays byte-identical for backward compat.

## Decisions (per the issue)

- v2 payload field name: `tris` (not `all_tris`) — JSON only has one tri stream so the prefix is redundant.
- `hex_face_tris()` triangulation: center-fan, fastest path.
- `SerializeGeo` lives in the lib (`crates/hex-grid/src/serialize.rs`), not the example.
- Gap-quad diagonal: `[v0, v2]` to match prior JS behaviour. Documented on `all_tris()`; revisit after a visual A/B.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p hex-grid` — 35 tests pass (4 new: `hex_face_tris_count_is_six_per_hex`, `hex_face_tris_share_height_per_hex`, `all_tris_count_matches_components`, plus four `serialize::tests` for each format)
- [x] `cargo build` (full workspace) — clean
- [x] `cargo clippy -p hex-grid --examples --tests` — clean
- [x] Smoke test: `geo_export -- 2 0.6 --format json-v2` produces `{"version":2,"tris":[...]}`; `--format json-v1` produces the gen1 shape; `--rich` still works
- [ ] Manual: `make svg-preview` and load `target/svg-preview/hex-terrain.html` in a browser to confirm the welded mesh renders identically (rust-owned diagonal vs. JS-owned diagonal)

author: kharebakavtaradze-source
body:
Root causes:
1. _build_mfe_map only read 10d horizon; hit_Xpct booleans read from stored DB columns which are NULL for rows written before the MFE migration.
2. _mfe_stats counted hits via m.get("hit_10pct") — always 0 on old data.
3. giveback_pct NULL for old rows — not derived from available fields.
4. _cg(c, "decision") used _cget which has default=False and looks for "decision" key — but DB stores it as "np_decision" → decision=false.
5. perf_decision lambda defaulted NULL np_decision to "AVOID", collapsing all unscored historical candidates into the AVOID bucket.

Fixes (research_bundle.py only; no scoring/routing changes):

_build_mfe_map: reads all 4 horizons with per-horizon suffixed keys (max_gain_{hz}_pct, max_high_{hz}, giveback_{hz}_pct, return_{hz}); derives giveback_pct from max_gain_pct - return_pct when stored column is NULL; derives hit_Xpct_10d booleans from max_gain_10d_pct >= threshold (mathematically equivalent to scanning window highs, works for old rows).

_mfe_stats: derives hit counts from mg >= threshold inline instead of reading stored hit_Xpct booleans; references renamed hit_Xpct_10d keys.

_build_mfe_sections:
- mfe_by_decision: use c.get("np_decision") or "UNKNOWN"
- mfe_by_structure_phase: resolve via np_data["structure_phase"] pattern
- top examples: use np_decision, structure_phase from np_data, hit_Xpct_10d keys, structure_score field

Phase 9 perf_decision + 3 cross-tab lambdas: change "or AVOID" to "or UNKNOWN" so real AVOID decisions are countable separately from missing data.

body:
## Summary
- Adds a new `proof` block type to the Website Builder canvas.
- Gives founders a structured way to add trust metrics, testimonials, press mentions, or credibility claims to draft landing pages.
- Updates WebsiteBuilder and type guard tests so the new block is covered in edit mode, preview mode, append behavior, and runtime type validation.

## What changed
- Added `proof` to the `WebsiteBlockType` union and `isWebsiteBlockType` guard.
- Added an `Add Proof` option to the Website Builder block picker.
- Added default proof-block copy focused on reducing buyer hesitation.
- Rendered proof blocks in preview as a distinct proof section, splitting newline-separated body copy into individual proof cards.
- Expanded tests for WebsiteBuilder and type guards.

## Why this change
The current Website Builder supports hero, features, CTA, and text sections, but it does not give founders a dedicated affordance for credibility proof. That makes generated landing pages easier to leave as feature-led drafts even when buyers need trust signals before taking the next step.

This improvement keeps the change narrow while addressing a high-leverage conversion gap: founders can now add proof points directly into the landing-page canvas instead of forcing testimonials, ratings, or traction metrics into a generic text block.

## Competitor/benchmark observations
- Mixo emphasizes conversion and trust on its homepage with a clear lead-generation promise, `Trusted by 750k+ businesses`, `4.8/5 on Trustpilot`, customer stories, and metrics such as `3M+ websites created`: https://www.mixo.io/
- Venturekit combines an AI planning promise with trust metrics and tangible outcomes, including `Trusted by 750k small businesses`, `28 pages`, `82 hrs avg time saved`, and customer stories: https://www.venturekit.ai/
- ValidatorAI pairs startup validation with visible proof such as `309325 entrepreneurs`, Product Hunt rating, recent idea scores, and founder-signal analytics: https://validatorai.com/
- Productboard Spark frames AI outputs around context-aware workflows and proof from customer quotes/time-saved claims, reinforcing that AI product experiences benefit from structured, credible artifacts: https://www.productboard.com/product/spark/

## Files changed
- `src/lib/types.ts` — adds the `proof` WebsiteBuilder block type and runtime guard support.
- `src/lib/__tests__/types.test.ts` — covers `proof` as an accepted website block type.
- `src/components/WebsiteBuilder.tsx` — adds `Add Proof`, default proof copy, and proof preview rendering.
- `src/components/__tests__/WebsiteBuilder.test.tsx` — covers proof edit visibility, Add Proof behavior, preview rendering, and newline splitting.

body: ## Summary Follow-up to #14. User reported the Merriweather sprite "flies up" while walking while CowNPC walks fine. Root cause: I hardcoded `Main.npcFrameCount[Type] = 25` in `SetStaticDefaults`, but the Guide (whose `AnimationType` we reuse) actually has 26 frames. Both our placeholder and the real intended sheet are sized for 26 × 56 px = 1456 px tall (same as `CowNPC.png`). With only 25 declared frames the game slices the sheet at 1456 / 25 ≈ 58.24 px per row, so each walk frame pulls from a progressively higher offset and the sprite drifts upward. Fix: mirror what `CowNPC` already does and set `Main.npcFrameCount[Type] = Main.npcFrameCount[NPCID.Guide]`, so our frame count stays in lock-step with the sheet layout the Guide animation expects. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] In-game: Wall-of-Flesh already dead, talk to Merriweather, then watch him walk around the house — his feet should stay on the ground, no vertical drift. - [ ] Shop / head icon / bestiary still behave as before. ### Notes - 1-line code change; build passes with `dotnet build --warnaserror`. - No sprite changes — the placeholder and any future 40×1456 sheet both work with this fix. body:
## Summary

Phase D Step 5-full. Single-validator end-to-end was covered in #371 (Step 5-lite). This extends to 4 independent Blockchain instances processing the SAME boundary block — proves the consensus-jail dispatch produces bit-identical state across peers (the actual mainnet invariant).

**Test-only PR** — no production-path changes. Code remains fork-gated (\`JAIL_CONSENSUS_HEIGHT=u64::MAX\` default).

## Tests

### \`phase_d_4validator_consensus_jail_determinism\` (positive)

1. Spin up 4 independent Blockchain instances with identical initial state (same active_set, same \`LIVENESS_WINDOW\` of misses)
2. Pad all 4 to (boundary - 1)
3. validators[0] = proposer; \`create_block_voyager\` → boundary block has \`tx[0]=coinbase\` + \`tx[1]=JailEvidenceBundle\`
4. Apply that exact block on all 4 via \`add_block\` (each runs Pass-1 + Q4 + Pass-2 + Phase C dispatch independently)
5. Asserts:
   - All 4 have \`downer.is_jailed = true\`
   - All 4 have **IDENTICAL** \`state_root\` (consensus determinism — if any diverges, mainnet would fork at this height)

### \`phase_d_4validator_diverging_evidence_rejected\` (negative)

Mutates ONE record on a peer's LivenessTracker so its \`compute_jail_evidence\` returns different counts than the proposer's. Asserts the peer REJECTS the block via dispatch's recompute-and-compare. **Safety mechanism** preventing a malicious/buggy proposer from jailing legitimate validators.

## Verification

- 5 consecutive runs of \`cargo test --test phase_d_4validator_determinism\`: 2/2 stable
- Full lib suite: 205/205 still green
- \`cargo clippy -p sentrix-core --tests -- -D warnings\` clean

## Phase D status

| PR | Step | Status |
|---|---|---|
| #368 | Step 1+2: helper + system tx auth | merged |
| #369 | Step 3+4: block_producer emit + Pass-1/2 skip | merged |
| #371 | Q4 presence + Step 5-lite (single-validator e2e) | merged |
| #372 (this) | Step 5-full (4-validator determinism) | open |

After this merges, **Phase D is code-complete + fully tested**. Next steps are operator-only:
- Step 6: testnet bake 24-48h with \`JAIL_CONSENSUS_HEIGHT=<low>\`
- Step 7: mainnet activation = halt-all + simultaneous-start with env var on all 4 validators

## Test plan

- [x] \`cargo test -p sentrix-core --lib\` (205/205)

author: ad-claw000
body:
This PR fixes the issue where `aperturedb` dependencies from PyPI were being cached during the Docker image build process. Even if a newer version of `aperturedb` was released on PyPI, Docker layer caching would reuse the old cached `pip install` layer because `requirements.txt` was not explicitly pinned/changed.

By adding `ADD "https://pypi.org/pypi/aperturedb/json" /tmp/aperturedb_version.json` right before the `pip` installation steps, Docker will now automatically detect whenever the PyPI package version updates and correctly invalidate the cache layer, forcing it to fetch and install the latest version.

author: slzwei
body:
## Summary
Fixes two production bugs surfaced by the new synthetic `mktr-lead-unassigned` probe. Both are in the path of MKTR's `lead.unassigned` webhook events.

### Bug 1 — `lead_activity_type` enum missing `'unassignment'`
- File: `supabase/functions/receive-mktr-lead/index.ts:170`
- Edge fn writes `type: 'unassignment'` to `lead_activities` on every `lead.unassigned` event.
- Enum doesn't include this value → INSERT silently fails (edge fn does not `await` or check the error).
- **Effect on prod today**: every `lead.unassigned` event loses its audit row. No way to tell from the DB which leads were unassigned via MKTR vs reassigned vs created.

### Bug 2 — `trigger_notify_lead_reassigned` doesn't null-guard
- File: defined in an earlier migration, runs AFTER UPDATE on `leads.assigned_to`.
- When MKTR sends `lead.unassigned`, the edge fn does `UPDATE leads SET assigned_to = NULL`.
- The trigger fires and calls `notify_insert(NEW.assigned_to, ...)` with `NEW.assigned_to = NULL` — violates `notifications.user_id NOT NULL`.
- The constraint violation aborts the entire UPDATE with a Postgres 500 — receive-mktr-lead returns `{"error":"Failed to unassign lead"}` to MKTR.
- **Effect on prod today**: MKTR's `lead.unassigned` events have been failing 500 on prod since `assigned_to` became nullable. The lead row is never updated, no notification is sent. This is a silent regression — MKTR has either been retrying or quietly disabling the webhook.

## Verification
Both fixes applied to staging via the synthetic-monitoring rollout. The R1c probe round-trip is now green:
- Create a lead, send `lead.unassigned`, assert `lead.assigned_to IS NULL` AND `lead_activities` has a row of type `'unassignment'` AND the lead row still exists (not deleted).

## Risk

author: timotejadamec
body:
## Problem Statement

The Snag desktop app wrote files to inconsistent and partially non-conventional locations:

- `JvmAppDataDirResolver` routed SQLite (`snag.db`, `sync.db`) and the Coil image cache through OS-conventional dirs, but on Windows pointed at `%APPDATA%` (Roaming). Roaming is wrong for the data: photos and DB are too large to roam across domain machines.
- Two sites bypassed the resolver entirely with a hardcoded `~/.snag/` dotfile:
  - `RealLocalFileStorage` wrote project + finding photos to `~/.snag/files`
  - `JvmEncryptedSettingsStore` wrote `auth.keystore` + `auth-tokens.enc` to `~/.snag/`
- Coil's image cache shared the data dir, ignoring first-class OS cache slots (macOS `~/Library/Caches`, Linux `$XDG_CACHE_HOME`).

## Solution

Two-slot model: every desktop file resolves through one of two OS-conventional dirs.

| OS | Data (DBs, photos, auth) | Cache (image_cache) |
|---|---|---|
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/cz.adamec.timotej.snag/` | `~/Library/Caches/cz.adamec.timotej.snag/` |
| Windows | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\cz.adamec.timotej.snag\` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\cz.adamec.timotej.snag\Cache\` |
| Linux | `$XDG_DATA_HOME` or `~/.local/share/cz.adamec.timotej.snag/` | `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` or `~/.cache/cz.adamec.timotej.snag/` |

Implementation:

- Added `JvmCacheDirResolver` interface + `RealJvmCacheDirResolver` impl, mirroring the data resolver.
- Renamed `JvmAppDataDirResolver` param `appData` → `localAppData`; flipped Windows fallback from `AppData/Roaming` to `AppData/Local`.
- `RealLocalFileStorage` now receives `<dataDir>/files` from Koin instead of a hardcoded `~/.snag/files`.
- `JvmEncryptedSettingsStore` takes a `baseDir: File`; the auth Koin module composes `<dataDir>` at the outermost layer (mirrors `SqlDriverFactory.jvm.kt`).
- `JvmImageLoaderInitializer` swapped to `JvmCacheDirResolver` and reads `LOCALAPPDATA` + `XDG_CACHE_HOME`.
- Two new build.gradle.kts deps (jvmMain only): `lib:storage:fe:impl` ← `lib:configuration:fe:api`; `feat:authentication:fe:driven:impl` ← `lib:storage:fe:api`.

All env-var/system-property reads stay at the outermost layer; resolvers remain pure functions of their inputs.

## Test Coverage

### Unit Tests

- `RealJvmCacheDirResolverTest` (new) — 9 cases: macOS, Darwin alias, Windows env-set, Windows env-missing fallback, Windows blank-env fallback, Linux XDG-set, Linux XDG-missing fallback, Linux blank-XDG fallback, unknown OS treated as Linux.
- `RealJvmAppDataDirResolverTest` — Windows expectations updated for the Roaming → Local flip; param rename propagated.
- `JvmAppDatabasePathTest` — param rename propagated; `lastAppData` → `lastLocalAppData`.

### Manual Testing

Verify on macOS:
- [ ] Launch desktop app, sign in. Expected after: `~/Library/Application Support/cz.adamec.timotej.snag/auth.keystore` + `auth-tokens.enc` exist; `~/.snag/` does not.
- [ ] Trigger sync. Expected after: `snag.db` and `sync.db` next to the auth files.
- [ ] Take or view a photo. Expected after: `files/projects/<id>/photos/...` in the data dir; `image_cache/` appears under `~/Library/Caches/cz.adamec.timotej.snag/` (not the data dir).

## References

None — `[J:MEP-0]`, no specific ticket.

author: torstendittmann
body:
## Summary

This PR enables out-of-order chunked uploads for the Local storage adapter by replacing the fragile `_chunks.log` file with `.part.{n}` files as the single source of truth.

## Problem

The Local adapter previously tracked uploaded chunks via a `_chunks.log` file. This had several issues:
- **No duplicate protection in `uploadData()`** — re-uploading a chunk would append duplicate log entries, inflating the count and potentially deadlocking the upload.
- **Write-before-move ordering in `upload()`** — the log entry was written *before* the part file was moved. If the move failed, the log and disk were out of sync.
- **No out-of-order support verified** — all existing tests uploaded chunks sequentially, so non-sequential uploads were not covered.

## Solution

### Local Adapter (`src/Storage/Device/Local.php`)
- **Removed `_chunks.log`** entirely.
- **Added `countChunks()` helper** that uses `glob()` to count existing `.part.{n}` files in the temp directory.
- **Fixed `upload()` and `uploadData()`** to:
  - Write/move the part file **first**.
  - Count parts on disk **after** the write succeeds.
  - Trigger assembly only when the count matches `$chunks`.
  - Silently skip duplicate re-uploads if the `.part.{n}` file already exists.
- **Fixed `joinChunks()`** to no longer attempt to delete the (now non-existent) log file.

### Tests
- **`testOutOfOrderUpload`** — uploads chunks 3→1→2 and verifies correct assembly.
- **`testOutOfOrderUploadWithRetry`** — uploads 2→1→retry 2→3, verifying duplicates are ignored.
- **`testJoinChunksMissingPartDoesNotFinalize`** — updated to reflect the safer new behavior (missing parts simply prevent finalization instead of throwing during assembly).
- **`testOutOfOrderPartUpload`** (S3) — uploads all chunks of a large file in reverse order to verify S3 natively supports out-of-order multipart uploads.

### Misc
- Added `.gitignore` to `tests/resources/disk-a/` to prevent test artifacts from being tracked.

## Testing

All upload-related tests pass:
```
OK (9 tests, 29 assertions)
```

The remaining failures in the full suite (`testTransferLarge`, `testTransferSmall`, `testGetFiles`) are pre-existing environment issues (missing AWS credentials / macOS permissions) and are unrelated to these changes.

# Grid Fracture Drop Engine: Hard-Synced CSS Contract

**Y is for Yolo.** The grid is a contract. You celebrate the lock, but the system must fracture. The output must feel like a coherent "Cult Movie" aesthetic, not a wireframe, satisfying the CSS contract and Wei Lin's boundary clamps.

author: bingqinglyu
body:
## Summary

- Add `Promise.race` timeout wrapper around `await entry.task()` in `pump()` to prevent hung promises from permanently jamming session lanes
- New `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` error class for timed-out tasks
- New `taskTimeoutMs` option on `enqueueCommandInLane` (default: 5 minutes, pass `0` or `Infinity` to disable)
- Diagnostic warning logged when a task times out (`lane task timed out: lane=... timeoutMs=...`)
- `timer.unref()` prevents timeout timers from keeping the process alive

## Problem

When an enqueued task's promise never settles (hung upstream API call, dropped WebSocket, unhandled exception), `completeTask()` never runs, `pump()` is never called again, and the session lane is permanently blocked. Session lanes use `maxConcurrent=1`, so one stuck task blocks **all** future messages for that session. The only recovery is a full gateway restart via SIGUSR1 (`resetAllLanes()`).

This affects all messaging channels (WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, webchat) and cron jobs. See #48488 for full root cause analysis with live diagnostic evidence.

## Changes

**`src/process/command-queue.ts`**:
- New `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` error class
- `DEFAULT_TASK_TIMEOUT_MS` constant (5 minutes)
- Extended `QueueEntry` with optional `taskTimeoutMs` field
- `pump()`: race each task against a timeout promise; on timeout, reject the entry, clear `activeTaskIds`, log warning, and call `pump()` to unblock
- Extended `enqueueCommandInLane` opts with `taskTimeoutMs`

**`src/process/command-queue.test.ts`**:
- 6 new tests covering: stuck task timeout + lane unblock, fast task completion, custom per-task timeouts, timeout disable (`taskTimeoutMs: 0`), diagnostic logging, and safe interaction with `resetAllLanes` generation bumps

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm build` passes
- [x] `pnpm test -- src/process/command-queue.test.ts` — all 23 tests pass (17 existing + 6 new)
- [x] `pnpm check` — lint/format clean
- [ ] Deploy to staging gateway and verify webchat sessions auto-recover from stuck lanes

Closes #48488

## Summary

Audit of `ibl5/classes/Utilities/` revealed that 8 classes have exactly one consumer module — they aren't shared utilities, they just live there by convention. Relocating them to their sole consumer's namespace reduces cross-module coupling and shrinks `Utilities` to its true shared core. Additionally, 2 classes had zero production callers and were deleted.

## Changes (5 commits)

1. **Dead code removal:** `SecureCookie`, `ScheduleParser` (+ tests) — zero production callers.
2. **Updater relocations:** `DateParser`, `RecordParser`, `ScheduleHtmParser`, `SeasonPhaseHelper`, `StandingsGrouper` (sole consumers: `ScheduleUpdater`, `StandingsUpdater`, `PowerRankingsUpdater`).

body:
## Summary

- Adds a Redis runner (F020) enabling scheduled jobs to `PUBLISH`, `RPUSH`, `LPUSH`, or `SET` on a Redis server when a matching rule fires
- Implements a hand-rolled, stdlib-only RESP2 codec with no new Zig dependencies, following the same per-execution connect/close pattern established by the AMQP runner
- Assigns persistence discriminant byte `5` (next available after the existing `0–4` mapping) to avoid logfile corruption on upgrade
- Gates integration tests behind a `-Dredis-integration` build flag and wires a `redis:7-alpine` service into CI and `compose.yaml`

## Changes

### Domain
- `src/domain/runner.zig`: Add `redis` variant with `url`, `command`, and `key` fields to the `Runner` tagged union

### Infrastructure — Redis adapter
- `src/infrastructure/redis/resp.zig`: New hand-rolled RESP2 encoder/decoder (array-of-bulk-strings encode, integer/simple-string/bulk-string/error decode)
- `src/infrastructure/runner/redis.zig`: New Redis runner — URL parsing, optional `AUTH`/`SELECT`, command dispatch, fire-and-forget success semantics, 30 s socket timeouts, credential redaction
- `src/infrastructure/runner.zig`: Wire `redis` variant into the runner dispatch table
- `src/infrastructure/persistence/encoder.zig`: Add encode/decode paths for discriminant byte `5` (redis), encoding `url`, `command`, and `key` as length-prefixed strings
- `src/infrastructure/tcp_server.zig`: Parse `redis <url> <command> <key>` tokens in `RULE SET`; validate command is one of `PUBLISH`, `RPUSH`, `LPUSH`, `SET` at parse time; reject unknown commands with `ERROR` before persistence

### Application
- `src/application/query_handler.zig`: Handle `redis` variant in the query/listrules response formatter

### Tests
- `src/functional_tests.zig`: Add functional integration tests for the Redis runner, gated by `redis_integration` build option

### Build & CI
- `build.zig`: Add `-Dredis-integration` build option and `redis_integration` build option flag
- `.github/workflows/ci.yaml`: Add `redis:7-alpine` service container and pass `-Dredis-integration` to the test step
- `Makefile`: Add `test-redis` target (boots compose stack, runs functional tests, tears down)
- `compose.yaml`: Add `redis:7-alpine` service bound to `127.0.0.1:6379` with healthcheck and named volume

### Documentation
- `docs/ADR/0006-redis-runner-design.md`: New ADR documenting six design decisions (codec, TLS, pooling, success semantics, payload shape, persistence discriminant)
- `docs/ADR/README.md`: Register ADR-0006
- `docs/development/architecture.md`: Add `redis` to the `Runner` tagged union description
- `docs/reference/protocol.md`: Document `RULE SET` Redis syntax, allowed commands, URL format, and worked examples
- `docs/reference/types.md`: Add `redis` runner type description, Zig code examples, and binary persistence format layout
- `docs/user-guide/writing-rules.md`: Add Redis runner section with `PUBLISH`, `RPUSH`, and authenticated-URL worked examples
- `README.md`: Mention Redis runner alongside AMQP in feature list and local dev stack instructions

### Housekeeping
- `.gitignore`: Add `dump.rdb` (Redis persistence artifact)
- `CHANGELOG.md`: Record F020 entry
- `.zpm/.gitignore`: Add ZPM knowledge base ignore rules

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests pass: `make test`
- [x] Redis integration tests pass locally: `make test-redis` (requires Docker)
- [x] `RULE SET` with an unsupported command (e.g. `FLUSHALL`) returns `ERROR` before the rule is persisted
- [x] Existing logfiles containing `shell`/`amqp`/`direct`/`awf`/`http` rules load without error after upgrading (persistence discriminant byte `5` does not clash with existing values)

Closes #39

author: gofarrrr
body:
## Summary

First experiment in the producer-stability investigation (design memo §9 ordering). Pure post-hoc analysis — no new pipeline calls.

**Verdict: consensus is not the first architecture lever.** k=2 makes trust *worse* (noisy rate goes from 31% to 50%) because the noisy anchors recur stably while the rare-but-acceptable anchors are each one-off. k=3 cleans trust but kills friction (17%).

## Headline numbers

Sample: post-fix only — rerun4 + rerun5 + rerun6 + rerun7 of `user-launch-independent-fintech`. `rerun3` excluded per §5 sample-contamination guard (pre-fix, contains the removed RMR trust breach).

| k | Anchors | Acceptable | Noisy | Noisy rate | Friction yield (strict / any-honest) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 13 | 6 | 4 | 31% | 33% / 67% |
| 2 | 4 | 2 | 2 | **50%** | 33% / 33% |
| 3 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0% | 17% / 17% |
| 4 | 0 | — | — | — | 0% |

The k=2 row is the headline. Consensus reinforces the wrong things.

## What recurs vs what's diverse

**Noisy anchors that recur at k=2:**
- `cognitive-dissonance` (r4 + r6) — noisy_adjacent on C1
- `checklists` (r4 + r5) — noisy_adjacent on C7

**Acceptable anchors that recur at k=2:**
- `optimism-bias-and-planning-fallacy` (3 of 4 reruns) — acceptable_secondary on C2
- `wysiati` (r4 + r7) — acceptable_secondary on C1

**Lost-but-honest at k=2** (acceptable at k=1, pruned by consensus):
- `step-back` — acceptable_secondary on C1 (r4 only)
- `optionality` — primary with quote drift on C4 (r5 only)
- `premortem` — primary with quote drift on C7 (r6 only)
- `representativeness-heuristic` — acceptable_secondary on C2 (r7 only)

Three of those four (Step Back, Optionality, Premortem) look like genuinely diverse defensible reads of the same source. Architectures that suppress them in pursuit of stability would degrade the product.

## Hypothesis state after E5

| Hypothesis | E5 evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|
| H1 — verifier stochasticity | not directly tested | open; E1 next paid test |
| H2 — fingerprint variance | not directly tested | open; E3 last |
| H3 — recall determinism | not directly tested | open; E2 next zero-cost test |
| **H4 — broad/meta sufficiency blind spot** | **strongly supported** by recurrence of noisy CD/Checklists | **leading; E4 tests next** |
| H5 — honest hypothesis diversity | partially supported by rare-acceptable diversity | partial; coexists with H4 |

## §7 decision tree mapping

Path C (consensus) is **eliminated as the first lever**. Path A (sufficiency gate) and Path B (verifier prompt restructure) remain live. Both target the noisy-recurrence pattern E5 surfaced.

The §7 entry implied: H4 leading + H5 partial. **E4 (broad/meta sufficiency rubric) is next per §9 ordering** — its outcome will discriminate between Path A and Path B.

## What this experiment did NOT do

- Did not run new pipeline calls. Pure post-hoc analysis.
- Did not test against another case. Out of scope here.
- Did not pick architecture. Decision tree requires E4 + (selectively) E1/E2/E3 outcomes.

## Test plan

- [ ] Marcin reviews scoring against §7 decision tree
- [ ] Marcin confirms E4 (sufficiency rubric audit) is the next experiment
- [ ] After merge, separate session executes E4

`supabase secrets set` was mixing explicit secrets with edge runtime secrets from config

somewhat command like `supabase secrets set BAR=bar` could unexpectedly send both `BAR` and secrets from `[edge_runtime.secrets]`

`secrets set` was using `[edge_runtime.secrets]` when building the payload for the bulk create secrets endpoint

That made explicit inputs like args behave unexpectedly because local edge runtime config secrets were included in the same request

### sol

Keep `secrets set` limited to explicit args and `--env-file`

I also considered keeping config secrets only for noarg `secrets set`

That would preserve the old  behavior while still avoiding mixed payloads when args or `--env-file` are used

I kept the other version because `functions serve` already handles edge runtime config secrets and 
remote uploads should be explicit IMO
wdyt?

## What
Added TypeScript interfaces and a runtime validation script for the `Question` and `Option` structures in the `shared-types` package. Additionally, this PR introduces `docs/DEVLOG-GAME.md` to document the schema and log the development progress.

## Why
We need a unified and agreed-upon structure for the questions generated by the AI Agent. Centralizing this schema in `shared-types` ensures that the backend, frontend, and AI Agent share the same data types and validation logic. This will prevent runtime errors caused by unexpected JSON structures.

- Created `Question` and `Option` interfaces in `packages/shared-types/src/question.ts` with strict typing.

body:
## Why this exists - On macOS Catalina+ and newer, `vmmap` can fail with `Mach error 268435459 (ipc/send) invalid destination port` for arbitrary targets, so the previous watchdog path was brittle. - Existing launchd install checks appeared successful, but real first-cron behavior had been failing with exit `255` after startup. ## What changed - Migrated the watchdog into cmuxlayer under `launchd/cmux-memory-watchdog/`. - `launchd/cmux-memory-watchdog/bin/cmux-memory-watchdog.sh` - `launchd/cmux-memory-watchdog/launchd/com.golems.cmux-memory-watchdog.plist` - `launchd/cmux-memory-watchdog/tests/cmux-memory-watchdog.sh` - Updated LaunchAgent program path to: - `/Users/etanheyman/Gits/cmuxlayer/launchd/cmux-memory-watchdog/bin/cmux-memory-watchdog.sh` - Replaced `vmmap -summary` dependency with dual-memory detection: - `aggregate_cmux_rss_bytes()` (sum RSS from cmux + bun children) - `vmstat_compressor_bytes()` (compressor pages × 4096) - Breach now triggers on either threshold: - `CMUX_MEM_WATCHDOG_RSS_THRESHOLD_GB` (default `5`) - `CMUX_MEM_WATCHDOG_COMPRESSOR_THRESHOLD_GB` (default `12`) ## Guardrails implemented - `handle_breach` now reports which signal(s) tripped (`rss`, `compressor`, or both) and both raw values. - No-pid path exits cleanly (`exit 0`) without failure. ## Verification (required) - Ran fixture matrix for: both below threshold, rss-only breach, compressor-only breach, both breach, and no-cmux process. - Performed real launchd first-cron validation: - `launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.golems.cmux-memory-watchdog.plist` - `cp .../launchd/cmux-memory-watchdog/launchd/com.golems.cmux-memory-watchdog.plist ~/Library/LaunchAgents/` - `launchctl load -w ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.golems.cmux-memory-watchdog.plist` - wait `70s` - `launchctl list | grep watchdog` - Observed: `-\t0\tcom.golems.cmux-memory-watchdog` (first-cron run exit 0, not 255) --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Medium risk because it introduces an automated LaunchAgent that can terminate `cmux` based on heuristic memory thresholds, which could cause unintended restarts if thresholds/measurement are off. > > **Overview** > Adds a new `launchd`-driven cmux memory watchdog (`cmux-memory-watchdog.sh`) that checks **both** aggregated cmux/bun RSS (via `ps`/`pgrep`) and system compressed memory (via `vm_stat`), tripping when either threshold is exceeded. > > On breach, it writes a snapshot log, sends a local notification payload, optionally records an event via the brainbar socket, and then terminates `cmux` with a TERM→KILL sequence; a new LaunchAgent plist runs this check every 60s and fixture-based shell tests validate no-breach and breach cases (rss, compressor, or both). > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 9bd9d65e6cf072f80028afb39c4223fe23968e01. author: videothek
body:
Closes #103

## Summary

Compose carried two horizontal action surfaces — the RichTextEditor's format toolbar at the top of the body, and a separate footer row at the bottom with Send / Attach / Talk / Event / etc. As more tools landed the footer was getting close to wrapping, and the user had to look in two places for "what can I do here".

Collapse them into **one bar at the top**, matching the Outlook-Web ribbon idea (no actual ribbon tabs — flat single row with visual dividers between groups).

## Changes

- **\`RichTextEditor\`** gains an \`actionsTrailing?: Snippet\` prop. When present, the editor's toolbar appends \`ml-auto\` + a divider + the snippet contents to the right side of its row, so editor controls and embedder actions read as left-half / right-half.
- **\`Compose\`** declares a \`composeActions\` snippet with two groups separated by a vertical divider:
  - **Attach & share** — Attach / Files / Talk / Event
  - **Send actions** — Save draft / Discard / Send (primary-filled, last in row)
- The bottom \`<footer>\` is **gone**. Cancel renamed to "Discard" with a red-on-hover variant so the destructive action reads as such.

## Visual

Each action button is a stacked **icon + tiny label** (\`flex-direction: column\`, 0.625rem label) — same idiom Outlook Web uses. Compact enough to fit alongside the rich-text controls without wrapping at typical Compose widths. \`:global\` CSS because the snippet renders inside \`RichTextEditor\`'s DOM subtree.

## Design decisions worth noting

- **Single row, no tabs** — issue says "Outlook ribbon but flat (no actual ribbon tabs)". Hiding actions behind tabs would slow the user down.
- **Send at top-right, not bottom** — agreed with the user to standardise on top-right primary-action across the app (matches the icon rail / ribbon-style direction the rest of Nimbus is heading; matches Gmail compose, Linear, Slack composer). Bottom-aligned send fights that consistency.
- **Responsive collapse / label-when-room** — explicit follow-up. The user's note: *"we have to iterate on this part anyway because we have to check the look and feel"*. This PR lays the structural foundation; behaviour tuning lands separately.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open Compose — one toolbar at the top with format/block/insert (left) and Attach/Talk/Files/Event + SaveDraft/Discard/Send (right), separated by vertical dividers
- [ ] Click Send → mail goes out as before
- [ ] Click Save draft → draft saved as before
- [ ] Click Discard → modal closes, Talk-room cleanup runs (#86) if a room was created
- [ ] Click Attach → file picker opens
- [ ] Click Files → Nextcloud picker opens
- [ ] Click Talk → Talk-room modal opens
- [ ] Click Event → calendar event editor opens
- [ ] Confirm no bottom footer remains; the body is taller than before because the footer space is now gone
- [ ] Resize the modal narrow — the toolbar wraps onto multiple rows (responsive collapse comes in a follow-up)

body:
When a player changes position (e.g. SG->C), raw stat comparison is unfair: a C with 14 RPG/10 PPG looks bad vs C average that includes high-scoring natural Cs (PPG weighted 40% in perf formula).

New approach for posChanged players: compare their avg NBA2K grade vs event average grade. The game already normalizes grades per position (a C with 14 RPG earns A-, that grade is the fair comparator).

  delta = clamp(round((gradeNum - evAvgGrade) / evAvgGrade * 20 + winBonus), -8, +8)

Scotty A- (11) vs event avg ~B+ (10): pct=0.1 -> +2 delta instead of -1.

author: e7217
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #279 / #280. The collaborative hint suffix was instructing the agent to *always* synthesize a final answer after a peer-ask — a redundant turn in our model where every agent (and the user) already sees peer replies via INGEST_ONLY broadcast. The mandatory framing also pushed the agent to chain extra peer-asks just to have something to summarise, weakening the depth-1 cascade cutoff.

This PR reframes synthesis as opt-in: the agent only consolidates when the user explicitly asks (e.g. "정리해줘") or when peer answers conflict.

## Why

Discussion in #279 surfaced that:
1. In a group-chat model the user reads peer replies directly — A doesn't need to repeat them.
2. Doorae rooms have `context_window_enabled` defaulted on (#28), so every agent absorbs peer messages as context anyway. A's "종합" is available on demand whenever the user asks for it.
3. Forcing synthesis as the default closes the loop A→B→A which our cascade cutoff is supposed to *prevent*. Removing the requirement keeps the safety net coherent.

## Changes

- `packages/agent/doorae_agent/client.py` — rewrite the `with_collaborative_hint=True` paragraph in `compose_roster_suffix`. One-paragraph change.
- `packages/agent/tests/test_integrations/test_claude_code.py` — update the assertion in `test_collaborative_non_orchestrator_gets_roster_with_hint` to check the new framing AND assert the old "synthesize a final answer" wording is gone (regression guard).

## Test plan

author: jeong-sik
body:
## Summary

Bootstraps the design-system **codegen pipeline**. All outputs land alongside originals with `.generated.*` suffix — **no consumer is migrated and no original file is deleted**. Migration happens in later waves.

### Pipeline

```
dashboard/design-system/tokens/source.ts   ← SSOT (TypeScript)
  ├─ build.ts (tsx)  →  4 generated outputs + DTCG JSON
  └─ scripts/check-equivalence.mjs (postcss + culori) → CI gate
```

### Files added

| File | Purpose | Lines |
|------|---------|------:|
| `dashboard/design-system/tokens/source.ts` | SSOT token authoring (raw + semantic + 2 themes) | 634 |
| `dashboard/design-system/tokens/build.ts` | Codegen driver, idempotent | 262 |
| `dashboard/design-system/tokens/scripts/check-equivalence.mjs` | postcss-AST equivalence + status canon + keeper ΔE | 190 |
| `dashboard/design-system/source_styles/tokens.generated.css` | Preview consumer | 407 |
| `dashboard/src/styles/tokens.generated.css` | Tailwind v4 `@theme {}` entry block (top-level, not @import-ed — required by tailwindlabs/tailwindcss#18966) | 345 |
| `dashboard/src/styles/tokens.generated.ts` | Preact typed const + `TokenName` literal-string union + `tokenVar()` helper | 351 |
| `dashboard_bonsai/src/tokens.ml` + `.mli` | OCaml polyvar `type semantic`, `var_of`, `name_of` for ppx_css interpolation | 691 + 363 |
| `dashboard/design-system/tokens/build/tokens.json` | DTCG 2025.10 format | 1639 |

### Dependencies added

- runtime/dev: `culori ^4.0.1` (OkLCH palette + ΔE), `postcss ^8.5.6` (AST parse), `tsx ^4.20.0` (TS runtime), `@types/node ^22.10.5`.

### Scripts

- `pnpm tokens:build` — regenerate all four outputs + DTCG JSON.
- `pnpm tokens:check` — verify generated CSS matches source on (1) name set, (2) status canon, (3) keeper ΔE < 2.

### Design choices

- **Keeper 12-slot palette is algorithmic**: `oklch({ l:0.68, c:0.09, h:i*30 })` via culori. The check script verifies each slot is within ΔE < 2 (CIE2000) of the OkLCH-generated hex, so palette drift fails CI loudly.
- **Status canon is locked**: `--ok #6b9e6b / --warn #c9a24a / --err #c46a5a / --info #6a8eb0`. Direct hex-equality check.
- **Status -fg is pinned, not derived**: a perceptual lift function would change the existing canon; conservative pinning preserves contrast.
- **Tailwind output is a top-level `@theme {}` block**, not nested under `:root`, per Tailwind v4's entry-CSS requirement.
- **Themes shipped**: `dark-fantasy` (default canonical) + `paper`. `cyberpunk`, `terminal`, `parchment` deferred per scope decision.
- **Sentinels (`_density-scope`, `_motion-scope`)** preserved verbatim for parity with the source, even though they only exist to close `:root` blocks before density/motion overrides.

## Out of scope (do not do in this PR)

- ❌ Modify any consumer (no `main.ts` import changes, no `[%css]` block edits).
- ❌ Delete `tokens.css`, `colors_and_type.css`, `dashboard/src/styles/tokens.css`, or any other original.
- ❌ Touch SPEC.md / SKILL.md / primitives.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm install` — succeeds with new deps
- [x] `pnpm tokens:build` — all 6 outputs written
- [x] **idempotence**: second `pnpm tokens:build` produces zero diff (verified with `git diff --exit-code`)
- [x] `pnpm tokens:check` — all three checks pass: 372 source tokens present, status canon pinned, keeper ΔE < 2
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — green
- [x] `pnpm lint` — green
- [x] `pnpm build` (vite) — green
- [x] OCaml `tokens.mli` + `tokens.ml` — standalone `ocamlfind ocamlc` typecheck + smoke run (`Tokens.var_of \`Color_bg_page` returns `"var(--color-bg-page)"`)
- [ ] `dune build` (full repo) — **pre-existing breakage in `lib/server/server_runtime_bootstrap.ml:36` on origin/main**, unrelated to this PR (Prometheus label-type mismatch present at HEAD `51e51f7331`).

## Next dependency unlock

Wave 2 stack swap (consumer migration) can now proceed because every consumer surface has a generated counterpart available side-by-side.

🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: SSRF and Open Redirect via weak `.includes()` domain validation, and XSS through failure to reject unsupported URL schemas like `javascript:` during sanitization.
🎯 Impact: Attackers could bypass URL checks with domains like `evzone.com.attacker.com` to exfiltrate tokens or force open redirects. Additionally, passing `javascript:alert(1)` to sanitization failed to neutralize it, leading to XSS vulnerabilities.

## 🔁 Remove Hardcoded Claim Detail Page & Migrate to Dynamic Route

### **Overview**

This PR removes the legacy hardcoded `claim-detail/page.tsx` implementation and fully migrates claim detail rendering to a dynamic route-based system (`claims/[id]`) backed by real API data.

The goal is to ensure each claim detail page reflects actual backend data rather than static mock content.

---

### **Problem**

The current implementation has a critical routing and data integrity issue:

* `claim-detail/page.tsx` ignores route parameters
* It relies on hardcoded mock data
* All claim detail pages incorrectly render the same “Climate” claim
* A proper dynamic route exists but is not being used as the canonical path

This leads to a broken user experience and misleading claim information in production.

---

### **Changes Introduced**

#### 🧭 Routing Cleanup

* Removed or redirected `claim-detail/page.tsx`
* Standardized claim detail access via:

  ```
  claims/[id]
  ```

---

#### 🔌 Dynamic Data Fetching

* Introduced `useClaimDetail(params.id)`
* Fetches real claim data from the API based on route parameter
* Eliminates all mock-data usage in production flow

---

#### ⚙️ UI State Handling

* Added proper **loading state** while fetching claim data
* Added **error state handling** for failed or missing claims
* Ensures UI behaves predictably across all request states

---

### **Expected Behavior**

* Visiting `/claims/:id` renders the correct claim from the backend
* Each claim page is unique and dynamically loaded
* No hardcoded or fallback mock claim content is shown in production

---

### **Before vs After**

**Before:**

* Static “Climate” claim shown for all routes
* No dependency on route params
* Mock data used in production flow

**After:**

* Dynamic claim rendering based on `id`
* Real API-driven content
* Proper loading and error states

---

### **Acceptance Criteria**

* [x] Claim detail page renders correct claim based on ID
* [x] No production usage of mock data in claim detail flow
* [x] Loading and error states implemented
* [x] `claims/[id]` is the canonical route for claim details

---

### **Impact**

This change significantly improves:

* Data correctness
* Routing consistency
* Frontend reliability
* Production readiness of the claims module
Closes #80

body:
## Summary

Closes #215

Adds `raise_dispute(caller)` - callable by either the buyer or the seller - which locks the escrow in `Disputed` state, freezing funds until the arbiter resolves it.

## Changes - `contracts/escrow/src/lib.rs`

**New event: `EscrowDisputeRaisedEvent`**
Carries `raised_by`, `token`, `amount`.

**New function: `raise_dispute(env, caller)`**
- Requires auth from `caller`
- Panics if `caller` is neither buyer nor seller
- Panics if status is not `Pending`
- Sets status to `Disputed` - no funds move, escrow is frozen
- Emits `EscrowDisputeRaisedEvent`

author: justice8096
body:
## Summary

The Clerk integration in #83 used \`import { Clerk } from '@clerk/clerk-js'\`, which resolves to Clerk's **headless** core bundle. Calling \`clerk.mountSignIn()\` on a headless instance throws — exactly what users saw on the deployed funnel:

\`\`\`
ERROR Error: Clerk was not loaded with Ui components
    at E.assertComponentsReady (main-QEQF2EIN.js:84:190694)
    at E.mountSignIn (main-QEQF2EIN.js:84:153469)
    at AuthService.mountSignIn (...)
\`\`\`

The sign-in screen rendered the heading text but the Clerk widget below it was missing.

## Root cause

\`\`\`
$ wc -c node_modules/@clerk/clerk-js/dist/{clerk.mjs,clerk.browser.js}
1488989 clerk.mjs           ← npm main, headless (no UI)
 267531 clerk.browser.js    ← UMD bundle, UI included
\`\`\`

Clerk's documented integration pattern is the UMD bundle from their per-instance CDN, not the npm import. The npm package is mostly types + headless core for SSR/server usage.

## Fix

\`AuthService.init()\` now:

1. Decodes the Clerk frontend-API host from the publishable key (base64 suffix — \`pk_test_bWludC1zbmFrZS0yMi5jbGVyay5hY2NvdW50cy5kZXYk\` → \`mint-snake-22.clerk.accounts.dev\`)
2. Injects a \`<script>\` tag pointing at \`https://<host>/npm/@clerk/clerk-js@6/dist/clerk.browser.js\`
3. Waits for \`window.Clerk\` to be defined
4. \`new window.Clerk(pk)\` + \`await clerk.load()\` — same as before but against the UI-inclusive instance

Everything downstream (signals, interceptor token, mount/unmount sign-in, sign out) works identically — only the bootstrap path changed.

A local \`RuntimeClerk\` interface defines the structural shape we touch, so we don't drag in \`@clerk/clerk-js\`'s headless type tree. The npm package stays in \`package.json\` as a dev-time reference but isn't used at runtime; nothing imports from it now, so esbuild tree-shakes it out of the bundle.

## Bundle impact

Should shrink the initial bundle meaningfully since Clerk's headless core no longer ships in the main bundle. The CDN script loads async and is HTTP-cached cross-tab, so first-paint cost is comparable.

## CSP

Existing CSP rules already allow \`https://*.clerk.accounts.dev\` for script-src, so the CDN load is permitted without changes.

## Verification plan

After merge + dashboard rebuild on rogue, hard-reload the funnel URL. The Clerk sign-in widget should render under the heading. Network panel should show a 200 response from \`mint-snake-22.clerk.accounts.dev/npm/@clerk/clerk-js@6/dist/clerk.browser.js\`.

**What this PR does**

- Remove `check_standard_compliance_array` from `src/utilities/utilities.js` and from the utilities export.
- Migrate the four callers (`adaptive_ashrae`, `pmv_ppd`, `set_tmp`, `use_fans_heatwaves`) to the scalar `check_standard_compliance` helper.
- Port the ASHRAE `airspeed_control` cross-field check and a `FAN_HEATWAVES` branch onto the scalar helper so applicability gating is preserved.
- Fix a pre-existing operator-precedence bug in the ISO branch (`key === "v" || (key === "vr" && ...)`) that was masking the `v`/`vr` range check.
- Remove the ASHRAE `[-100, 100]` PMV output gate (port-era artifact not in pythermalcomfort 3.9.3) while preserving the ISO `[-2, 2]` PMV applicability bound from ISO 7730.
- Replace the array-form tests with scalar coverage for the ported branches.
- Remove `t_o_array` from `src/psychrometrics/t_o.js` (its only in-tree caller was the removed helper).
- Remove 18 stale `*_array` display-name keys from `docs_theme/index.js`.
- Remove three broken example files in `docs/examples/` (`calc_adaptive_EN.js`, `calc_pmv_ppd.js`, `calc_utci.js`) that imported array APIs removed in PR #141.

**Why this change is needed**

`check_standard_compliance_array` was the last `*_array` utility export remaining after PR #141. This PR removes it along with the residual references (`t_o_array`, docs theme keys, broken examples), so no `*_array` public export remains at the source level.

**How I tested it**

- [x] `npm test` — 68 suites, 2137 tests, all green
- [x] `npm run build`

**Notes for reviewers**

The ISO precedence fix and `FAN_HEATWAVES` branch are in this PR because the migration would otherwise change behaviour for `use_fans_heatwaves` and silently mask a `v`/`vr` validation gap.

Generated docs are not regenerated in this PR. A fresh `npm run docs` on this branch would also migrate the theme to a multi-page setup, which is unrelated to this cleanup. Docs regeneration is left for a separate pass.

Closes #159. Partially addresses #142.

# Pull Request: CredentialCard Component

## Description

This PR introduces a reusable `CredentialCard` component for the QuorumProof dashboard that displays credential information in an accessible, visually appealing card format.

## Type of Change

- ✅ New feature (adds new component)
- ✅ UI/UX enhancement
- ✅ Accessibility improvement

## Issue

Closes: #331 

## Changes Made

### Component Implementation
- Created `CredentialCard.tsx` - Main component for displaying credentials
- Implemented TypeScript types in `credential.ts`
- Added comprehensive CSS styling in `credentialCard.css`

### Features Implemented
✅ Display Requirements:
- Credential type icon with color coding (degree, license, employment, achievement)
- Credential ID (truncated to first 8 and last 8 characters)
- Subject address display
- Issuance date with relative time formatting
- Attestation status badge (Attested / Pending / Revoked)

✅ Interactivity:
- Click/keyboard navigation to credential detail view
- Full keyboard support (Tab, Enter, Space keys)
- Card rotation and hover effects for non-revoked credentials

✅ Revoked Credentials:
- Muted styling with 0.7 opacity

✅ Accessibility (WCAG AA Compliant):
- Semantic HTML with proper heading hierarchy
- ARIA labels on status badges and interactive elements
- Role attributes for keyboard navigation
- Screen reader friendly
- Full keyboard navigation support
- Focus indicators visible to users
- Respects `prefers-reduced-motion` setting
- High contrast and color-safe design
- Proper use of `<time>` elements with ISO dates

### Project Setup
- Created React + TypeScript dashboard with Vite

- Added mock credential data for demo

- Created responsive grid layout

### Files Added

- ✅ Semantic HTML used throughout

`./gradlew :shared-libs:db-migration:flywayMigrate` fails with `No database found to handle jdbc:postgresql://...` because the Flyway Gradle plugin (v10.x) runs in its **own isolated classloader** — it never sees the project's `runtimeClasspath`. The PostgreSQL JDBC driver was only declared `runtimeOnly`, making it invisible to the plugin at task execution time.

## Changes

- **`shared-libs/db-migration/build.gradle.kts`** — added the JDBC driver and Flyway's PostgreSQL dialect module to the `flyway` Gradle configuration, which is the only classpath the plugin resolves from:

```kotlin
// Flyway Gradle plugin uses its own isolated classloader — runtimeOnly is not enough
flyway("org.postgresql:postgresql")
flyway("org.flywaydb:flyway-database-postgresql")
```

Flyway 10+ requires **both**: the raw JDBC driver and the dialect module. Missing either produces the `No database found to handle` error.

author: spartan-quannguyen
body:
Fixes findings from the security audit + JS dep audit.

## Backend
- **Vuln 1 — admin RBAC:** every `/api/v1/*` admin handler (policies CRUD, users CRUD, audit logs) now calls `requireJWTAdmin(ctx)`. Without this, a `role:user` JWT issued by aegis-auth was accepted for delete-policy / create-user / read-audit-log.
- **Vuln 2 — JWT typ claim:** `jwtauth.Claims` gains `Typ`. OAuth-issued tokens are stamped `typ=refresh`; MCP 60s infra tokens `typ=access`. `/v1/auth/refresh-token` and `/oauth/token` reject anything that is not `typ=refresh`. Hardcoded `Roles: ["admin"]` in the refresh response replaced with the actual claim value.
- **Breaking:** existing user sessions (no `typ` claim) will be rejected at refresh and need to re-login.

## Frontend / dependency hygiene
- `axios` pinned exact, bumped past **GHSA-43fc-jf86-j433** (`>=1.13.5`).
- `frontend/.npmrc` adds `audit=true`, `save-exact=true`, `engine-strict=true`.

## CI
- `pnpm audit --audit-level=high --prod` is now a hard gate.
- Lockfile resolution check (HTTPS-only, registry.npmjs.org).
- `security-scan.yml` re-enabled on push/PR (was workflow_dispatch only).
- `.github/dependabot.yml` configured for **security updates only** (`open-pull-requests-limit: 0`).

## Other
- `.gitignore`: TLS / signing keys (`*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.p8`, `kubeconfig`).

## Verified
- `go test -count=1 ./...` green for every backend module.
- New unit tests cover `requireJWTAdmin` / `requireAdmin` and the typ-claim round-trip.
- `pnpm -r build` green; `pnpm audit --audit-level=high --prod` exit 0.

## Follow-ups (separate PRs)
- Pin GitHub Actions to commit SHA.
- SBOM generation in `build-images.yml`.
- `eslint-plugin-security` wired into `@spartan/eslint-config`.
- `--ignore-scripts` on pnpm install once `pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies` allowlist is established.
- Refresh-token revocation list (currently stateless = no logout / forced revocation).

author: nerdcopter
body:
## Summary

Fixes two independent persistence issues in the Electron main process.

### 1. Last-used dialog folder memory (the main fix)

The `dialog:choose-entry` IPC handler was ignoring `lastDialogFolder` entirely — neither reading it for `defaultPath` nor saving it after a successful pick. The OS therefore fell back to its own recent-files list on every dialog open.

**Fix:** `dialog:choose-entry` now:
- Reads `lastDialogFolder` from `config.json` before opening the dialog
- Uses it as `defaultPath` for both `openFile` and `saveFile` dialogs
- Saves `path.dirname(chosenFile)` back to `config.json` on every successful pick
- Does not update the saved folder on cancel

### 2. Unified config file (config.json)

Replaced the zoom-only `zoom.json` with a single `config.json` that persists both `zoomLevel` and `lastDialogFolder`. This eliminates two competing config formats.

- `loadConfig()` — reads `config.json`, returns `{ zoomLevel, lastDialogFolder }`
- `saveConfig(patch)` — sanitizes known fields (`zoomLevel` clamped to `[MIN, MAX]`, `lastDialogFolder` coerced to string), merges with existing config, writes atomically
- `applyZoom()` calls `saveConfig({ zoomLevel })` directly — no intermediate helpers
- Redundant single-callsite helpers (`loadZoomLevel`, `saveZoomLevel`, `setWebContentsZoom`) removed per best-practices rule

### Files changed
- `main.js` — all changes are in the Electron main process only

body:
## Summary

- Pins the study status SQL literal strings in `apps/capture-worker/src/poller.ts` (spec §5.11)
- `'capturing'` — filter condition in `pollOnce` SELECT: `WHERE s.status = 'capturing'`
- `'visiting'` — state transition write in `maybeAdvanceStudy`: `SET status = 'visiting' WHERE ... AND status = 'capturing'`
- Structural test asserting the write appears after the read in the file

## Why this matters

These are the SQL template-literal strings driving the first leg of the study state machine (`capturing → visiting`). They are not TypeScript types — renaming either compiles cleanly but breaks the poll at runtime: the capture-worker would never pick up studies (wrong filter), or never hand off to the visitor-worker (wrong write value).

This pull request completes Phase 3.1 of the project roadmap by implementing the foundational data model for Points of Interest (POIs) within the map builder application. The changes introduce a new `PointOfInterest` class, a `POIType` enum for type safety, and extend the `MapGrid` class to manage POIs. Additionally, comprehensive unit tests have been added to ensure correctness and maintainability. There are also updates to planning and progress tracking files to reflect the completion of this phase.

**POI Data Model Implementation:**

* Added `PointOfInterest` class with all required properties (id, x, y, type, name, description, customColor, customIcon, createdAt, createdByRule), following an immutable-after-construction pattern for core fields and editable fields for UI editing. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-448215bb7465ea448c9de4a26ea739669e7df1c9c4a1542b8111815b5d9d3bbdR1-R228) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3c0be83f31fb188e28a19378ef144aee709e1567083e9bd9612a5a4a2f91d44aR1-R181)

**Testing and Quality Assurance:**

* Added `PointOfInterestTest.java` with 11 unit tests covering all public methods and ensuring correct behavior for POI creation, editing, and storage in `MapGrid`. author: codebysayak
body:
## Summary
This PR addresses a critical bug in the note parsing logic where octaves greater than or equal to 10 (e.g., "C10", "A#11") were incorrectly parsed. The previous implementation relied on fixed-width string slicing (`.slice(-1)` and `.substring(0, len - 1)`), which assumed all octaves were single digits. This led to incorrect frequency calculations, broken pitch mapping in temperaments, and distorted audio output for higher registers.

### Changes
- **Refactored `noteToPitchOctave`**: Replaced fragile string slicing with a robust regular expression (`/^(.+?)(-?\d+)$/`). This correctly handles:
  - Variable-length note names (accidentals like `A#`, `Bb`, `C##`).
  - Multi-digit octaves (e.g., `10`, `11`).
  - Signed integers for octaves (e.g., `-1`).
- **Widespread Audit & Fix**: Updated all identified instances of the "single-digit assumption" across core utilities and widgets:
    - **`js/utils/musicutils.js`**: Refactored core helpers and `calcOctave` logic.
    - **`js/utils/synthutils.js`**: Fixed frequency calculation and temperament transition paths.
    - **`js/widgets/temperament.js`**: Corrected pitch-to-number mapping and UI frequency displays.
    - **`js/turtle-singer.js`**: Sanitized the synthesizer trigger path for accurate audio playback.

body:
## Summary

Adds Documenso ([documenso.com](https://documenso.com), open-source DocuSign alternative) as a portal app template, following the proxied-app pattern documented in `CLAUDE.md`.

Documenso is a fully-proxied Next.js app (not path-split static + API), so the shape differs from `admitly.io`:

- nginx hand-edit replaces the **entire** generated static block with `proxy_pass` to `documenso-backend:3000`.
- **No `--oauth`** — public per-recipient signing URLs (`/sign/<token>`) must reach the app without portal auth, and Documenso owns its own auth for operators. Putting Google forward-auth in front would break recipient signing.
- Postgres lives on an `internal: true` bridge network so it's unreachable from other portal apps.

## Files

- `apps/documenso/docker-compose.yml` — `postgres:15-alpine` + `documenso/documenso:v2.9.1` (current upstream stable). Two networks (`edge` external + `documenso-internal` internal-only), no host ports, named volume for pg data, bind-mount for the signing cert. Healthchecks on both services.
- `apps/documenso/.env.example` — required crypto secrets, DB URL, SMTP, signing-cert passphrase, upload limit. Inline comments flag the data-loss footgun: losing `NEXT_PRIVATE_ENCRYPTION_*` orphans existing documents.
- `apps/documenso/nginx-site.conf.example` — replacement server block with `client_max_body_size 50m` (default 1m would 413 PDF uploads), proxied `location /`, and 5-minute proxy timeouts for slow PDF rendering.
- `apps/documenso/README.md` — six-step install runbook, backup recipe, upgrade flow, and the OAuth-would-break-signing warning.
- `systemd/portal-app-documenso.service` — `oneshot` + `RemainAfterExit` unit running `docker compose up -d` in `/srv/portal-apps/documenso/`, with `Requires=portal-nginx.service` so the routing edge is up first. Same `restart` (not `start`) gotcha as the existing portal units.
- `.gitignore` — generic `apps/*/.env`, `apps/*/certs/`, `apps/*/uploads/` patterns so future apps inherit the same rule. The `*.example` templates stay tracked; operator-populated copies live at `/srv/portal-apps/<name>/` and never come back into the repo.

## Test plan

- [ ] `docker compose -f apps/documenso/docker-compose.yml config` validates clean once a `.env` is staged from `.env.example` *(verified locally)*.
- [ ] CI passes (`bash -n`, shellcheck, gitleaks). No shell scripts touched, but gitleaks scans the new `.env.example` — `CHANGEME-*` placeholders shouldn't match any rule.
- [ ] On a staging host: copy `apps/documenso/` → `/srv/portal-apps/documenso/`, follow the README, hit `https://sign.<fqdn>/`, complete an end-to-end signing flow (upload PDF → invite recipient → recipient signs via emailed link → final signed PDF downloads).
- [ ] Verify the postgres container has no port published on the host and no route off `documenso-internal` (`docker inspect documenso-postgres` shows only the internal network).
- [ ] Reboot the staging host and confirm both `portal-nginx.service` and `portal-app-documenso.service` come up cleanly with the documenso site reachable.

## Summary First exercise of the new CHANGELOG-driven auto-tag-on-merge release pipeline. Cuts v0.5.1, a repository-infrastructure-only patch release. This release bundles all the post-v0.5.0 governance and tooling work that has merged onto `main` (PRs #11, #12, #13–15, #16) plus two small workflow correctness fixes from deferred Codex P2 findings: 1. **Versioning narrative softened** in `ROADMAP.md` to acknowledge that pre-1.0 releases may include compatibility-tightening changes when documented in the changelog (matching the v0.3.0 `cri_tier` precedent). 2. **Regex dot-escaping** in both release workflows, so a malformed CHANGELOG heading like `0x6x0` cannot satisfy a `0.6.0` release. Bash parameter expansion `${VERSION//./\\.}` produces a regex-safe form before grep and awk pattern matching. The CHANGELOG entry includes everything that landed since v0.5.0. ## Test plan This PR is itself the smoke test of the release pipeline. The expected end-to-end behavior: - [ ] `Release notes check` workflow passes on this PR (validates branch name format, dated CHANGELOG section presence, tag absence on origin) - [ ] All other CI checks pass: schema drift guard, validator CI, Codex review, Greptile review - [ ] On merge: `Release on merge` workflow fires, resolves version `0.5.1` from branch name, finds no existing `v0.5.1` tag, checks out the merge commit, extracts the v0.5.1 CHANGELOG section as release notes, creates and pushes annotated tag `v0.5.1`, runs goreleaser to build six-platform binaries with `CLIVersion=0.5.1`, publishes the GitHub Release with binaries and notes attached - [ ] Verify `ulc version` on a downloaded binary reports `0.5.1` (validates the goreleaser `-ldflags` wiring end-to-end) ## Callouts for reviewers 1. **No spec changes.** Reference records and templates from v0.5.0 are unaffected. This release ships zero normative content. 2. **The CHANGELOG entry includes out-of-band changes** (org team creation, ruleset patches, label set application). These were applied via the GitHub API during the v0.5.1 development window and are recorded in the changelog narrative for traceability even though they're not in the file diff. 3. **FUNDING.yml stays a placeholder** per the deferred-until-identified plan for founding partners. 4. **If the release pipeline fails:** the workflow has idempotent retry. Re-trigger via `workflow_dispatch` with version `0.5.1`. If the tag was pushed but goreleaser failed, the retry checks out the existing tag and re-runs goreleaser only. 5. **Recovery if everything goes sideways:** no tag protection ruleset means you can `git push --delete origin v0.5.1` and re-cut from a fresh branch.
