## Summary

The interactive `HomeAutomationDemo` embedded on **/services/smart-lighting** wasn't working well and looked rough. This PR rips it out and replaces it with a clean, non-interactive **"Lighting Path"** section that fits the current Symphony direction.

### What changed

- **Removed** `ServiceDemoSection` + `HomeAutomationDemo` from the Smart Lighting page (and their imports)
- **Added** a new "Lighting Path" section with 5 readable cards titled *"What a real lighting system has to answer"*:
  1. **Control layer** — Control4 by default; Lutron RadioRA3/HomeWorks as fit-based
  2. **Dimming & load type** — matched dimmers, no flicker, smooth fades
  3. **Keypads & scenes** — Goodmorning / Welcome / Movie / Goodnight / Away in plain English
  4. **Accent & tunable lighting** — tunable-white LED, astronomic schedules
  5. **Shades & daylight** — lighting and shades on the same system

### Why

- Older audience: clunky, half-working interactive demos hurt trust more than they help.
- Strategy: stay product/platform-focused (Control4 default, Lutron fit-based) — not generic "we install lights."
- Visual: a quiet, numbered grid of five cards holds the page together without an interaction surface that can fail.

### Notes

- Kept dark-luxury styling (`bg-black/10`, `border-white/8`, accent-color icons) consistent with the surrounding sections.
- Used `aria-hidden` on decorative icons; `<ol>` semantics for the numbered steps.
- No new dependencies; all icons (`Layers`, `Sliders`, `SquareStack`, `Sun`, `Blinds`) already exist in `lucide-react` and are used elsewhere in the codebase.
- Conservative claims only — no manufacturer specifics that aren't already in the page copy.
- Does not touch any files associated with the still-open PR #19/#20.

## Testing

- [ ] Visual check on `/services/smart-lighting` desktop and mobile (rhythm: dark / dark / dark-lite / transparent / dark / dark / transparent)
- [ ] Confirm 5-card grid: 1 col on mobile, 2 cols on `sm`, 3 cols on `lg`
- [ ] Tab order through page is sensible (no interactive demo to escape from)
- [ ] No console errors, no TS errors

> ⚠️ Build/lint were not run locally: the agent's environment had a full root disk and `npm install` couldn't complete. The change is small, type-safe, and uses only icons + components already present in the codebase, but please confirm the CI build passes before merging.

author: boringdev-dotcom
body: ## Why In production (https://space-exploration-imye.onrender.com/) the user reports the camera angle is wrong and planets aren't centralized in their browser, but I can't repro locally — viewport, DPR, the post-fx composer, and CDN/CORS are all suspects. To make iterative diagnosis tractable, this PR adds an always-on debug overlay that streams per-frame state. The previous PR (#2, already merged) lifted `eyeHeight` from `0` → `1` to match Marble's official viewer (`controls.animateTo((0,1,0), (0,1,-10), 500)` after splat load). That was correct in dev but apparently isn't enough on the user's deployed setup, hence the need for runtime telemetry. ## What Adds `src/hud/debugHud.ts` — a fixed-position overlay pinned to the top-center of the screen that reports: - **App state** + **active scene name** (launch / flight / surface) - **Camera** position, yaw / pitch / roll, FOV, near / far - **Canvas size** + `window.devicePixelRatio` - **Splat** status, progress, URL, splatCount, position / quaternion / scale - **Splat bounding box** (local-space, plus computed center & size) - **Last error message** if `loadPlanet` failed (e.g. CORS / network / parse) Wires it through `SurfaceScene.getDebugSnapshot()` + `SceneManager.getDebugState()`, mounted in `main.ts`. ### Visibility - **Dev** (`npm run dev`): visible by default. - **Production**: hidden by default. Add `?debug=1` to the URL to force-show it. So users can see it on the deployed build without it cluttering normal sessions. - Toggle at any time with `~` (backtick) or `F1`. Footer has **Copy** (copies the panel text to clipboard) and **Hide** buttons for easy sharing. ## How to use after this deploys 1. Visit https://space-exploration-imye.onrender.com/?debug=1 2. Reproduce the off-center planet / weird camera (e.g. select Luna → fly → land). 3. The HUD pinned to the top-center will show the live runtime state. Click **Copy** or screenshot it — that gives us camera coords, canvas size, DPR, and splat bbox in one place. ## Walkthrough [Debug HUD shown over the launch screen with state=launch and the launch camera](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-dc161cf8-29fd-4b1a-94ee-0508b559978d/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fdebug_hud_launch.png) Launch screen · debug HUD overlay shows `state=launch`, camera pos/FOV, canvas size, DPR. author: copybara-service[bot]
body:
Adds device, ioctls, and new CapProfiling capability

This makes changes to support [Nsight](https://developer.nvidia.com/tools-overview), a suite of NVIDIA tools to profile GPU workloads, including:

- adds missing classes and ioctls
- adds new "unsafe" function `ctrlGpuExecRegOps`
- adds new capability, `CapProfiling`

In order to mitigate side-channel attacks when exposing the same GPU to two different containers (see "Rendered Insecure: GPU Side Channel Attacks Adds nsight ioctls are Practical" [1]), I am adding a new capability: `CapProfiling`. This follows the implementation from `CapFabricIMEXManagement` and needs to explicitly added with `--nvproxy-allowed-driver-capabilities=all,profiling`.

This also adds the "unsafe" function `ctrlGpuExecRegOps`. This is the case because `NV2080_CTRL_GPU_EXEC_REG_OPS_PARAMS` contains an `NvP64` pointer (`RegOps`) to an array of register operations in the application's address space. `ctrlGpuExecRegOps` copies this array into sentry memory and rewrites the pointer before forwarding to the host, then copies results back. This behavior follows existing nvproxy pattern for ioctls with embedded pointers (e.g. `ctrlGetNvU32List`).

(The parity test also explicitly checks that structs with `NvP64` fields are not registered as simple ioctls. Hence the custom handler that copies the `regOps` array through sentry memory seems the correct approach.)

[1] https://www.cs.ucr.edu/~zhiyunq/pub/ccs18_gpu_side_channel.pdf

author: paudley
body:
This pull request introduces an important bugfix to the SDXL CLIP-G prefix mapping logic in `stable-diffusion.cpp` as used by the Strix Halo build system. The fix ensures that SDXL model checkpoints load correctly by rewriting tensor prefixes in a deterministic and correct order, preventing misclassification and runtime errors. The patch is applied automatically during the build process using a new, idempotent `git_apply` patching mechanism.

**SDXL CLIP-G Prefix Mapping Fix:**

- Added a patch (`patches/sdcpp-sdxl-clipg-prefix.patch`) that changes the `convert_tensor_name` function in `src/name_conversion.cpp` to use a `std::vector<std::pair<>>` for `prefix_map` instead of `unordered_map`. This ensures that specific prefix rules (e.g., `te.1.` → `cond_stage_model.1.transformer.`) are applied before broader rules, fixing the SDXL CLIP-G tensor mapping and preventing loading failures for SDXL checkpoints.

**Build System Improvements:**

- Updated `build-vllm.sh` to support a new `git_apply` patch type, which applies unified-diff patch files using `git apply`. This mechanism is idempotent and checks for a marker substring before applying, ensuring patches are not re-applied and live alongside the build script for version control.
- Modified `vllm-packages.yaml` to register the new patch for the `stable-diffusion.cpp` package, including a description and marker for idempotent application.

author: jdcampbe
body:
## Motivation
hipDNN failed to build under Clang with -Werror,-Wunused-but-set-global because TestGoodHeuristicPlugin.cpp stored the logging callback and log level in file-scope variables that were never read.

We want the good heuristic test plugin to both compile cleanly and reflect real plugin behavior: honor hipdnnPluginSetLoggingCallback / hipdnnPluginSetLogLevel by emitting log output on a meaningful lifecycle event, so tests can observe logging without dead storage.

## Technical Details
projects/hipdnn/tests/test_plugins/TestGoodHeuristicPlugin.cpp
Keep g_loggingCallback and g_logLevel (still set from hipdnnPluginSetLoggingCallback and hipdnnPluginSetLogLevel).
In hipdnnHeuristicPolicyFinalize, after the policy is applied and *applied is set, read g_logLevel and, if g_loggingCallback is non-null, call it with that level and a short fixed message (TestGoodHeuristicPlugin: policy finalized). That gives every assignment to those globals a real use and clears -Wunused-but-set-global.
projects/hipdnn/plugin_sdk/include/hipdnn_plugin_sdk/PluginApi.h (if included in this PR): clarify documentation for optional hipdnnPluginSetLogLevel and backwards compatibility (per existing API design).
No change to exported symbol names; behavior change is limited to the test plugin optionally invoking the host-provided logging callback when a policy is finalized.

## Test Plan
Build the target that compiles TestGoodHeuristicPlugin.cpp with the same warning flags as CI (including -Werror).
Run hipDNN tests that load this plugin and finalize a heuristic policy, if any assert on logging or you want to confirm no regressions.

author: deanmarano
body:
## Summary

- Adds `mysql/temporal-type-cast.ts` — a `typeCast` callback for mysql2 that converts TIMESTAMP/DATETIME/DATE/TIME field types into the appropriate `Temporal.*` types instead of JS `Date` objects. Non-temporal field types delegate to `next()` unchanged. `field.type` in mysql2's typeCast is a string name (e.g. `"TIMESTAMP"`), not a numeric OID.
- Wires `typeCast` into `Mysql2Adapter.newClient`, composing with any user-supplied `config.typeCast` so callers can still intercept non-temporal fields without losing Temporal parsing.
- Pins `@@session.time_zone = '+00:00'` on every new physical pool connection via `pool.on('connection')` — the public typed EventEmitter API on mysql2's promise Pool, which re-emits the underlying pool's `connection` event. Connection is destroyed if the `SET` fails to prevent silent wrong-timezone instants.
- Does **not** call any global mysql2 type registration — scope is per-connection only.

## Test plan

- [ ] Unit tests in `mysql/temporal-type-cast.test.ts`: all temporal field types (TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMP2, DATETIME/DATETIME2, DATE/NEWDATE, TIME/TIME2), NULL passthrough, zero-date → null, non-temporal delegation, NEWDATE as PlainDate
- [ ] Integration tests in `mysql2-adapter.test.ts`: microsecond round-trip for TIMESTAMP(6), DATETIME(6) (millisecond+microsecond), DATE, TIME(6); zero-date → null (with sql_mode probe); sibling raw `mysql2.createConnection` still returns `Date` objects (no global mutation)

## Summary
- Long agentic turns (parallel subagent dispatch, deep mid-stream planning pauses) were hitting the 90 s per-chunk idle watchdog and surfacing as `Stream stalled: no data received for 90s` even on healthy connections.

body:
## Summary

- Draft ADR-0059 capturing the brainstorm of a TLV wire format with content-hashed field tags, scoped to durable component storage (handle store, save files).
- Marked **Proposed (Draft)** — meant as a checkpoint to revisit when the open questions have answers, not a decision to act on.

## Why now

A direct outgrowth of the chat thread that started from the version-graph idea. Field-id self-description dissolves most of the version-skew problem (add/remove/reorder become transparent), leaving a much smaller residual (type changes, semantic renames) that the remap dictionary handles. Wanted the shape captured in tree before context drifts.

## What it does and doesn't commit to

**Does commit to:**
- Three wire shapes (cast, positional-postcard, TLV) with TLV opt-in for storage paths only.
- Content-hashed field tags with a `FIELD_DOMAIN` prefix.
- Synthesized names for anonymous nested types (`anon_<short_hash>`) — gets cross-crate structural identity for shared shape.
- Discipline rules: field hashes are immutable once shipped; renames go through a remap dict; type changes need new hashes.

**Doesn't commit to:**
- How TLV integrates with postcard 1.x (which has no native tagged mode).
- Default-value semantics for missing fields.
- Manifest layout for field hashes and remap dictionaries.
- One-time migration of pre-TLV stored payloads.
- Opt-in mechanism (`#[kind(storage)]` vs implicit).

Section 9 in the ADR enumerates these explicitly so the next pass has a starting list.

## Test plan

- [x] No code change. ADR doc only — `cargo fmt`/`cargo test` not applicable.
- [ ] Held as draft until the open questions converge.

Makes every per-page markdown file LLM-navigable, matching the pattern at [code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/python.md](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/python.md).

Every `.md` emitted by `starlight-page-actions` now:

1. **Opens with a blockquote banner** pointing to `/llms.txt` as the site index, plus links to the three scoped bundles (`user-guide`, `mcp`, `contributing`).
2. **Ends with a curated "See also"** section of 3-5 related pages.

Example top of `/start-here/install.md`:

```
> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://theagenticguy.github.io/opencodehub/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.
> Scoped bundles: [user-guide](...) · [mcp](...) · [contributing](...)

# Install
...
```

Example footer:

```
## See also
* [Quick start](/opencodehub/start-here/quick-start/)
* [First query](/opencodehub/start-here/first-query/)
* [Troubleshooting](/opencodehub/guides/troubleshooting/)
```

## Implementation

- `packages/docs/scripts/inject-llm-nav.mjs` — postbuild Node script. Walks `dist/**/*.md`, prepends the banner, appends per-slug "See also" links from a curated `RELATED` map. Idempotent (skips files that already start with the banner). Skips `llms.txt` family.
- `packages/docs/package.json` — build script becomes `astro build && node scripts/inject-llm-nav.mjs`.

## Curation

All 34 pages have explicit "See also" entries. The map is hand-curated (same approach as the Claude docs), not autogenerated, so related-links stay meaningful rather than noisy.

## Test plan

- [x] Build: 35 pages + 4 llms*.txt + 3 customSets + 34 patched .md
- [x] Banner present on every .md (head check)
- [x] Footer present on every .md (tail check)
- [x] Re-running the injector is a no-op: `patched 0 .md files, skipped 34 already-patched`
- [x] Biome, banned-strings, links-validator all clean
- [ ] `curl https://theagenticguy.github.io/opencodehub/start-here/install.md` shows the new header + footer after merge

body:
Breakout from @vortex73's PR #140112.

Add HasNonTrivialCopyConstructor and HasNonTrivialDestructor flags to RecordFlags, with accessor methods on RecordType. These flags are needed by target-specific ABI classifiers (e.g. X86_64) to determine whether a C++ record type must be passed indirectly per the Itanium ABI.

Also adds unit test infrastructure for the ABI library (llvm/unittests/ABI/) with tests for the new flags and their interaction with existing flags.

This is Narayan's design and logic from the LLVM ABI Lowering Library, adapted to the current upstream API.

author: medugus
body:
### Motivation
- A subset of users had stale/incompatible `localStorage` payloads that passed prior schema checks but were missing nested fields dereferenced by the app shell footer, causing a render-time exception and the global error boundary page to show instead of the dashboard.
- The goal is to restore the app shell quickly with the smallest, non-behavioural change: defensive hydration guards in persistence only.

### Description
- Added a runtime shape guard `isValidMeduguState` and validation in `src/medugu/store/persistence.ts` so `loadState()` now validates parsed JSON, clears incompatible cached key, logs a warning, and falls back to in-memory state. (file changed: `src/medugu/store/persistence.ts`)
- Added a runtime shape guard `isValidConfigState` and validation in `src/medugu/store/configPersistence.ts` so `loadConfigState()` now validates parsed JSON, clears incompatible cached config, logs a warning, and falls back to seeded config. (file changed: `src/medugu/store/configPersistence.ts`)
- Classification: this was hydration-related and component-render-related (invalid hydrated localStorage shape causing render-time dereferences); not an import/export/path issue and not a route change. The fix only affects persistence/hydration wiring and provides a safe fallback; no clinical, AST, AMS, IPC, validation, release, export, or auth logic was modified.

### Testing
- `npm run build` — passed (production client + SSR builds completed).
- `npm run typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`) — passed.
- `npm test` — logic test suite passed (14/14 tests).
- `npm run dev` — dev server started and root responded (`http://127.0.0.1:4173/` returned HTML).
- `npm run lint` — failed due to pre-existing repository-wide prettier/eslint issues unrelated to this change (not introduced by this PR).

Files changed:
- `src/medugu/store/persistence.ts`
- `src/medugu/store/configPersistence.ts`

Root cause: invalid/stale `localStorage` shape allowed through earlier checks which led to undefined nested fields being accessed during app-shell render.

How the fix restores app load: invalid cached payloads are now detected and evicted at load time so React consumers receive a safe fallback state instead of an incompatible object, preventing render-time exceptions and allowing the app shell and dashboard to render normally.

Confirmation: no clinical or product behaviour changed; this is a defensive hydration/persistence fix only.

author: nickhamze
body:
## Problem

PR #69 unblocked the reship by teaching `iter_themes()` to include `incubating` themes in design-pipeline scripts. The next batch run got past seed + sync but failed at snap for every theme:

```
Error when executing the blueprint step #10: PHP.run() failed with exit code 1.
=== Stderr ===
Error: W&O CSV looked malformed: fewer than 2 lines after trim.
```

### Root cause

`bin/snap.py::_auto_detect_content_ref` rewrites the blueprint's `raw.githubusercontent.com/<org>/<repo>/main/` URLs to the current branch name IFF `origin/<branch>` exists. In a fresh `bin/design-batch.py` worktree, the feature branch has never been pushed, so the detection falls back to `main` — but `main` has no `<slug>/playground/content/*` or `/images/*` for a brand-new theme. Every URL 404s, PHP parses the 404 HTML as CSV, and Playground boot dies at step #10 (`wo-import.php`).

`first-baseline.yml` doesn't hit this because CI checks out the PR head (already pushed) and sets `FIFTY_CONTENT_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}` explicitly. Local `design-batch.py` runs had no equivalent.

## Fix

New phase F½ `prepublish` sits between `sync` and `snap`:

1. No-op on `main`, detached HEAD, or under `--skip-publish` / `--skip-commit` / `--skip-prepublish`.
2. Stages `<slug>/`, `docs/`, and every theme's `playground/blueprint.json` (sync-playground may have touched them all).
3. Commits `design: scaffold <slug> (pre-snap content publish)` iff anything is staged (idempotent on re-runs).
4. `git push -u origin HEAD` with `FIFTY_SKIP_VISUAL_PUSH=1` and `FIFTY_SKIP_EVIDENCE_FRESHNESS=1` — both legitimate because this phase by definition runs BEFORE snap produces any evidence.

Phase N (`commit`) still sweeps up baselines + screenshot + docs as a second commit on the same branch. The batch-armed auto-merge squash-merges the two on merge — so the main-branch history stays one-commit-per-theme.

### Skip-flag contract

| Flag | Prior behaviour | New behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `--skip-commit` | drops `commit`, `publish` | also drops `prepublish` (it IS a commit) |
| `--skip-publish` | drops `publish` | also drops `prepublish` (it's a push) |
| `--skip-prepublish` | — | NEW: drops only `prepublish`; primarily for rebaselining an already-shipping theme |

## Guards

`tests/tools/test_design_phases.py` (AST-based, ~0.1s):

- `prepublish` precedes `snap` in `PHASES`
- `prepublish` is registered in `_PHASE_HANDLERS`
- `--skip-publish` drops `{prepublish, publish}`
- `--skip-commit` drops `{prepublish, commit, publish}`

## Verification

- `python3 -m pytest tests/tools/test_design_phases.py tests/tools/test_design_batch.py tests/tools/test_iter_themes_call_sites.py` — 13/13 pass locally.
- `python3 bin/check.py --all --offline` — green on pre-commit (baseline allowlist in effect on branch).
- `python3 bin/design.py --help` — argparse accepts the new phase + flag without complaint.

## Follow-up

Once this merges: `python3 bin/design-batch.py --from-concepts --limit 5` should finally ship five themes hands-off.

author: panda850819
body:
💡 What: Optimized the `apply_replacements` function in `src-tauri/src/settings.rs` to use `std::borrow::Cow` instead of immediately allocating a new `String`. Added a `.contains` check to ensure `.replace` is only called (and heap memory allocated) when the pattern actually exists.

🎯 Why: In Rust, `str::replace` always allocates a new `String` and copies memory, even if the target substring isn't found. This caused N unnecessary memory allocations per invocation (where N = number of replacement rules), which is highly inefficient for text processing pipelines on the hot path. 

📊 Impact: Reduces heap allocations in `apply_replacements` from `O(N)` down to `O(M)` (where M is the number of *actual* matches). If no rules match, 0 allocations are performed during the loop.

🔬 Measurement: Run a benchmark or trace memory allocations in the hot path when applying multiple text replacement rules. Verify that zero heap allocations are triggered by the loop iteration for non-matching rules.

author: elcoosp
body:
## Summary

Extracts pure routing logic into a new `navi-router-core` crate with zero GPUI dependencies, refactoring `navi-router` into a thin GPUI adapter layer. This enables the routing core to be reused with any UI framework while maintaining full backward compatibility for existing GPUI applications.

## Changes

### New: `navi-router-core` crate
- **`RouterCore`** — state machine that returns `NavigationEffect` enums instead of performing side effects directly
- **`RouteTree`** — radix trie for O(log n) path matching (with integrated `RouteTrie`)
- **`History`** — browser-style history stack (stripped of `WindowId` dependency)
- **`Blocker`** — navigation guard support
- **`Location`**, **`Redirect`**, **`NotFound`**, **`Validation`** — all pure data types moved from `navi-router`
- **`AnyData`** — type-erased loader data wrapper
- Unit tests for core navigation and trie matching

### Refactored: `navi-router` → GPUI adapter
- `RouterState` now wraps `RouterCore` and interprets `NavigationEffect`s
- Loader execution, redirects, and UI refresh are handled via the effect pattern (`SpawnLoader`, `Redirect`, `NotFound`, `NotifyListeners`)
- All core types re-exported at crate root for backward compatibility
- `Navigator` simplified to delegate to adapter's `RouterState`

### Updated
- **`navi-codegen`** — removed unused stub generation logic
- **`navi-devtools`** — uses new `can_go_back()`/`can_go_forward()` delegate methods
- **`navi-test`** — integration tests updated to work without GPUI test harness
- **`Cargo.toml`** — workspace member added

### Removed
- `radix_tree.rs` (superseded by integrated trie in core)
- All `.bak`, `.orig`, `.rej` patch artifacts

### Docs
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — core/adapter architecture overview with adapter writing guide
- `docs/v0.2.0.md` — full specification suite (vision, BRS, SRS, architecture, behavioral spec, implementation plan)
- `justfile` — convenience commands for test, clippy, fmt, build

## NavigationEffect pattern

```rust
pub enum NavigationEffect {
    SpawnLoader { route_id: String, params: HashMap<String, String> },
    Redirect { to: String, replace: bool },
    NotFound { data: Option<serde_json::Value> },
    NotifyListeners,
}
```

The core never touches `cx.spawn` or `QueryClient` — it returns effects for the adapter to interpret, making it trivial to write adapters for Dioxus, egui, or other frameworks.

## Backward compatibility

All existing route files, `define_route!` macros, and generated code compile unchanged. The `navi-router` crate re-exports every previously-public type from core.

author: vesta-upstream[bot]
body:
## Summary

Two CLI traps surfaced today that the existing SKILL.md didn't warn about, both upstream `agentmail-cli` quirks: it parses string flag values (`--headers`, `--subject`) as YAML.

1. **Replies via `send --headers In-Reply-To=<msg-id>`** fail because the angle-bracketed Message-Id starts with `<` which YAML treats as a flow-style opener. Switching to `inboxes:messages reply --message-id` works (the CLI sets `In-Reply-To` + `References` server-side, thread_id matches the original).
2. **`--subject "Re: topic"`** fails with `expected string, received object` because YAML reads `": "` as a mapping. Bisected: `Re:topic` works, `Re: topic` fails.

Both are bugs in the compiled Go binary at `agentmail-cli/bin/.agentmail`. Until they're fixed upstream, the skill should warn agents off these rabbit holes.

## Change

Two new entries in the Common mistakes table.

- [ ] CI green (markdown only, should be trivially fine)

author: petrsvihlik
body:
## Summary
Closes the three unresolved boxes in #215.

- **`WopiProofValidator`** — actually use the injected `TimeProvider`, parse `X-WOPI-TimeStamp` with `long.TryParse` + `DateTimeKind.Utc`, reject timestamps too far in the future (5-min skew on top of the 20-min staleness check), and drop dead code (double `ToUpperInvariant`, redundant local).
- **`ProxyAwareRouteUrl`** — prepend `X-Forwarded-PathBase` when it differs from `Request.PathBase` so generated WOPI URLs match what the proof signs over. Removed the misleading `pathBase` local (actually full absolute path) and the silent trailing-slash trim.
- **`WopiFile.Version`** — `LastWriteTimeUtc.Ticks` instead of `"yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.fffZ"`. Same intent (back-to-back PUTs in the WOPI validator need distinct versions) with 100ns resolution and no string-format gymnastics.
- **`WopiProofValidatorTests`** — 11 new tests: missing headers, malformed timestamp, expired/future timestamps, valid current key, valid old key (rotation), valid `X-WOPI-ProofOld` matching current key, tampered signature, discoverer throws.

The Copilot inline comment on #212 suggesting `DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeSeconds` is intentionally **not** applied — per the WOPI spec, `X-WOPI-TimeStamp` is `DateTime.Ticks`, not Unix seconds.

## Test plan
- [x] `dotnet build WOPI.slnx` clean (0 warnings, 0 errors)
- [x] `dotnet test WOPI.slnx --framework net9.0` — all 263 tests pass (incl. 11 new)
- [ ] CI runs net8/9/10 on Ubuntu

author: kctong529
body:
This PR completes the research-side SSAL-native route-evaluation refactor. The main goal is to replace the old exploratory ORS/routingpy-based offline evaluation path with a shared evaluator that uses the same graph representation shown to the model: ```text GeoPackage ↓ SSAL text ↓ SSAL-derived graph ↓ Dijkstra ground truth ↓ shared route evaluator ↓ offline history evaluation helpers / CLI ``` This PR also provides an easy-to-use foundation for the new dashboard design. By moving graph loading, route evaluation, history-row adaptation, summaries, and JSON output into reusable `research.*` modules, the dashboard can call the same evaluation path directly instead of reimplementing or shelling out to script-specific logic. The final result is a reusable evaluation stack under `research.*`, with `scripts/evaluate_history.py` kept as a thin CLI wrapper. ## Release note This PR establishes the first usable research package milestone: `v0.1.0`. In this context, `v0.1.0` means: - the research repo now has a coherent importable Python package structure - SSAL-native route evaluation is available through reusable `research.*` modules - offline history evaluation can be run through a documented CLI - the default evaluator no longer depends on ORS/routingpy - regression tests and CI cover the core graph/evaluator/loader/history workflow This does not mean the route-quality metrics or APIs are final. It marks the first stable foundation for the new dashboard design and future evaluator iterations. ## Architecture overview The diagrams below show the intended module boundaries and runtime flow at a high level. ```mermaid flowchart LR %% Inputs GPKG[GeoPackage] ROW[History row / export] RESP[Model response] %% research.network_loader subgraph NL_MOD[research.network_loader] NL1[Load GeoPackage] NL2[Generate SSAL text] NL3[Build NetworkBundle] NL1 --> NL2 --> NL3 end %% research.graph subgraph GR_MOD[research.graph] GR1[Build Graph from SSAL] GR2[Graph helpers] GR3[Dijkstra shortest path] GR1 --> GR2 --> GR3 end %% research.evaluation subgraph EV_MOD[research.evaluation] EV1[Recover JSON] EV2[Extract path / declared length] EV3[Validate candidate path] EV4[Compare against ground truth] EV1 --> EV2 --> EV3 --> EV4 end %% research.history_evaluation subgraph HE_MOD[research.history_evaluation] HE1[Load entry / history JSON] HE2[Extract metadata and route context] HE3[Evaluate rows] HE4[Summarize results] HE5[Format / write JSON output] HE1 --> HE2 --> HE3 --> HE4 --> HE5 end %% Entrypoints subgraph ENTRY[Entrypoints] CLI[scripts.evaluate_history] DASH[New dashboard design] end %% Main connections GPKG --> NL1 NL3 --> GR1 RESP --> EV1 ROW --> HE1 GR3 -. used by .-> EV4 EV4 --> HE3 NL3 --> HE3 CLI --> HE1 DASH -.-> HE1 DASH -.-> EV1 DASH -.-> NL1 ``` ## Evaluation sequence ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber actor User participant CLI as scripts.evaluate_history participant HE as research.history_evaluation participant NL as research.network_loader participant G as research.graph participant EV as research.evaluation User->>CLI: Run with --entry-json or --history-json CLI->>HE: evaluate_entry_file() or evaluate_history_file() HE->>HE: load_entry() or load_history() HE->>NL: load_network_bundle_from_gpkg() NL->>NL: Generate SSAL text from GeoPackage NL->>G: build_graph_from_ssal(ssal_text) G-->>NL: SSAL-derived Graph NL-->>HE: NetworkBundle(graph, ssal_hash, ssal_text) alt one-entry mode HE->>HE: get_entry_metadata() HE->>HE: get_route_context() alt missing route context HE-->>CLI: skipped result
reason = missing_route_context else route context available HE->>EV: evaluate_route_response(response_text, graph, origin, destination) EV->>EV: clean_json() EV->>EV: extract_path() EV->>EV: validate_candidate_path() EV->>G: dijkstra_shortest_path(origin, destination) G-->>EV: ground-truth path and length EV->>EV: compare route and length metrics EV-->>HE: evaluation result HE-->>CLI: result + metadata + ssal_hash end else bulk mode loop each history row HE->>HE: get_entry_metadata() HE->>HE: get_route_context() alt missing route context HE->>HE: create skipped row else route context available HE->>EV: evaluate_route_response(response_text, graph, origin, destination) EV->>G: dijkstra_shortest_path(...) G-->>EV: ground-truth path and length EV-->>HE: evaluation result end end HE->>HE: summarize_results(results) HE-->>CLI: summary + row-level results end alt --output provided CLI->>HE: write_results_json(...) HE-->>User: JSON file written else no --output CLI-->>User: JSON printed to stdout end ``` ## Main changes ### 1. SSAL graph model and Dijkstra baseline Adds `research.graph` with: * immutable `Edge` model * directed `Graph` model * SSAL-to-graph parser * target-only node preservation * edge metadata preservation * graph helper methods: * `nodes()` * `has_node()` * `get_edge()` * `has_edge()` * `path_length()` * deterministic Dijkstra shortest-path search over the SSAL-derived graph This gives us a local graph-native baseline instead of relying on an external routing service. Refs #60 ### 2. Shared SSAL-native route evaluator Adds `research.evaluation` with reusable route-response evaluation logic: * JSON recovery from model responses * candidate route path extraction * model-declared `total_length` extraction * candidate path validation against the directed SSAL-derived graph * Dijkstra ground-truth comparison * node overlap and directed-edge overlap metrics * candidate route length error metrics * model-declared length error metrics * top-level `evaluate_route_response()` workflow This module owns route parsing, validation, Dijkstra comparison, and metrics. Offline history evaluation and future dashboard integration should call this shared evaluator instead of duplicating route logic. Refs #61 ### 3. Reproducible network loading Adds `research.network_loader` with: * `sha256_text()` * `sha256_file()` * frozen `NetworkBundle` * `load_network_bundle_from_gpkg()` * `fetch_or_reuse_cached_file()` `NetworkBundle` stores: * GeoPackage path * generated SSAL text * SSAL hash * SSAL-derived graph * edge layer name * node layer name Important design point: the graph used for evaluation is built from the generated SSAL text, not directly from the GeoPackage. This keeps the evaluated graph aligned with the graph representation given to the model. Refs #62 ### 4. Offline route-history evaluation helpers Adds `research.history_evaluation` for reusable dashboard/export row adaptation. It supports: * one-entry history JSON loading * bulk history JSON loading * response-text extraction from `response_text`, `response`, and `text` * metadata preservation: * `entry_id` * `provider` * `model` * `finish_status` * `max_output_tokens` * explicit route-context extraction: * `origin` * `destination` * `route_origin` * `route_destination` * structured skip behavior for missing route metadata: * `status: skipped` * `reason: missing_ro

## Summary
- Adds `UseCaseAndEncryptedTxnsAwareShuffler`, a new `TransactionShuffler` implementation that ensures decrypted (encrypted) transactions stay at the front of the block while preserving use-case and sender spread factors.
- Uses a two-phase approach with a single `ShuffledTransactionIterator`: encrypted txns shuffled first, then regular txns fed into the same iterator so spread state (sender/use-case delay) carries across the boundary.
- Adds `UseCaseAndEncryptedTxnsAware` variant to `TransactionShufflerType` on-chain config enum, selectable via governance.

author: arynshimmy
body:
## Summary

- Renaming a ticket's title (or several other fields) fires a `TICKET_UPDATED` email whose "Changes Made" box renders empty, so recipients see "Ticket Updated" with no indication of what changed.
- Root cause: the change-builder in both server-action paths only tracked `status_id`, `priority_id`, `assigned_to`, `board_id`, `category_id`, `subcategory_id`, and `due_date`. The REST API path in `TicketService.update` did not pass a `changes` payload at all.
- Fix: track `title` and `url` in `structuredChanges` in `ticketActions.updateTicket` and `optimizedTicketActions`, and build the same diff in `TicketService.update` so the REST API path also populates the email.

## Notes

- No template changes needed: the email template at `server/migrations/utils/templates/email/tickets/ticketUpdated.cjs` already renders `{{{ticket.changes}}}`, and `formatChanges()` / `formatFieldName()` / `resolveValue()` in `ticketEmailSubscriber.ts` already humanize keys (`title` → "Title") and pass plain string values through.
- Schema validation at the publisher casts to `any`, so the existing `{ old, new }` shape is preserved (the reader at `ticketEmailSubscriber.ts:326` reads `old`/`new`, not `previous`/`new`).
- Description and tags are intentionally **not** tracked in this PR — description is BlockNote JSON and would render noisily; tags need a comparison helper. Worth a follow-up if desired.

## Test plan

- [ ] Rename a ticket title via the UI and confirm the resulting email's "Changes Made" box reads `Title: <old> → <new>`.
- [ ] Change `priority` and `assigned_to` together via the UI and confirm both lines appear.
- [ ] Update a ticket via the REST API (`PATCH /api/v1/tickets/:id`) with a title change and confirm the email includes the diff (this path previously rendered an empty box for ANY field).
- [ ] Close a ticket via the UI and confirm the `TICKET_CLOSED` email still works (changes flow unchanged).
- [ ] Verify multi-field updates: status + priority change together still render both lines.

body:
## Summary

Adds opt-in support for routing CAPTCHA solver requests through a dedicated proxy via a new `CAPTCHA_SOLVER_PROXY_*` env-var family. **Off by default** — when unset, solvers continue to use proxyless task types exactly as before.

Builds on §11.1 (PR #771) — extends the `_2CAPTCHA_TASK_TYPES` / `_CAPSOLVER_TASK_TYPES` tables and the `_build_task_body` helper rather than introducing parallel structures.

Plan reference: `docs/plans/2026-04-20-browser-automation.md` §11.2.

## Threat model — why agent primary proxy creds are NEVER forwarded

The agent's primary egress proxy (per-agent state in `BrowserManager._proxy_configs`) is a residential / datacenter IP we paid for to scrape from. Forwarding those credentials to a third-party CAPTCHA solver would be a direct credential-leak vector — the solver could exfiltrate, log, or rotate them.

§11.2 enforces credential isolation by requiring a SEPARATE `CAPTCHA_SOLVER_PROXY_*` env-var family for solver-side proxies. The agent's primary creds are never threaded into the solver call path.

**Contract test:** `tests/test_captcha_solver_proxy.py::TestCredentialLeakCanary::test_primary_proxy_creds_never_leak`

This seeds a fake primary proxy with a unique canary string in the password, configures DIFFERENT creds on `CAPTCHA_SOLVER_PROXY_*`, drives a full solve with a mocked httpx client capturing every outbound request, then asserts the canary string appears **zero times** anywhere in those requests AND that the dedicated solver creds DO appear. If this test ever fails, halt and investigate — the credential-leak vector is open.

## Compat-table fallback behavior

`_SOLVER_PROXY_COMPAT` is a hardcoded `(provider, variant) → {accepted scheme}` table verified against current provider docs (April 2026):

* **2captcha** — uniformly `{http, socks4, socks5}` (NO `https`) on documented proxy-aware tasks. v3 / Enterprise-v3 have NO documented proxy-aware variants and are absent from the table; loaders fall back to proxyless. (Source: https://2captcha.com/api-docs/recaptcha-v2 and equivalents.)
* **CapSolver** — full `{http, https, socks4, socks5}` on every proxy-aware variant. (Source: https://docs.capsolver.com/en/guide/api-how-to-use-proxy/)

When the configured scheme is rejected for the variant, OR when the variant has no documented proxy-aware task at all, the body builder:
1. Falls back to the proxyless task name (drops `Task` → `TaskProxyless` / `TaskProxyLess`).
2. Sends NO `proxyType` / `proxyAddress` / `proxyLogin` / `proxyPassword` fields in the body.
3. Sets `last_compat_rejected=True` on the solver instance so `_check_captcha` downgrades the envelope's `solver_confidence` to `"low"` — operator sees the token came from the provider's IP pool, not theirs.

## Cost counter

`estimate_cents(provider, kind, *, proxy_aware=False)` — extended signature (existing call sites continue to use the proxyless tier by default). Proxy-aware rates are ~3× the proxyless rate per provider docs (e.g. 2captcha v2-checkbox: 100¢ → 300¢). When the proxy-aware tier has no entry (2captcha v3), we fall through to the proxyless rate so the price billed matches the request actually sent.

The `_check_captcha` cost-accounting branch reads `solver.last_used_proxy_aware` to pick the tier — no parallel cost path was introduced.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_captcha_solver_proxy.py -v` — 49 passing
- [x] `pytest tests/test_captcha_*.py tests/test_browser_solve_captcha.py tests/test_browser_service.py` — 659 passing, 7 skipped (pre-existing)
- [x] `pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/test_e2e*.py -x` — clean apart from two pre-existing flakes (`test_browser_inspect_requests` / `test_cli_commands::test_version_flag`) that are environmental and not touched by this PR
- [x] `ruff check src/ tests/` — clean

## Compat-table corrections / spec drift notes

* The §11.2 spec example listed `("2captcha", "recaptcha-v2-checkbox"): {"http", "https", "socks4", "socks5"}`. Provider docs (April 2026) explicitly list only `http | socks4 | socks5` for `RecaptchaV2Task` / `HCaptchaTask` / `TurnstileTask` — `https` is NOT a documented value. The compat table reflects the documented set; setting `CAPTCHA_SOLVER_PROXY_TYPE=https` with a 2captcha provider falls back to proxyless + `solver_confidence="low"`.
* 2captcha has no documented proxy-aware `RecaptchaV3Task` as of April 2026 — only `RecaptchaV3TaskProxyless`. The task-type table has `"proxy_aware": None` for `recaptcha-v3` and `recaptcha-enterprise-v3` on 2captcha; the compat table omits those entries; loaders fall back to proxyless and downgrade confidence.
* FunCaptcha is mentioned in the §11.2 SOCKS5-rejection note but is deferred to §11.5; commented in `_SOLVER_PROXY_COMPAT` for when that lands.

## Files

- `src/browser/captcha.py` — `SolverProxyConfig`, `get_solver_proxy_config`, `_SOLVER_PROXY_COMPAT`, restructured task tables, refactored `_build_task_body` to return `(body, used_proxy_aware, compat_rejected)`, threaded proxy_config through `_solve_2captcha` / `_solve_capsolver` / `solve`.
- `src/browser/captcha_cost_counter.py` — added `PRICING_CENTS_PROXY_AWARE` table and `proxy_aware` kwarg on `estimate_cents`.
- `src/browser/service.py` — `_check_captcha` reads `solver.last_compat_rejected` to downgrade confidence; cost-counter call site reads `solver.last_used_proxy_aware` for tier selection.
- `tests/test_captcha_solver_proxy.py` (new) — 49 tests covering loader, normalizer, compat table, task-body builder, cost counter, and the credential-leak canary.
- `tests/test_captcha_recaptcha_classifier.py` — updated existing §11.1 task-table tests for the new `{proxyless, proxy_aware, extra}` schema.

author: garthdb
body:
## Summary

Closes #94. Final 1.2.0 sub-issue alongside #90 (cursor pagination), #91 (streaming), #92 (batch fetch), #93 (selective invalidation).

Adds a `CachePreloader` trait registered on `ThingsCache` via `set_preloader` / `clear_preloader`. After every `get_*` access the cache calls `predict(accessed_key)` to enqueue follow-up keys for warming; the warming-loop tick then calls `warm(key)` for each top-priority queued entry — replacing the previous no-op stub in `start_cache_warming`.

Ships a `DefaultPreloader` with three hardcoded heuristics over the existing top-level keys:

- `inbox:all` → `today:all` (priority 8)
- `today:all` → `inbox:all` (priority 10)
- `areas:all` → `projects:all` (priority 7)

Holds a `Weak<ThingsCache>` to break the otherwise circular `Arc<ThingsCache>` ↔ `Arc<dyn CachePreloader>` reference. If the cache is dropped, `warm` becomes a no-op.

## Notable design choices

- **Trait is sync** (matches the `CacheInvalidationHandler` convention from #93); implementors `tokio::spawn` async work themselves. Keeps trait dispatch dyn-compatible without `async-trait`.
- **`predict` fires on both hit and miss paths** of every `get_*` method — so the heuristic sees every access, not just fetches.
- **Warming queue is drained after dispatch** — `predict` re-adds keys on the next access if they remain hot. Prevents a full queue from blocking new entries.
- **Default behavior unchanged**: no preloader registered means `predict` and `warm` are never called; existing callers are unaffected.

## Stats

`CacheStats` gains `warmed_keys` and `warming_runs` counters so tests and operators can confirm the loop is doing work. Existing `CacheStats` constructor literals updated to `..Default::default()`.

## Out of scope

- **`project_tasks:<uuid>` cache key namespace** — the issue's literal example ("opening a project warms its task list") would need a new key namespace and a new `cache.get_project_tasks(uuid, fetcher)` method. Once `CachePreloader` lands, a `ProjectTasksPreloader` impl is a small follow-up. Filed as cleanup once this lands.
- **Wiring the cache into production paths** — CLI / MCP currently call `ThingsDatabase` directly, bypassing `ThingsCache`. Preloading is observable via `get_stats()` and tests but won't preload real user fetches until a separate cache-wrapping change happens.

## Test plan

- [x] 7 new unit tests in `cache::tests` covering: predict rule table, predict firing on hit + miss, warming queue population, no-preloader noop, warming loop dispatching `warm`, `clear_preloader` disabling predict, and `Weak` cycle protection.
- [x] 1 full integration test (`test_default_preloader_warms_via_db`) that builds a real test DB, registers `DefaultPreloader`, fetches `inbox:all`, sleeps past the warming interval, then asserts `today:all` is served from cache (panicking fetcher would fire if not warmed).
- [x] `cargo test -p things3-core --features full --lib` — 579 passed
- [x] `cargo test --workspace` — full workspace passes
- [x] `cargo clippy -p things3-core --lib -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo clippy -p things3-core --lib --features full -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` — clean

author: jpwinans
body:
## Summary
- Add `filed_at_ts` (Unix epoch float) at all 9 drawer/closet/diary write sites, paired with the existing `filed_at` ISO string
- New `mempalace.backfill_filed_at_ts` module: direct-SQL backfill for existing palaces (bypasses HNSW per the global ChromaDB safety contract)
- 12 new tests covering ISO parsing, end-to-end backfill, dry-run, idempotency, cursor pagination

## Why

Companion to vestige#78. Vestige's NREM dream cycle needs a server-side date filter:

```python
{"filed_at_ts": {"$gte": cutoff_epoch}}
```

Chroma `$gte` is strictly numeric; `filed_at` is an ISO string, so the filter raises `ValueError` every cycle and falls back to a client-side scan over all 90K+ drawers. Adding the numeric sibling field makes the filter usable.

## Write-side changes

Every place that writes a `filed_at` ISO string now also writes a `filed_at_ts` epoch float, derived from the same `datetime.now()` call so they refer to the same instant:

- `mempalace/miner.py`: drawer + closet metadata (lines 542, 663)
- `mempalace/convo_miner.py`: registry sentinel + chunk drawers (lines 73, 339)
- `mempalace/closet_llm.py`: LLM-generated closet (line 285)
- `mempalace/diary_ingest.py`: diary drawer + closet (lines 130, 144, 174 — shared `_now`)
- `mempalace/mcp_server.py`: `file_drawer` + `diary_write` (lines 642, 939)

## Backfill

New `mempalace/backfill_filed_at_ts.py` module, runnable as `python -m mempalace.backfill_filed_at_ts`:

```
$ python -m mempalace.backfill_filed_at_ts --dry-run
[backfill] palace=/Users/.../palace rows_needing_backfill=96260 batch_size=5000 dry_run=True
[backfill] progress scanned=5000 inserted=5000 unparseable=0
...
[backfill] done scanned=96260 inserted=96260 unparseable=0 skipped=0 dry_run=True
```

Mechanism: opens `chroma.sqlite3` directly, reads rows where `key='filed_at'` AND no `filed_at_ts` exists, parses each ISO string to epoch, INSERTs sibling rows with `key='filed_at_ts'` and `float_value`. **No `col.update()` call** — uses SQL only, bypasses HNSW entirely. Per CLAUDE.md ChromaDB safety: this is the explicit safe path for metadata mutation at scale.

Cursor-paginated by `id` (not OFFSET, which would break under the self-modifying WHERE clause once batches commit). Idempotent: rows that already have `filed_at_ts` are skipped.

## Tests

12 unit tests in `tests/test_backfill_filed_at_ts.py`:
- ISO parsing: tz-bearing, Zulu suffix, naive, unparseable, empty, non-string
- End-to-end backfill: 3-row synthetic palace, results validated by re-reading
- Dry-run: writes nothing, counts correctly
- Idempotent: pre-seeded `filed_at_ts` rows preserved
- Unparseable: counted separately, doesn't abort
- Missing db: raises FileNotFoundError
- Cursor pagination correctness: 25 rows × batch_size=10

All pass. Validated dry-run on prod palace: 96260/96260 parseable.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/test_backfill_filed_at_ts.py` — 12/12 pass
- [x] `python -m mempalace.backfill_filed_at_ts --dry-run` on prod palace
- [ ] After merge: run actual backfill on prod palace (with James's approval)
- [ ] After backfill: vestige `_iter_recent_drawers` migrated to `filed_at_ts` query (separate vestige PR)

Companion to vestige#78

author: kropiunig
body:
## Summary
Fix the 'View on Safe' link so it navigates to the Safe transaction details page instead of redirecting to Safe's welcome page.

## Root cause
`getSafeWebUrl` in `libs/core/src/gnosisSafe/index.ts` was constructing the URL using a path-style safe identifier:

```
https://app.safe.global/<chainShortName>:<safeAddress>/transactions/tx?id=multisig_<safeAddress>_<safeTxHash>
```

Safe's web app does not recognize this nested-route format for transaction details and silently redirects to `/welcome/accounts`. The transaction URL requires the safe identifier as a `safe=` **query parameter**, not as a path segment:

```
https://app.safe.global/transactions/tx?safe=<chainShortName>:<safeAddress>&id=multisig_<safeAddress>_<safeTxHash>
```

This format is consistent with what Safe themselves use in [`safe-cli-nodejs`](https://github.com/safe-global/safe-cli-nodejs) and what other Safe-integrated apps (e.g. ShapeShift) use.

## Changes
- `libs/core/src/gnosisSafe/index.ts`: rewrite `getSafeWebUrl` to use the query-param format.
- `libs/core/src/gnosisSafe/index.test.ts`: add unit test asserting the URL format.

`getSafeAccountUrl` is intentionally left as path-style — that route (the safe overview) does work with the path format.

## Test plan
- [ ] Place a TWAP order while connected to a Safe wallet
- [ ] Click 'View on Safe' on the order popup
- [ ] Verify the link opens the transaction details page in Safe (not the welcome page)

Fixes #6898

author: mrrayg
body:
## What
Three coordinated additions to **`server/replyEngine.ts`**, all inside the existing `generateReply()` function (single file, single function, no caller-side changes):

1. **`buildVoiceBlock()` injection** in the system prompt at `server/replyEngine.ts:183` — brings `SOURCING_GROUNDING_RULE` into the reply path for the first time.
2. **Citation discipline block** at `server/replyEngine.ts:185-191` — five APA-style per-claim bullets, reply-tailored. The last bullet directly counters the "Be the expert" framing's failure mode.
3. **`verifyClaims` post-write wiring** at `server/replyEngine.ts:259-282` — mirrors `server/signalBriefEngine.ts:295-330`. Verify → on `HARD_FAIL` log + drop + return null, no revise loop.

Single file changed: **`server/replyEngine.ts`** (+39 / −1).

## Why
The parity audit (`engine_citation_parity.md`, Tier 3) flagged `replyEngine.ts` as the **largest structural gap** in the entire content-engine fleet — three separate things missing simultaneously:
- No `buildVoiceBlock` import → no `SOURCING_GROUNDING_RULE` → no Lane A/B framing in the prompt.
- No per-claim citation discipline language.
- No `verifyClaims` post-write check.

The specific risk surface: replies on AI/tech topics are explicitly told *"share your actual perspective — you have 70 years of AI history to draw from. Be the expert."* (`server/replyEngine.ts:221`). That framing is exactly the surface that produces unsourced bare-stat replies — Agent 306 reaching into KB / training memory and asserting it confidently with no attribution. Across the recent verifier-failure pattern, replies were the only generation surface with no backstop.

## Pattern sources
- **Verifier wiring** — `server/signalBriefEngine.ts:295-330` (canonical: verify → on `HARD_FAIL` log + drop + return null, no revise loop) and **PR #234** (https://github.com/MrRayG/agent306-dashboard/pull/234) for dispatch-handler shape.
- **Citation block** — **PR #235** (https://github.com/MrRayG/agent306-dashboard/pull/235) — the comparator at `server/articleEngine.ts:311-317`.
- **Companion rollouts** — **PR #236** (https://github.com/MrRayG/agent306-dashboard/pull/236, parity rollout — replyEngine intentionally excluded because of the verifier+voice gaps) and **PR #237** (https://github.com/MrRayG/agent306-dashboard/pull/237, dispatchEngine companion). PR-D3 closes the last content-engine gap in this series.

## Discipline framework
- APA in-text citations — Purdue OWL: https://owl.purdue.edu/owl/research_and_citation/apa_style/apa_formatting_and_style_guide/in_text_citations_the_basics.html
- Stanford paper-writing guide — Widom: https://cs.stanford.edu/people/widom/paper-writing.html

## Wiring details

### Imports (line 19-20)
```ts
import { buildVoiceBlock } from \"./voice.js\";
import { verifyClaims } from \"./claimVerifier.js\";
```
Both paths confirmed against signalBriefEngine.ts (`./voice.js`) and PR #237's dispatchEngine wiring (`./claimVerifier.js`). Spec text mentioned `./voiceInstructions.js` as a candidate path but the canonical import across all peer engines is `./voice.js`; followed the spec's instruction to "confirm exact path matches what signalBriefEngine.ts imports."

### Voice block + citation block insertion (system prompt, lines 181-191)
Inserted between `\${agentCtx}` and the `\"You are Agent 306 — Sovereign AI Thought Leader\"` reply-format header. Position chosen so the discipline reads as foundational voice rather than as a reply-specific constraint.

### Verifier source set
The parent tweet (`opts.text`) plus any pre-fetched x_search research context (already in `opts.researchContext` for AI/tech replies) are joined as the source set:
```ts
const upstreamSourceText = [
  `Parent tweet from @\${opts.username}:\n\${opts.text}`,
  opts.researchContext ? `Research context (x_search):\n\${opts.researchContext}` : \"\",
].filter(Boolean).join(\"\n\n\");
const verdict = await verifyClaims({
  draftText:   cleaned,
  sourceText:  upstreamSourceText,
  sourceUrl:   opts.tweetUrl ?? \"\",
  sourceTitle: `Reply to @\${opts.username}`,
});
```

### `HARD_FAIL` handling
Same shape as signalBriefEngine.ts:307-312, so the dashboard log filters work unchanged:
```ts
console.error(`[ClaimVerifier] REJECTED reply to @\${opts.username}: \${verdict.unsupportedClaims.length} unsupported claims`);
for (const c of verdict.unsupportedClaims) {
  console.error(`  - \${c.reason}: \${c.sentence.slice(0, 180)}`);
}
return null;
```
The function already returns `string | null`; existing call sites (`runMidnightReplies` at line ~388, `runFarcasterReplies` at line ~528) already treat `null` as \"no reply produced\" (`if (!generated) { ... continue; }`). No caller-side change needed — verifier rejection is functionally indistinguishable from any other generation failure to the loop.

### Insertion point (post-generation, pre-side-effect)
The verifier sits AFTER the LLM response is parsed and the signature is enforced, but BEFORE `generateReply` returns. This is upstream of the quality gate, validateXPost, and the actual `xWrite.v2.tweet(...)` call. A rejected reply never reaches the X API, never records to conversation memory, and never increments `state.totalRepliesSent`.

### Fail-closed-on-judge-outage
Preserved automatically — `verifyClaims` itself raises severity to `HARD_FAIL` when the judge LLM is unavailable (`server/__tests__/claimVerifier.judgeOutage.test.ts`).

## Reply-length / verifier-sensitivity concern (flag for monitoring)

Replies are short (often 1-3 sentences). The verifier's claim-extraction logic in `server/claimVerifier.ts` was designed against longer-form content (briefs, articles, blogs). A grep for min-length guards (`draftText.length`, `min`, `MIN_`, `minSentences`, `too short`) in `server/claimVerifier.ts` returns **zero hits** — there is no length-based bypass. Per spec, this PR does **not** add one.

**Possible follow-up if monitoring reveals over-rejection on short replies:**
- The verifier may be aggressive on a 2-sentence reply where one sentence makes a single statistical claim ("inference cost dropped 99%") and the parent tweet doesn't establish that fact. Under the new prompt the model should hedge ("inference costs reportedly dropped ~99%") which the verifier accepts as Lane B; if it doesn't hedge, the verifier rejects — which is the intended behavior, but at low-source-context surfaces like replies it may produce more drops than dispatch/article paths.
- If post-merge logs show `[ClaimVerifier] REJECTED reply` firing at >5% rate without obvious bare-stat issues, candidate fix is a reply-length-aware threshold in claimVerifier.ts (separate PR — out of scope here).

## Risk
Low. Same battle-tested pattern as five other engines that already verify post-write. Caller sites already handle `null` returns from `generateReply` as a no-op (existing flow path). Worst case: one extra round-trip per reply on a hard-fail (matches signalBrief / dispatch behavior). Pure additions; no removals; no contract changes.

## Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit` is **clean** on this branch (matches `origin/main` baseline — also clean).
- `git diff --stat origin/main` → exactly **1 file changed: `server/replyEngine.ts`** (+39 / −1).
- `grep \"buildVoiceBlock\\|verifyClaims\" server/replyEngine.ts` confirms both imports + both call sites.
- No CI configured on this repo (per prior PR observations).

## Out of scope (handled separately)
- **PR-E** *(future, noted in PR #235)* — KB URL surfacing in `contextWindow.ts` formatters at lines 179, 195, 206, 362. Once it lands, every engine's \"verbal hedge\" bullet (including this PR's) can be tightened from \"hedge verbally\" to \"cite the KB-provided URL.\"
- **PR-F** *(future)* — verifier \"supported elsewhere\" lane for sibling-source attribution.
- Reply-length-aware verifier threshold (only if post-merge monitoring shows over-rejection — see concern note above).

This PR closes the last content-engine gap from the parity audit. After PR #236, P

author: maleadt
body:
The bytecode encoder previously emitted a fresh ConstantOp for every literal, even when the same (type, bytes) was already materialised in the kernel. The translator CSEs them in its bytecode optimiser, but the duplication still bloats the bytecode payload and type table.

Add a per-CGCtx (TypeId, Vector{UInt8}) -> Value cache, populated by the new get_or_emit_constant! helper that wraps encode_ConstantOp!. The cache is region-scoped via with_region_constant_scope! around If/For/Loop/While body callbacks: with_region rewinds next_value_id on exit, so any Value created inside is ephemeral and must not be reachable from the parent's cache.

Not convinced we want this. It does make the generated bitcode a bit cleaner, but doesn't have a performance impact.

author: seanmhanson
body:
This documents a workflow for copilot usage from plan approval, version control handling, execution, agent self-review, and preparing for copilot and manual review. As included are notes on the manual review process I recommend and follow in tandem with this flow.

##  Workflow Outline

### Pre-Workflow
- user uses the ask agent or other resources as needed for planning
- user uses the planning agent to draft and revise a plan until ready for execution

### Trigger
- the user approves a plan, to begin execution of the plan

### Workflow - Pre-Execution/Execution
- the agent opens a new feature branch from the most recent version of main
- the agent executes the workflow:
  - on failure, the agent reports failure, preserves changes and shows them in `git status`, and preserves the branch for manual intervention
- the agent commits the initial changeset from the execution of the plan and pushes to the branch

### Workflow - Agent & Copilot Review
- the agent reviews the changeset independently of the goal-centric teleology of the execution and planning actions
- the agent commits the agent review changes and pushes to the branch
- the agent assigns me to the MR and tries to assign Copilot as a reviewer
  - on silent failure, the user will need to manually see this and update it
  - on other failures, the agent will not assign a reviewer and will report this to the user
 
 ## Manual Actions (By Personal Preference)
  - the copilot review is not automated; manual review will accompany Copilot feedback
  - after reading and prioritizing, provide the review to the agent to evaluate both as feedback and in terms of the plan and feature goals (to reduce drift)
  - repeat copilot review whenever finished adding new sets of commits

### Manual Review Areas
The manual review I use in association with this workflow maintains a two-prong approach with the goal of shrinking the amount of manual review feedback by addressing each of the two concerns.

#### Big Bucket concerns
- overall accuracy, global concerns, regressions, human-recognizable concerns, relationship to other codebases, business logic,
- effectively targeted by improving input quality, plan, and research/data upfront

#### Small Bucket concerns
  - style, consistent patterns, test methodologies, prioritization of smaller decisions, clarity, legibility
  - effectively targeted by improving agent instructions, by way of manual review feedback

## Summary

v0.5.7 typography tokens patch. Closes 4 library gaps surfaced by scout-hub `O1.1 /pl/login` refactor (PARTIAL @ 8.77 weighted, atelier-absent rubric). Library-wide WCAG 2.2 AA brand-fill text audit expanded scope to 6 components.

**Per OS quality > speed mandate:** library v0.5.7 ships first, then scout-hub bumps consumer + reattacks O1.1 on its parked branch for clean ≥9.0 PASS — single scout-hub PR with full evidence.

## What changed

### Added
- **`Text variant="eyebrow"`** — inline-light atelier eyebrow path. Same uppercase / 0.7rem / 0.08em-tracked / tabular-nums / medium-weight vocabulary as the standalone `Eyebrow` atom but WITHOUT the numeric prefix + hairline ornament. Single source of truth via shared `mx.eyebrow-typography` mixin in `_mixins.scss`. `TextVariant` union 5 → 6.
- **`Heading size="hero-editorial" | "form-card-title" | "form-card-subtitle"`** — three editorial-tier sizes. `hero-editorial` clamp 36→52px (login asides) sits between `display-md` (48px ceiling) and `display` (72px ceiling); `form-card-title` 22px fixed (between Heading lg + xl); `form-card-subtitle` 15px fixed (between Text small + base). Three new `--font-size-{hero-editorial,form-card-title,form-card-subtitle}` semantic tokens. `HeadingSize` union 10 → 13.

### Fixed
- **WCAG 2.2 AA contrast for text on brand fills (light mode)** — primary `Button` text in light theme used `--color-text-inverse` which resolves to `white`. White on mid-tone brand seeds (e.g. teal `#14B8A6`) yields ~2.49:1 — FAILS WCAG 2.2 AA. Introduced dedicated `--color-text-on-brand` semantic token (default `#25292E` near-black; ~5.88:1 on teal — PASS AA body + AA UI). **Library-wide audit migrated 6 components together**: Button.variantPrimary, Calendar.cellButtonSelected, Carousel (.indicator:hover + .pauseButton:hover + [aria-pressed='true']), Tabs pill .trigger[data-state='active'], Toggle.pressed, TableRow.selected (3-token cascade). Badge.colorBrand + IconBox.variantBrand correctly excluded — they use tinted-bg pattern (--color-brand-subtle bg + --color-brand-strong text), not brand-fill text rendering. **Visible change in light theme** across these 6 surfaces (white → near-black on teal). **Dark theme unchanged** (both old `neutral-950` value of `--color-text-inverse` and new `--color-text-on-brand: #25292E` are near-black).

### Compatibility
- Public API: Text + Heading union widening is backward-compatible (TS supertype). Existing prop usages render byte-equivalent.
- Eyebrow component renders byte-equivalent post DRY refactor (mixin expands to identical CSS).
- Component count unchanged at 91. Demo routes unchanged at 55 (52 `/components/*` + root + `_not-found` + `/demo`).
- Migration note for consumers with project-local `--color-on-brand`: library now ships canonical `--color-text-on-brand` semantic; consumers can remove their local override block.

## Audit evidence — Phase 7.1 Critical Consistency Audit

3-iteration converge:
- **Iter 1 FAIL** (1 CRITICAL + 6 IMPORTANT) — caught E03's incomplete brand-fill audit (claimed only Button primary; expanded to 6 components library-wide). Plus README size description / route count drift / Text.tsx JSDoc gaps / CLAUDE.md size-klas count.
- **Iter 2 FAIL** (1 CRITICAL + 5 IMPORTANT) — caught FFG-split-retry pattern (CHANGELOG L19+L25 mis-labeled Tabs fix as 'segmented' when actual was 'pill') + work-unit-level docs not swept by Iter 1.
- **Iter 3 PASS** — 0 CRITICAL + 0 IMPORTANT + 5 NITPICK acknowledged. All Iter 2 findings verified RESOLVED. No regressions introduced by cascade edits.

Reports: `internal/bleizlabs-ui/work/2026-04_v0-5-7-typography-tokens/phase-71-audit-iter-{1,2,3}.md`.

## Test plan

- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `npm run lint` clean (incidentally fixed pre-existing v0.5.6 drift in `app/components/grid-layout/page.tsx` — 4 react/no-unescaped-entities errors)
- [x] `node playground/build.mjs` sass build clean (`compiled.css` 17.24 KB → 17.50 KB; additive only)
- [x] `npm run build` clean (55 routes prerendered, ~2.7-2.9s)
- [x] WCAG contrast math-verified: `#25292E` on teal `#14B8A6` = 5.88:1 (PASS AA body 4.5:1 + AA UI 3:1)
- [x] Phase 7.1 Critical Consistency Audit converged at Iter 3 PASS
- [ ] Live Playwright visual regression — DEFERRED to v0.5.8 sprint (algebra suffices for token-level fix)

## Commits (range `2f4765e..afd35f6`, 6 commits)

- `51680e8` chore: fix react/no-unescaped-entities in grid-layout demo (v0.5.6 drift)
- `d8ace7a` feat(E01): add Text variant="eyebrow" + share mx.eyebrow-typography mixin
- `7f492b3` feat(E02): add Heading editorial scale (hero-editorial + form-card-title + form-card-subtitle)
- `9a1c904` feat(E03): add --color-text-on-brand semantic token (WCAG 2.2 AA fix)
- `4578820` fix(E04): phase-7.1 audit iter-1 fixes — library-wide brand-fill audit + count drift
- `afd35f6` fix(E04): phase-7.1 audit iter-2 fix — CHANGELOG Tabs variant attribution

## Origin

scout-hub `O1.1 /pl/login` refactor (parked branch `work/refactor-pl-login` at scout-hub/`bfe5305`). Library gaps documented in `internal/scout-hub/dev/LOG/refactor/login/audit-round-5.md`. v0.5.7 unblocks scout-hub re-attack for clean ≥9.0 PASS in a follow-up scout-hub PR.

### Motivation
- Add support for users to upload manual payment receipts for manual payment providers and to check payment status from the user UI.
- Prevent manual confirmation without an attached receipt and provide admins with the uploaded receipt for verification.
- Improve user experience by adding explicit "payment status" buttons across invoice/payment UIs.

### Description
- Added new UI builders in `app/user_ui.py`: `build_user_manual_receipt_keyboard`, `build_user_manual_receipt_request_text`, `build_user_manual_receipt_uploaded_text`, and `build_user_payment_status_*` helpers and added "📊 Статус оплаты" buttons to invoice/payment keyboards.
- Implemented receipt upload and validation in `bot.py`: new allowed mime/extension sets `RECEIPT_ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES`/`RECEIPT_ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS`, helper validators `_receipt_extension` and `_is_supported_receipt_document`, and intent lookup `_find_latest_payment_intent_for_invoice`.
- Added handlers: `handle_user_upload_receipt_callback` to start upload flow, `handle_user_payment_status_callback` to show status, and `handle_user_payment_receipt_message` to accept photo/document messages, validate them, store confirmation payload via `payment_service.save_manual_confirmation_payload`, and notify admins with the receipt as photo or document.
- Enforced receipt requirement: when calling manual confirmation (`user_manual_paid`), the code now checks `confirmation_payload_json.receipt_uploaded` and redirects users to upload a receipt if missing, and admins cannot confirm manual payments without a receipt.
- Updated admin notification flow to include the uploaded receipt and use `_admin_manual_payment_keyboard` for approve/reject actions.

### Testing
- Ran the project's unit test suite and linters (where present); all tests and checks completed successfully.
- Performed automated handler invocation checks during development (no failing automated tests observed).

body:
## Summary

- `@sentry/nextjs` v10 OpenTelemetry integration uses `require-in-the-middle` to monkey-patch Node modules at startup
- Turbopack hashes the module name to `require-in-the-middle-<hash>` at compile time but cannot resolve it at runtime
- This crashes the instrumentation hook on every `pnpm dev` start with `Failed to load external module require-in-the-middle-2ca7b9c2766f317e`

Fix: add `skipOpenTelemetrySetup: process.env.NODE_ENV === "development"` to `sentry.server.config.ts`. In dev, Sentry skips OTel module patching while keeping error capture. In production, Webpack builds load OTel normally with `skipOpenTelemetrySetup: false`.

## Test plan

- [x] Run `pnpm dev` in WSL — confirm no `require-in-the-middle` error
- [x] Confirm `Ready` without instrumentation hook crash
- [x] Production build (`pnpm build`) unaffected — `NODE_ENV === "production"` means OTel runs normally

### Motivation

- Restore and rework KSeF API sync pipeline (v2.x) by introducing modular services for authentication, export and incremental sync with HWM and environment separation.

- Add design/implementation plan documentation to guide staged rollout and review.

### Description

- Added a new implementation plan document `docs/KSEF_API_INTEGRATION_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_2026-04-25.md` describing the to-be architecture and staged rollout.

author: 0x3k
body:
## Summary

Replace the flat virtualized list of 30k+ events with a collapsible list grouped by route. Each route shows a one-line summary (name, time range, total event count, per-type chips) and expands on click to show its events.

- **New endpoint** \`GET /v1/devices/:dongle/event-routes\` returns one row per route that has at least one event matching the active type/severity filter. Each row carries \`event_count\`, \`type_counts\` breakdown, and the most-recent matching event timestamp. **Routes with zero matching events are filtered out server-side**, so the user never sees empty rows.
- **\`ListEventsByDongleID\` gains a \`route_name\` filter** so the expanded row can lazy-fetch a single route's events on demand. Capped at 100 events per expansion; the route page handles the long tail.
- **Moments page UI** is now a list of route cards with collapsed-by-default rows. Click expands and shows the events list (severity, type, offset, payload summary, when). Each event still links into the route player at the right offset.

Pagination is now route-level (10/25/50/100 routes per page). Multi-type filters fan out one request per type and merge client-side, mirroring the previous flat-list behaviour.

## Test plan

- [x] \`go vet ./...\`, \`go test ./internal/api/... ./internal/worker/...\`
- [x] \`pnpm --dir web type-check\`, \`pnpm --dir web lint\`
- [ ] After deploy: \`/moments\` shows the 26 routes that have events, with \`alert_warning\` heavy and \`disengage\` sparse. Filter chips narrow the route list correctly. Expanding a route lazy-fetches its events.

author: steelbrain
body:
Cameras occasionally return a different Session ID on audio SETUP than was issued on video SETUP. Previously the default policy threw, with `.useFirst` available as an opt-in escape hatch. Neither covered the case where the camera only honors the latest ID at PLAY time, so users hit dead-ends without a clear remedy.

The new behavior unconditionally adopts whatever ID the latest SETUP returned. This matches what most of the ecosystem already does silently — GStreamer rtspsrc, Live555 (and VLC via Live555), gortsplib/MediaMTX, and ExoPlayer all overwrite on every response. FFmpeg is the lone "use first" outlier, and retina (the Rust project IPCamKit was ported from) is the only library that exposes a policy enum at all.

Removes the public `SessionIdPolicy` type and the
`sessionIdPolicy:` parameter from `RTSPClientSession.init`; breaking change, ships in 0.2.0.

> **🔄 Rebased onto post-refactor patterns (config-refs (env var read sites))**
> This PR has been rebased to use the per-thing file layout established by refactor PRs #116/#117/#118/#119. Behavior shipped is identical to the original; only the internal code shape changed.

> **What this PR now ships:**

> - **`src/db/migrations/006-config-refs.ts`** — `config_refs` table
> - **`src/config-refs/index.ts`** — pure regex extractor

> - `src/index-hooks/registry.ts`, `src/db/migrations/index.ts`, `src/mcp/tools/registry.ts`, `src/mcp/tools/types.ts` — registry entries

>
> **What you'll see in the diff:** until #116-#119 land, the diff against `main` includes the refactor commits as part of the branch history. After they merge, GitHub auto-shrinks this PR's diff to just the files above. Full context: #120.
>
> ---

## Summary

Extracts environment-variable read sites (`process.env.X`, `os.getenv("X")`, `os.environ`, `os.Getenv`, `System.getenv`, `ENV[...]`, `env!`, `std::env::var`) into a new `config_refs` table. Surfaces via a new `codegraph_config` MCP tool to answer "what reads `OBSIDIAN_PORT`?" and "what config does this codebase read?" without grep noise.

**Why a separate table, not graph nodes/edges** — env vars are a global namespace with no single source-of-truth file. Giving them a synthetic `file_path` would pollute the main graph. Treating them like `symbol_issues` (a side-table queried via a dedicated tool) keeps the core graph clean.

## Empirical signal on `mcp-obsidian-extended` (the spike target)

Indexing that repo with this PR's build reproduces the spike numbers exactly:

| Key | Reads |
|---|---:|
| `TOOL_PRESET` | 8 |
| `OBSIDIAN_PORT` | 8 |
| `OBSIDIAN_SCHEME` | 7 |
| `INCLUDE_TOOLS` | 7 |
| `TOOL_MODE` | 6 |
| `OBSIDIAN_CONFIG` | 5 |
| `OBSIDIAN_DEBUG` | 4 |

These are the central knobs an agent should know about when editing the codebase. Codegraph itself is sparse (4 reads) because it's a CLI with file-based config — this feature shines on service-style codebases.

## What's added

- **`src/config-refs/index.ts`** — per-language regex catalogue (TS/JS, Python, Go, Java/Kotlin, Ruby, Rust). Upper-case-only key filter avoids `process.env.foo` (a Node variable) and dynamic accesses. Cheap line-level pre-filter (`includes('env'|'Env'|'ENV')`) skips 99% of irrelevant lines.
- **Migration v4** — new `config_refs` table with FK cascade. Defensive `ensureConfigRefsTable()` at every persistence path covers the migration-collision case with #112 and #113.
- **`runConfigRefsPass`** — full rescan after `indexAll`; incremental on `sync` with delete-then-reinsert per file (so a file edited to remove its last env read drops its row). Per-pass enclosing-function resolver cache avoids O(reads × symbols) scans.
- **`codegraph_config` MCP tool** — no-arg form lists top-N keys with read counts; `key` form lists all read sites with enclosing function.
- **Config flag**: `enableConfigRefs` (default true).

## Tests

399 pass total, **19 new**:

- Parser per-language (7): TS, JS, Python, Go, Java/Kotlin, Ruby, Rust
- Parser correctness (5): upper-case-only filter, unsupported lang skip, 1-indexed line numbers, resolveEnclosing closure threading, missing file
- End-to-end (7): basic + enclosing function, reverse view, `enableConfigRefs:false`, incremental sync replace, **regression for empty-rows data-corruption bug** (file edited to remove its last env read), deletion sweep, **v4-collision defense** (drop table after init)

## Reviewer pass

## Summary

- New top-level **Region** settings page (replaces the Units page) with three subheads: **Language**, **Temperature unit**, **Distance unit**.
- Adds a `Region` enum to `:core:domain` (SYSTEM / en-US / en-GB / en-AU). Defaults to SYSTEM — i.e. follow the phone's locale.

💡 What: Refactored `OrdersHistory.tsx` to memoize the filtering logic and aggregate status statistics in a single pass instead of multiple passes on every render.

## Summary
This update refines the signaling finite state machine (FSM) transitions for call setup and enhances the media controller's screen sharing functionality. It also includes minor test improvements and formatting adjustments.

## Context and Motivation
The changes address inconsistencies in the signaling FSM's state transitions, particularly when entering the "CALLER_WAITING" state, ensuring more accurate state management during call setup. Additionally, the media controller's screen sharing method was updated to explicitly specify video and audio constraints, improving reliability. These updates improve the robustness and correctness of the call handling logic.

## Main Changes
- Updated signaling FSM to transition from "CALLER_WAITING" to "NEGOTIATING" on "enter" event with appropriate effects.
- Adjusted signaling FSM test cases to validate new transition logic and expected states.
- Modified MediaController's startScreenShare method to explicitly request video and audio in getDisplayMedia.
- Minor formatting improvements in test files and code for consistency.

## Technical Details
- The FSM now uses a "SETUP_PC" effect with role "caller" instead of "ROLLBACK_AND_RESTART_ICE" when transitioning from "CALLER_WAITING" to "NEGOTIATING".
- Tests were updated to reflect the new expected states and transitions, ensuring coverage of the new logic.

## How to Test

- Test screen sharing functionality to confirm video and audio streams are correctly obtained.
- Verify that call notices trigger appropriate toast messages and clear notices as expected.
