author: derekg1729
body:
## TLDR

PR-A v2: full image-tag fix included. Adopting GitHub Merge Queue on `main` to anchor preview-environment content to the merged tree.

Defeats the bug class observed in PR #924 and PR #1033 (squash-merge re-tag of pre-rebase image content shipped to preview, even though `main`'s git tree was correct).

## Why merge queue, why now

- **Bug class observed twice.** The merge queue's only meaningful purpose in our pipeline is making the pr-build → flight-preview re-tag chain sound by ensuring `pr-{N}-{X}` content matches the merged tree.
- **Lighter alternatives evaluated and rejected**:
  - `Require branches to be up-to-date` → rebase-thrash hostile to external contributors.
  - Operator-driven rebase via `core__vcs_*` → puts an LLM in the merge path. Conflicts with "deterministic tools, not ad-hoc agentic ops."
- **GH Merge Queue is the deterministic vendor primitive.** GitLab Merge Trains is the equivalent — vendor-portable.

## The structural fix

The merge queue alone doesn't solve the bug. `flight-preview.yml` re-tags `pr-{N}-{X}` → `preview-{mainSHA}` from images built at PR head SHA. With the queue rebasing PR-B's tree to Y but `pr-build` only firing on `pull_request`, no one rebuilds the image, so the same stale-content gets re-tagged for preview.

This PR makes `pr-build.yml` fire on `merge_group` events too. On those events:

1. Resolve PR number from `merge_group.head_ref` (format: `gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-{N}-{X}-{salt}`).
2. Look up the full PR head SHA via `gh api pulls/{N}.head.sha` (head_ref's SHA portion may be abbreviated; full SHA needed to keep tag format consistent with pull_request builds).
3. Check out the queue commit (Y); build the rebased tree.
4. Push under the same `pr-{N}-{X}` tag — overwriting the pre-rebase image.

`flight-preview.yml`'s existing resolver (line 135) still calls `gh api pulls/{N} → head.sha` and gets X. Re-tagging `pr-{N}-{X}` → `preview-{mainSHA}` now sources rebased content. **No change to flight-preview.**

`manifest` is added to the required-status set. Without it, the queue could squash-merge before pr-build(merge_group) overwrites the tag, recreating the bug.

## Changes

- **`.github/workflows/ci.yaml`**: `merge_group:` trigger added.
- **`.github/workflows/pr-build.yml`**: `merge_group:` trigger added with a new `resolve` job. Downstream `detect`/`build`/`manifest` jobs read `needs.resolve.outputs.*` instead of `github.event.pull_request.*` directly. Concurrency keys split by event type.
- **`infra/github/branch-protection.json`**: required-status set: `CodeQL, Validate PR title, static, unit, component, stack-test, manifest`. Strengthens today's set (adds `static` and `manifest`).
- **`infra/github/merge-queue.json`**: queue config (squash, ALLGREEN grouping, depth caps tuned for ~1-2 PR/day cadence).
- **`infra/github/README.md`**: apply procedure, drift detection.
- **`docs/spec/agentic-contribution-loop.md`**: Step 8 (Request merge) + image-tag mechanism + `MERGE_QUEUE_DETERMINISM` / `NO_AGENTIC_REBASE` invariants.
- **`work/items/task.0389.enable-merge-queue.md`**: full design rationale + serialization analysis with `promote-and-deploy`.

## Deployment impact

**None on this PR**. `merge_group:` events only fire once the queue is enabled (PR-B). Until then both new triggers are dormant.

## Serialization analysis

| Race | Outcome | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Two queued PRs merge sequentially | Different `N` → different tags → no collision | None needed |
| Author force-pushes while enqueued | Queue evicts on push (GH built-in) | Existing |
| Queue rejects on rebased tree | Orphan `pr-{N}-{X}` v2 with rejected content; PR returns to review; next push or re-enqueue overwrites | Acceptable |
| flight-preview reads `pr-{N}-{X}` before pr-build(merge_group) finishes | **Bug recreated** | `manifest` is required-on-merge_group → queue can't squash-merge until image is up |
| Direct push to main (incident path) | flight-preview's existing logic exits cleanly (L118–127) | Existing |

`flight-preview.yml`'s concurrency group `flight-preview` and `flight-preview.sh`'s three-value lease (`unlocked → dispatching → reviewing`) serialize `promote-and-deploy` runs against `deploy/preview-*`. Path A doesn't change this.

`candidate-flight.yml` uses `pr-{N}-{X}` tags but resolves to digests at flight time (via `resolve-pr-build-images.sh`), then deploys digests. Post-flight tag overwrites don't affect already-flighted candidate-a deploys.

## Manual steps (PR-B, after this lands)

```bash
# 1. Enable repo-level auto-merge (UI: Settings → General → Pull Requests → "Allow auto-merge").

# 2. Apply branch protection.
jq 'del(._comment)' infra/github/branch-protection.json \
  | gh api -X PUT repos/Cogni-DAO/node-template/branches/main/protection --input -

# 3. Enable merge queue (UI: Settings → Branches → main → "Require merge queue", form values from infra/github/merge-queue.json).

# 4. Verify.
gh api repos/Cogni-DAO/node-template/branches/main/protection | jq '.required_status_checks.contexts'
# expected: ["CodeQL","Validate PR title","static","unit","component","stack-test","manifest"]
```

## Out of scope (sequenced follow-ups)

- **PR-C (adapter swap)**: `core__vcs_merge_pr` → GraphQL `enablePullRequestAutoMerge`. Required because direct REST merge returns 405 once queue is enabled. Separate PR because it changes pr-manager graph's expected return shape.
- **`deploy_verified` as a required check**: `validate-candidate` skill currently outputs Markdown, not a check-run. Promoting to a gate requires the GH App to run the skill itself.
- **Branch-protection reconciler workflow**: would require granting cogni-git-review GH App `administration:write`. Defer until drift recurs.

## E2E validation plan

- exercise: after PR-B lands, open a no-op docs PR. Click "Merge when ready". Confirm GH enqueues. Watch CI: `pr-build(merge_group)` should rebuild and push `pr-{N}-{X}`. Then queue squash-merges. flight-preview triggers, re-tags to `preview-{Z}`. Manually verify the image digest under `pr-{N}-{X}` differs between pr-build(pull_request) and pr-build(merge_group) runs (rebased tree should produce a distinct digest).
- second exercise: open two PRs simultaneously, queue both. Confirm second waits, rebases on top of first's merge, re-runs gates including pr-build, merges. Preview should reflect the second PR's rebased tree.
- observability: GH branch-protection event log shows queue activity. `gh api repos/Cogni-DAO/node-template/branches/main/protection | jq '.required_status_checks.contexts'` matches `infra/github/branch-protection.json`.

## Summary

Implements custom tool creation, approval, and dispatch for constellation-lite. The agent can now author TypeScript "custom tools" at runtime, list them, and execute approved ones in a fresh Deno sandbox with declared secrets injected as env vars.

- **`CustomToolManager`** (`src/tools/custom-tool-manager.ts`) — persists tools as `customtool:<name>` documents in the SQLite store. SHA-256 hash of `code + JSON.stringify(parameters)` auto-revokes approval on change.

author: foojanbabaeeian
body:
## Summary

The deployed backend was returning the cryptic Supabase error **"JWS Protected Header is invalid"** on every photo upload, with nothing in the logs that pointed at the root cause. Almost always this turns out to be a malformed env var: a stray newline copied in from a `.env` line, trailing whitespace from a shell paste, or surrounding quotes that didn't get stripped.

This PR makes the failure diagnose itself.

### `supabase_client.py`

- **`_clean_env(name)`** — reads the env var, strips whitespace and surrounding quotes, and warns once via the structured logger when it had to clean anything. The next deploy with a stray newline now shows up as `env var SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY contained whitespace or surrounding quotes` in the boot logs instead of an opaque 503 later.
- **`_looks_like_jwt(token)`** — a JWT is three dot-separated base64url segments. If a key fails this check, an early `logger.error` explains that Storage / Postgrest will reject every request with `"JWS Protected Header is invalid"` and the key needs to be re-pasted.
- **`has_service_role`** now requires the key to be non-empty AND look like a JWT, so we don't claim service-role access when the key is junk.

### `routers/gallery.py` upload endpoint

The storage-upload `except` previously bubbled the raw vendor error string straight to the user. Now it pattern-matches the two common failure modes:

- `JWS Protected Header is invalid` / `JWT … invalid` → `503` with **"Storage credentials look malformed (server-side). Ask an admin to verify SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY..."**
- `row-level security` / `RLS` → `503` explaining the bucket policy needs review or the service-role key isn't set.

Anything else still falls through to the trimmed raw error so the toast stays useful for novel failures.

## What you (the operator) need to do for the deployed JWS error

This PR fixes the diagnostics. The actual root cause on the deployed backend is the env var itself. To verify:

```sh
ssh user@vps
cat /etc/.../travelerhub.env | grep SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY | cat -A
```

If you see `$` in the middle of the value or trailing whitespace, that's the bug. Re-paste the key from the Supabase dashboard with no surrounding quotes / whitespace and restart the backend.

After this PR's `_clean_env` lands, a stray newline / quotes will be auto-stripped and the boot logs will tell you it happened.

## Test plan

- [x] `python -m pytest -q` — 21/21 pass
- [x] Smoke-tested `_looks_like_jwt` on real-shape and malformed inputs
- [x] Smoke-tested `_clean_env` strips whitespace and surrounding quotes (logs a warning)
- [ ] Redeploy and check boot logs — if the env var was malformed, you'll see the warning
- [ ] Try uploading a photo. If it still fails, the toast will name the actual cause (creds malformed, RLS, etc.)

author: nikolays
body:
## Why

Code keeps shipping to `main` faster than it ships to prod. Today's session merged 16 PRs while `willbuy.dev` continued running pre-fix code — every "go on" added more code without moving prod. This breaks that loop.

## What

`.github/workflows/deploy.yml` triggers on `push` to main and on `workflow_dispatch`. It runs `.github/scripts/deploy.sh` over SSH on willbuy-v01 — same commands as issue #488 runbook, but automated.

The deploy script is **idempotent**:
- `git fetch + reset --hard` — safe to re-run
- migrations — sqlever guards re-applies
- `SHARE_TOKEN_HMAC_KEY` — generated only if missing
- `willbuy` user docker-group membership — added only if not already there
- service files — copied only if changed (avoids spurious daemon-reload)
- aggregator image — rebuilt only if sources changed
- post-deploy: full `bash scripts/smoke-test.sh` — workflow fails if not 8/8

## One-time setup

```sh
# Generate dedicated deploy key
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f /tmp/willbuy-deploy -N "" -C github-actions-deploy

# Authorize on server (uses your 1Password agent — Touch ID prompt)
ssh -p 2223 root@87.99.135.213 'cat >> /root/.ssh/authorized_keys' < /tmp/willbuy-deploy.pub

# Store as GitHub secrets
gh secret set DEPLOY_SSH_KEY --repo NikolayS/willbuy < /tmp/willbuy-deploy
gh secret set DEPLOY_HOST --repo NikolayS/willbuy --body 87.99.135.213

# Clean up local copies
rm /tmp/willbuy-deploy /tmp/willbuy-deploy.pub
```

## After setup

Every merge auto-deploys. Manual deploys (e.g. config-only refresh):
```sh
gh workflow run deploy.yml --repo NikolayS/willbuy
```

## Test plan

After merging this PR:
1. Run the one-time setup above (≈ 2 min, single 1Password Touch ID prompt)
2. Trigger deploy: `gh workflow run deploy.yml`
3. Watch logs: `gh run watch`
4. Smoke test runs at the end — workflow fails red if not 8/8

author: latam-cse-dev
body:
This PR adds support for FortiOS username/password authentication using `POST /api/v2/authentication`, while preserving the legacy `/logincheck` flow.

Newer FortiOS versions may return the authenticated session through `session_key_*` and `ccsrf_token_*` cookies instead of returning `session_key` in the JSON body. This patch supports both behaviors:

- JSON `session_key` → uses `Authorization: Bearer`
- Cookie-based session → uses `Cookie` + `x-csrftoken`
- Legacy `/logincheck` remains as fallback

Tested successfully with:

- FortiOS 7.6.6 on FortiGate 50G-SFP
  - `device.open()` returns HTTP 200
  - `device.status` returns version/model/serial
  - `basic_status()` returns HTTP 200

The change is backward-compatible because `/logincheck` is still used as fallback when `/api/v2/authentication` does not work.

Grade remains **orange** because Aave's own `app.aave.com` applies A3-active enforcement (TRM Labs wallet screening + jurisdictional ToS restrictions), and the existence of an alternative frontend mitigates but does not eliminate that gating for the average user.

The disagreement centers on the 5-of-9 Protocol Guardian Safe holding `ReservePaused` power with no time cap and no escape hatch — when paused, `withdraw`/`repay`/`liquidationCall` are gated indefinitely at the Guardian's discretion. We submit this for community discussion: does an indefinite-pause power held by a 5-of-9 multisig without a time-bounded fallback warrant red, or is it sufficiently mitigated by governance veto / on-chain reputation?

Codex grades red while Claude and Gemini grade orange. author: riddy21
body:
## Summary

Removes a stale early-`break` in `build_pipeline_from_topology` (`tt_metal/distributed/experimental/blitz_decode_pipeline.cpp`) that I accidentally left behind during a rebase. The break caused the loopback exit → stage 0 entry pair search to fail on topologies where the directly-connected pair wasn't among the first chips in coord-enumeration order.

## Background

When constructing the blitz decode pipeline, the builder needs to pick two unclaimed chips on `mesh_0` that are **physically wired together by an intra-mesh ethernet link** — one becomes the loopback exit, the other becomes stage 0's entry.

The flow is:

1. Walk `mesh_0`'s chips in coord order.
2. Collect unclaimed ones (chips not already claimed by the inter-mesh ring) into a candidate list.
3. Search the list for a directly-connected pair.

## The bug

Step 2 had a leftover early-`break` that stopped collecting once the list reached `unclaimed_needed` (2) entries:

```cpp
unclaimed_mesh_0_nodes.push_back(fn);
if (unclaimed_mesh_0_nodes.size() >= unclaimed_needed) {
    break;
}
```

This is wrong: the first two unclaimed chips in coord-enumeration order are **not guaranteed to be ethernet neighbors**. Coord order is a logical iteration over the (x, y) grid — it has no relationship to which chips have a direct cable between them. So step 3 would search a candidate set of size 2, fail to find a directly-connected pair, and trip the `TT_FATAL`:

```
loopback_exit_fn.has_value() && stage_0_entry_fn.has_value()
"Could not find a directly-connected unclaimed pair on mesh 0 for loopback exit -> stage 0 entry"
```

## Why it was missed
Rebase onto main re-introduced code that should have been deleted

## Fix

Remove the 3-line early-break block so we collect all unclaimed `mesh_0` chips before searching for the directly-connected pair. This brings the production code back in line with the gtest reference. The extra cost is iterating at most ~6 more chips on `mesh_0`, which is negligible.

## Test plan

- [x] `./build_metal.sh`
- [x] Re-run the failing pytest:
  ```bash
  TT_METAL_SLOW_DISPATCH_MODE=1 tt-run \
    --tcp-interface ens5f0np0 \
    --mpi-args "--tag-output --rankfile=blitz_decode_pipeline_rank_file_single_pod --host $HOSTSP" \
    --rank-binding blitz_decode_pipeline_rank_binding_single_pod.yaml \
    pytest -svv models/demos/deepseek_v3_b1/tests/unit_tests/test_multi_host_pipeline.py::test_passthrough_pipeline_block
  ```
- [x] Confirm `ControlPlaneFixture.SP5_TestBlitzDecodePipelineBuilder` still passes.

author: askumar27
body:
## Summary

The Looker source no longer writes `client_id`, `client_secret`, and `base_url` to `os.environ`. Instead, it constructs a custom `ApiSettings` subclass that returns credentials from in-memory state and passes it to `looker_sdk.init40(config_settings=...)`. Credentials never touch the process environment.

## Motivation

The previous implementation set `LOOKERSDK_CLIENT_ID`, `LOOKERSDK_CLIENT_SECRET`, and `LOOKERSDK_BASE_URL` in `os.environ` immediately before `looker_sdk.init40()`:

```python
os.environ[\"LOOKERSDK_CLIENT_ID\"] = config.client_id
os.environ[\"LOOKERSDK_CLIENT_SECRET\"] = config.client_secret.get_secret_value()
os.environ[\"LOOKERSDK_BASE_URL\"] = config.base_url
self.client = looker_sdk.init40()
```

This is problematic for two reasons:

1. **Security** — `LOOKERSDK_CLIENT_SECRET` is stored in plaintext in the process environment, accessible via `/proc/<pid>/environ` on Linux and to any code running in the same process.
2. **Unnecessary** — the Looker SDK provides a supported mechanism for programmatic credential injection via `init40(config_settings=...)`. The SDK's own README recommends this over env vars for production use.

A previous attempt (release `v0.3.17`) tried to clear the env vars _after_ init, but that doesn't work: `auth_session._login()` is lazy — it calls `self.settings.read_config()` on the first authenticated request, well after any cleanup would run, and the secret is still observable in the meantime.

## Changes Overview

**Refactoring:**
- New private class `_DataHubLookerApiSettings` (subclass of `looker_sdk.rtl.api_settings.ApiSettings`) that overrides `read_config()` to return credentials from instance state.
- `LookerAPI.__init__` now constructs this settings object and passes it via `looker_sdk.init40(config_settings=settings)`. The three `os.environ[...] = ...` writes and the now-unused `import os` are removed.

No changes to `LookerAPIConfig`, `transport_options`, retry logic, or any other source files. The configuration schema is unchanged.

## Architecture / Design Notes

The Looker SDK forces this approach. `ApiSettings` deliberately does **not** store `client_id` / `client_secret` as instance attributes — they only live inside the dict returned by `read_config()`, which `auth_session._login` calls lazily on every login. So:

- Setting `settings.client_id = ...` would be ignored.
- Setting then clearing `LOOKERSDK_*` env vars doesn't work because login is lazy.
- Subclassing and overriding `read_config()` is the SDK's documented extension point.

## Testing

**New unit tests** (`metadata-ingestion/tests/unit/looker/test_looker_lib_wrapper.py`):
- `test_credentials_not_written_to_environ` — asserts no `LOOKERSDK_*` keys appear in `os.environ` after `LookerAPI` construction.
- `test_init40_called_with_in_memory_config_settings` — asserts `looker_sdk.init40` receives a `_DataHubLookerApiSettings` whose `read_config()` returns the supplied credentials.
- `test_settings_read_config_ignores_lookersdk_env_vars` — asserts `read_config()` returns the in-memory creds even when `LOOKERSDK_*` env vars are set on the process.

**Existing tests:** all 74 looker/lookml unit tests pass. The looker integration tests that mock `looker_sdk.init40` are unaffected; the one that constructs a real `LookerAPI` (`test_independent_soft_deleted_looks`) passes.

**Live verification:** ran both `looker` and `lookml` ingestion against a real Looker instance.

Both runs successfully authenticated, proving the new `read_config()` path works end-to-end (login flow could not have completed otherwise).

**Lint:** `./gradlew :metadata-ingestion:lint` clean (ruff + ruff format + mypy on 2,285 files).

## Impact Assessment

- **Affected components:** `metadata-ingestion` Looker / LookML connectors only.
- **Breaking changes:** None. `LookerAPIConfig` schema, recipe format, and external behavior are unchanged. Anyone relying on the side effect of `LOOKERSDK_*` env vars being set after a Looker ingest run will find them missing — this is a private SDK detail and was not a documented contract.
- **Performance impact:** None.

author: ericspencer00
body:
Closes #157

## Summary

Adds `resilient/src/inline.rs`: a bytecode pass that replaces `Op::Call(idx)` to small leaf functions with the callee's body, eliminating call-frame push/pop overhead and exposing follow-on optimization opportunities.

A function is inlineable when ALL of:
- Body ≤ `INLINE_THRESHOLD` (= 10) bytecode ops, excluding the trailing `ReturnFromCall` terminator.
- No self-recursion (`Call(self_idx)` or any `TailCall`).
- No closures (`MakeClosure`, `LoadUpvalue`).
- No foreign calls (`CallForeign`) — opaque side effects, conservatively skipped.

At each call site, the rewrite:
1. Allocates fresh local slots `[base..base+local_count)` in the caller (bumps caller's `local_count`).
2. Emits `StoreLocal(base + a-1) … StoreLocal(base + 0)` to consume args off the stack (mirrors the VM's `Op::Call` ABI).
3. Inlines the callee body, remapping `LoadLocal/StoreLocal/IncLocal` indices through `+base`, re-interning constant-pool indices into the caller's pool, and rewriting `ReturnFromCall` → `Jump(end)` so the result on top of the stack lands exactly where a normal `Call` would have left it.

Iterates to fixpoint (capped at `MAX_PASSES = 5`).

Wired into `compiler::compile()` right before the `Program` is returned, next to `const_fold`'s call. Gated behind `RESILIENT_INLINE=1` exactly as `const_fold` is gated behind `RESILIENT_CONST_FOLD=1` — pre-existing tests pin specific opcode sequences (e.g. `compile_call_emits_call_op`) that inlining would change.

22 unit tests covering: inlineable / not-inlineable predicates (small leaf, recursive, large, tail-call, foreign, closure), threshold boundary, body-counter terminator stripping, end-to-end inlining of zero-arg / unary / arithmetic-body fns, idempotence, env-var differential. The differential test serializes through a static mutex so concurrent test threads don't race the env var.

## Test changes

No existing tests modified. Gated behind `RESILIENT_INLINE=1` env var.

author: omerhochman
body:
## Summary

Three bugs surfaced after [#46](https://github.com/nlqdb/nlqdb/pull/46) shipped:

1. **Live `<nlq-data>` on hero rendered "set a db attribute".** Element validates `db` as required (`element.ts:104`); my last PR dropped `db="demo"` along with the bad endpoint. Restored on both the live element and the copy-paste snippet. The demo endpoint accepts any `dbId` and ignores it; `"demo"` is the conventional value the snippet shows.
2. **Magic-link `POST` failed with CORS error** when sent from `nlqdb.com` → `app.nlqdb.com`. Better Auth's `trustedOrigins` config is CSRF allowlisting only — it does NOT emit `Access-Control-*` headers. Added Hono `cors()` middleware on `/api/auth/*` and `/v1/chat/*` with an explicit allow-list (credentials require a specific origin, not `*`). Also covers PR-preview URLs (`pr-N.nlqdb-web.pages.dev`) via regex match so future preview deploys of auth changes work end-to-end without rewiring.
3. **GitHub + Google buttons missing on /sign-in.** `auth.ts` already has both providers wired (`socialProviders.github`, `.google`). Page just didn't expose them. Added two buttons that POST `/api/auth/sign-in/social` with `{provider, callbackURL}` and follow the returned `url`. Same `callbackURL` plumbing as magic-link, so `?return_to=` round-trips through OAuth too.

## What changed

| File | Why |
|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/components/Hero.astro` | Add `db="demo"` back on live element + visible snippet |
| `apps/api/src/index.ts` | `cors()` middleware with credentialed allow-list on `/api/auth/*` + `/v1/chat/*` |
| `apps/web/src/pages/sign-in.astro` | GitHub + Google buttons + divider + minimal styles |

## CORS allow-list

```
https://nlqdb.com
https://www.nlqdb.com
https://nlqdb-web.pages.dev
/^https:\/\/pr-\d+\.nlqdb-web\.pages\.dev$/
http://localhost:4321
http://localhost:8787
```

`/v1/demo/*` keeps its own `*`-origin policy (no credentials, public read). `/v1/ask` stays uncovered — revisit when third-party `pk_live_` `<nlq-data>` embeds land (Phase 1).

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a self-contained `semg-jepa` project based on `dgaddy/silent_speech` to support raw-EMG JEPA self-supervised pretraining and CTC recognition workflows. 
- Reuse and adapt the existing EMG data loading / preprocessing logic so dataset I/O and normalization match the original pipeline. 
- Refactor the model to separate the raw-EMG encoder from the CTC output head to enable pretraining the encoder and later attaching an output head for CTC fine-tuning.

### Description
- Added a new Python package `semg_jepa/` with adapted data utilities in `data_utils.py` and dataset loader in `read_emg.py` that expose the requested fields (`emg`, `raw_emg`, `text_int`, `session_ids`, `silent`) and preserve `combine_fixed_length`, `decollate_tensor`, `SizeAwareSampler`, and `EMGDataset.collate_raw` usage. 
- Refactored architecture into `GaddyRawEMGEncoder(raw_emg) -> [B, T, D]`, `CTCHead([B, T, D]) -> [B, T, vocab+1]`, and a `BaselineCTCModel` wrapper in `semg_jepa/architecture.py`. 
- Implemented augmentations in `semg_jepa/augmentations.py` supporting channel dropout, time masking, amplitude scaling, Gaussian noise, and small temporal shifts for JEPA views. 
- Implemented JEPA pretraining flow in `train_jepa_pretrain.py` with student / EMA teacher, weak/strong augmentations, cosine latent prediction loss plus variance anti-collapse regularizer, and export of the pretrained encoder. 
- Implemented baseline CTC training in `train_baseline_ctc.py` to reproduce original CTC training, and fine-tune script `train_jepa_finetune_ctc.py` that loads a pretrained encoder and supports frozen or full fine-tuning. 
- Added `semg_jepa/ctc_utils.py` and `evaluate_ctc.py` to run beam-search decoding and compute WER using the same `CTCBeamDecoder` settings as the original pipeline. 
- Project metadata and docs: `pyproject.toml` and `README.md` with expected `--data-config` keys and script descriptions.

### Testing

author: joeydewaal
body:
First of three PRs splitting the production deploy work for easier review. **Supersedes #44** (please close).

## Architecture

- **Backend** → Fly.io (`fly deploy`)
- **Frontend** → Cloudflare Pages (`cd frontend && npm run deploy`, no auto-deploy)
- **Avatars** → still on the Fly volume in this PR; moves to R2 in PR 3

## What's in this PR

### Backend
- Multi-stage `Dockerfile` at repo root: `rust:1.95-slim-bookworm` builder, `debian:stable-slim` runtime, no frontend stage. `.dockerignore` excludes target/, node_modules, .env, sqlite files
- `fly.toml`: dockerfile build, `DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///data/database.db` (avoids the silent in-memory default), `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, `PUBLIC_API_URL`, `min_machines_running = 1`, `/health` check
- New `GET /health` endpoint
- `Config::allowed_origins` (comma-separated env) drives the CORS layer; `CorsLayer::permissive()` only when no origins are configured (i.e. dev)
- `Config::public_api_url` makes avatar URLs absolute (`PUBLIC_API_URL/avatars/<id>.webp`) so a cross-origin frontend renders them
- OIDC `use_dev_cookies(true)` is now gated to `!cfg!(feature = "prod")`

### Frontend
- Switch `adapter-auto` → `adapter-static` with `fallback: "index.html"` (the app already runs `ssr = false`)
- `lib/api/client.ts` and `lib/live-match.svelte.ts` honour `VITE_API_BASE_URL` for both HTTP and WebSocket
- `wrangler` dev dep + `npm run deploy` script — manual deploys per your "no auto-redeploy" requirement
- `frontend/.env.example` documents `VITE_API_BASE_URL`

### CI / hygiene
- New CI job `docker-build` runs `docker buildx build --load .` so a broken Dockerfile fails the PR
- `.gitignore` now covers `.env`, target/, sqlite files, node/build artifacts
- `backend/.env.example` template

## Operator steps before / after deploy

- [ ] Create the CF Pages project named `noordpool` and set `VITE_API_BASE_URL=https://api.noordpool.joeydewaal.com` in its build env
- [ ] DNS: `noordpool.joeydewaal.com` → CF Pages, `api.noordpool.joeydewaal.com` → Fly
- [ ] Update Google Cloud Console OAuth redirect URL to `https://api.noordpool.joeydewaal.com/api/auth/google/callback`
- [ ] `fly secrets set FRONTEND_URL=https://noordpool.joeydewaal.com`
- [ ] Rotate VAPID keys (briefly committed on a feature branch)

## Follow-up PRs

- **PR 2** — rustls cleanup: swap web-push HTTP transport to reqwest+rustls (kills curl-sys / native-tls)
- **PR 3** — R2 avatars: presigned uploads, drop `/avatars` ServeDir, drop `image` + `multipart`

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo build` clean
- [x] `cargo test` — all green
- [x] `npm run build` produces `frontend/build/index.html`
- [ ] CI `docker-build` passes
- [ ] Local: `cargo run` and frontend dev server still work

body:
Removes the YAML-manifest agent path from the registry and consolidates on Python `agent.py` custom agents. This eliminates the dynamic `type()` builder, the Pydantic `AgentManifest` model, and the `_write_merged_mcp_config` MCP-sidecar writer — a net security improvement (removes a dynamic-import sink driven by user-controlled YAML).

The `agent.yaml` companion sidecar used to declare `models:` alongside a Python agent is **unchanged**.

## What changed

- **`registry.py`**: deleted `AgentManifest`, `_load_manifest_agent`, `_create_manifest_agent_class`, `_write_merged_mcp_config`; `_load_from_dir` now skips YAML-only dirs with a `DeprecationWarning`; `AgentRegistration.source` narrowed to `Literal["builtin", "custom_python"]`; companion YAML guard warns if manifest-style keys are present.
- **`export_import.py`**: export side no longer bundles YAML-only dirs; import side surfaces a migration error for incoming YAML-only bundles.
- **`ui/models.py`**: `AgentInfo.source` narrowed to `Literal["builtin", "custom_python"]`.
- **Tests**: manifest tests removed; new `TestYamlOnlyDeprecation`, `TestCompanionYamlGuard`, `TestRemovedSymbols` classes added; `sys.modules` autouse fixture prevents importlib leakage across tests; `test_export_import.py` covers YAML-only bundle rejection.
- **Docs**: migration section added to `custom-agent.mdx`; `plugin-registry.mdx` and `sdk/patterns.mdx` purged of manifest docs; stale refs removed from `CLAUDE.md`, agent builder, CI workflow.
- **Deleted**: `schemas/agent-manifest.schema.json`, `util/gen_manifest_schema.py`.

## Test plan

- [ ] `python -m pytest tests/unit/agents/test_registry.py tests/unit/test_export_import.py -xvs`
- [ ] `python -m pytest tests/unit/ -x`
- [ ] `python util/lint.py --all --fix` (no errors)
- [ ] `grep -rn "AgentManifest\|_load_manifest_agent\|_create_manifest_agent_class\|_write_merged_mcp_config\|custom_manifest" src/ tests/ docs/` returns only the deprecation-warning string in `registry.py`

Closes #912

author: omer475
body:
## Summary
Replaces the text-length expected_read estimate (PR #85) with **actual median dwell of other readers** on each article. This is the exact Kuaishou production approach.

## Why
PR #85 used \`expected_read_seconds = 3 + bullet_chars/20 + (component? 6 : 0)\`. Reasonable estimate, but Kuaishou's actual approach (CIKM 2023) is to compare to **other users' watch percentile** on the same content. We have ~140 dwell events per active user; we have data; we just weren't using it.

## What ships
- **Migration 073**: \`article_dwell_stats\` table + \`refresh_article_dwell_stats()\` RPC. Aggregates last 30 days of \`article_exit\` events. Requires ≥5 observations per article. Initial backfill: 32 articles, avg median dwell 20.5s.
- **track.js**: parallel \`Promise.all\` fetch of article meta + dwell stats — same wall-clock latency as one query. \`expectedReadSecondsFromArticle\` prefers observed median, falls back to text estimate for cold-start.
- **main.js Phase F session-delta**: same pattern — batch-fetches dwell stats alongside embeddings, builds a lookup map.
- **cloudrun_entrypoint.py**: refreshes stats in the existing 03:00 UTC nightly slot (same as cluster centroid rebuild). Cheap aggregate, runs in seconds.

## Source
Kuaishou CIKM 2023 ([arXiv:2308.13249](https://arxiv.org/html/2308.13249)) — GVV/EVV/FVV definitions use percentile-of-other-users, not absolute thresholds.

body:
## Summary

- Preserve the `symlink_metadata` error source when canonicalization first reports `NotFound` and metadata probing then fails for a different reason.
- Keep true not-found entries classified as `PathViolation::Missing` only when both canonicalization and metadata probing report `NotFound`.
- Keep dangling symlinks and suspicious missing-like cases failing closed as `CanonicalizeFailed`.

## Diagnostic behavior

Before: `canonicalize` returning `NotFound` followed by `symlink_metadata` returning a non-`NotFound` error still reported the original canonicalize `NotFound` source.

After: `symlink_metadata` non-`NotFound` errors are preserved as the `CanonicalizeFailed` source, so permission or environment failures report the more accurate filesystem error.

## Trust behavior

No trust-policy behavior changes. Dirty Git-index entries that are truly missing remain skippable, while dangling symlinks, permissions failures, root escapes, and other non-missing canonicalization failures fail closed.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt-check`

## Summary
End-to-end visual overhaul of the actor sheet and chat cards, plus the small TS/template/migration plumbing the redesign relies on.

### UI redesign (SCSS + tabs binding + header markup)

Neutralizes Foundry's stark default `1px solid #999` cell outlines inside `.od6s` (the main source of the previous tax-form appearance) and reintroduces intentional surfaces in the component layer.

- New `foundry:init-config` Task that disables telemetry in the dev container's `options.json` before startup, plus `FOUNDRY_TELEMETRY=false` env var.

author: andyluo7
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a correctness-first HIP/ROCm path for the HiSparse JIT cache-loading kernel.

- Remove the direct `cuda_runtime.h` include and rely on the existing JIT `utils.cuh` CUDA/HIP abstraction.
- Keep the existing optimized CUDA warp/inline-PTX implementation under the non-ROCm path.
- Add a simple serial per-request HIP path for correctness on ROCm, avoiding wave32/wave64 assumptions and CUDA inline PTX while the optimized HIP implementation is developed.
- Skip `cudaFuncSetAttribute` on ROCm.
- Register the HiSparse JIT unit test in AMD CI.

## Scope

This is stacked on top of #23877, which updates HiSparse NSA backend policy so HIP selects `tilelang` instead of CUDA-only `flashmla_sparse`.

This PR is intentionally correctness-first. The HIP path is not yet optimized; performance tuning should follow after end-to-end ROCm HiSparse validation.

## Testing

Tested in a nightly SGLang ROCm container on an 8x AMD Instinct MI350X server (`gfx950`, HIP 7.0):

```bash
python3 -m pytest python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_hisparse.py -q
python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py -q
python3 -m py_compile python/sglang/jit_kernel/hisparse.py python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_hisparse.py
python3 - <<'PY'
from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import ut_parse_one_file
regs, has_main = ut_parse_one_file('python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_hisparse.py')
assert any(r.backend.name == 'AMD' for r in regs)
assert has_main
PY
```

Results:

```text
python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_hisparse.py: 5 passed
 test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py: 42 passed, 5 warnings
```

Ruff is not installed in this nightly container, so I could not run `ruff check` locally.

## Additional MI300X / FP8 KV Validation

The stacked HiSparse ROCm path was also validated on an 8x MI300X server with GLM-5.1-FP8, TP8, ROCm TileLang NSA, `--enable-hisparse`, and `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`.

Relevant to this PR, the HiSparse JIT validation passed on MI300X:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=$PWD/python python3 -m pytest python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_hisparse.py -q -s
```

Result:

```text
7 passed
```

The final stacked validation in #23970 passed long-prompt serving up to 25,513 prompt tokens, 16-way concurrent completion, and GSM8K 5-shot 200-question accuracy at `0.955` vs the GLM-5.1 threshold `0.93` while the runtime selected `torch.float8_e4m3fnuz` for FP8 KV cache.

Caveat: SGLang logs that FP8 KV scaling factors are not provided and defaults them to `1.0`; the accuracy signal passed despite that, so the FP8 KV support claim should stay scoped to the validated GLM-5.1-FP8 MI300X ROCm/TileLang path for now.

Local MI300X artifacts are saved under `/models/sglang_hisparse_mi300x_results_20260428T235702Z/`.

author: janhilgard
body:
## Summary

- **Fix `batch_generator` stats not propagated**: `BatchedEngine.get_stats()` promotes selected keys from MLLM scheduler stats to top-level, but `batch_generator` was missing from the promoted keys list. This caused `generation_tps` and `prompt_tps` to always be 0 in `/v1/status`.
- **Fix batch extension time attribution**: Mid-generation batch extension (text-only requests joining an active batch) set `prompt_processing=True`, causing the entire step time to be attributed to `prompt_time` even though the dominant cost is generating tokens for existing requests. This made `generation_tps` permanently 0 while `prompt_tps` was artificially inflated.
- **Expose `generation_tps` and `prompt_tps`** from `MLLMBatchStats` in the `/v1/status` endpoint so monitoring dashboards can consume server-side throughput metrics.

author: mkopnsrc
body:
## Summary

Adds a cron-driven workflow that walks each Beat package up the missing-version ladder one version per tick, gated on the previous version's chocolatey.org moderation status. The CCR moderation queue becomes the implicit pacing.

## Changes

### Workflows
- `.github/workflows/backfill.yml` — **new**. Cron `0 */6 * * *` + `workflow_dispatch`. Two jobs:
  1. `plan` (Linux): reads `automatic/*/backfill.json`, queries CCR OData for each package's existing versions + `PackageStatus`, decides next-version-to-push per package.
  2. `push` (matrix → reusable workflow): calls `package-build-test.yml` per (package, version) tuple.
- `.github/workflows/package-build-test.yml` — refactored to add `workflow_call:` trigger alongside `workflow_dispatch:`, plus a new `force_version` input that sets `$global:au_Version` before `./update.ps1` runs.

### Per-Beat changes
- `automatic/<beat>/update.ps1` — `au_GetLatest` now honors `$global:au_Version`: when set, skips the elastic.co page scrape and uses the override directly to construct the URL.
- `automatic/<beat>/backfill.json` — **new**. Per-package version target list:
  ```json
  { "versions": ["8.19.14", "9.3.0", "9.3.1", "9.3.2", "9.3.3"] }
  ```

## Gate logic (per package, per cycle)

| CCR latest status | Action |
|---|---|
| Submitted / Pending | Skip — still in moderation |
| Rejected | Skip + log error annotation; manual fix needed |
| Approved | Find lowest version in `backfill.json` not yet on CCR; push it |
| (empty / no versions) | Push lowest backfill version |

## Pre-conditions

- `CHOCO_API_KEY` repo secret (already in place; inherited by called workflow)
- `actions/checkout@v5`, `actions/upload-artifact@v5` already in allowlist

## Test plan

- [ ] Merge
- [ ] Manual dispatch of `backfill.yml` with `dry_run=true` to verify the plan computation against the live CCR API (should propose `8.19.14` for all 5 Beats)
- [ ] Re-dispatch with `dry_run=false` to actually push 5 × `8.19.14`
- [ ] Wait for chocolatey moderation; on next cron tick after approval, verify it auto-advances to `9.3.0`
- [ ] After all 5 Beats reach `9.3.3`, the `plan` job should report "caught up" for each

## Caveats

- AU's choco-version-check is left on; if a target version already exists on CCR, AU will skip the push (correct idempotent behavior).
- Repo nuspec stays at `8.14.1` between backfill cycles (we don't commit the bumped nuspec back to master). Each cycle starts from master and bumps in CI only. The CCR/published version is the source of truth.
- Per-cycle parallelism is unlimited (all 5 Beats can submit simultaneously). If chocolatey moderators flag this, switch to `max-parallel: 1` in the matrix.

author: cirwel
body:
## Summary

`UNITARESMonitor.last_update` was set in `__init__` but never serialized in `save_persisted_state`. Combined with lazy monitor construction in `agent_lifecycle.py:21-56`, this silently froze cross-restart gaps to ~0 — a 17h overnight gap integrated as 0.5s of decay, losing decay terms (μ·S, δ·V) that should have integrated.

Live-verifier counted **540 of 543** agent state files have a last checkin predating the current server start, so all of them would exhibit the freeze on next checkin without this fix.

## Changes

- `save_persisted_state` writes `last_update_iso` (sibling key to `behavioral_eisv` in the JSON payload)
- `load_persisted_state` reads it back and assigns directly to `monitor.last_update`; absent field falls back to the in-memory `__init__` value (backward compat with pre-fix state files)
- `process_update` clamps `elapsed_seconds = max(0.0, ...)` as defense against NTP backward step
- `info` log line emitted when `scaled_dt > DT_MAX` so saturation is operator-visible — semantics of multi-hour gap saturation are deferred to a paper-coupled follow-up; current numerical behavior unchanged

## Council review

This change went through two rounds of dialectic-architect + code-reviewer + live-verifier. The first round had the bug direction inverted (claimed silent DT_MAX *inflation*); the re-review caught that lazy construction makes the actual failure mode silent *freeze*, not inflation. Files referenced:

- `src/governance_monitor.py:131` — where `last_update` is set in `__init__`
- `src/agent_lifecycle.py:21-56` — lazy monitor construction
- `src/governance_monitor.py:728-736` — original `effective_dt` formula

Note: a `simulate_update` race the first reviewer flagged was confirmed a **false positive** on re-review (proper save/restore at lines 649/693 with `finally` block). No fix needed there.

## Out of scope (filed as follow-ups)

- DT_MAX saturation semantics — once persistence ships, a 17h gap and 30h gap integrate identically (1.0 unit decay). Needs a paper-coupled answer (variable-step integrator, "stale-agent" verdict bypassing ODE above τ, or explicit doc as known approximation).
- Adjacent same-class `__init__`-sets-`now()` bugs: `_prev_checkin_time = monotonic()` (line 158), `created_at = datetime.now()` (line 238), `dual_log.py` ContinuityLayer/RestorativeBalanceMonitor internal clocks.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_last_update_persistence.py` — 8 tests, all green
- [x] Full suite: 7737 passed, 23 skipped, 1 deselected (`test_epoch_registry::test_current_epoch_has_registry_row` is a pre-existing DB-migration failure on master, not introduced by this PR)
- [x] Pre-push smoke: 138 passed

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a runnable MVP implementing the core idea: interactive 3D globe and 2D map with jurisdiction-aware prayer-time results and a developer-friendly architecture for future refinement. 
- Ship a data-driven jurisdiction -> method mapping and a normalized prayer-method registry so calculation policy (high-latitude/polar/elevation) is explicit and configurable. 
- Deliver an initial UX with timeline controls, method selection modes (`auto-jurisdiction`, `global-method`, `compare`) and a location details panel that shows sea-level and elevation-adjusted times. 

### Description
- Project scaffold: added a Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind app with scripts `dev`, `build`, `preview`, `lint`, `type-check`, and `test`, plus lockfile and TS configs. 
- Views & UI: implemented a Three.js `GlobeView` (raycast click selection, subsolar marker, directional light, proper cleanup) and a canvas `MapView` (click->lat/lon, day/night shading, sampled visual prayer lines), and built dense control components: `ControlPanel`, `TimelineControls`, `MethodSelector`, `ViewToggle`, and `LocationDetails`. 
- Prayer domain & policy: added `PRAYER_METHODS` registry and `buildMethodParameters` wrappers, `prayer-times` calculation that supports high-latitude and polar overrides and elevation adjustments, and a `jurisdiction-methods.json` + `policyForCountry` resolver to map ISO country -> policy. 
- Geo & environment services: added `timezone-lookup` (uses `tz-lookup` with longitude fallback and cache), coarse `country-lookup` bbox resolver (MVP), and `elevation-service` (Open-Meteo lookup, cache, `ElevationSample` with `confidence`). 
- Solar helpers: added `solar-position` and `terminator` helpers used to place the subsolar marker and shade day/night. 
- Docs & notes: added `docs/methodology.md` and `docs/accuracy.md` documenting architecture, fallbacks, and known limitations (notably: coarse bbox country lookup and sampled overlay approximations). 
- Tests & types: added Vitest tests for coordinate conversions, timezone/country lookup, method registry, prayer calculations including high-latitude and elevation adjustments, plus `src/types.d.ts` for `tz-lookup`. 

### Testing
- Ran lint: `npm run lint` — succeeded (ESLint checks passed after adding environment globals). 
- Ran type-check: `npm run type-check` — succeeded (`tsc --noEmit`). 
- Ran unit tests: `npm run test` — Vitest executed `tests/prayer.spec.ts` (8 tests) and all tests passed. 
- Production build: `npm run build` — Vite production build succeeded; note Vite emitted a bundle-size warning about large chunks (suggest code-splitting/manualChunks). 
- Notes: automated checks and build succeeded for the MVP; known limitations (documented) include coarse bbox country lookup (not yet polygon geofencing) and global prayer overlays implemented as sampled visual guidance rather than fully-tiled jurisdiction-resolved contour fields.

The cache-hit prologue was duplicated verbatim across the two
rule-entry opcodes. A single `RuleEnter(MemoId, RuleKind, Label)`
runs the prologue once under one borrow on `self.memo`; only the
post-miss frame layout (push `Memo` vs walk-stack-and-push `LFrame`)
branches on `RuleKind`. The exit-side factor is a `cache_success`
helper that both `MemoClose` and `LRTail`'s no-growth branch share.

Semantics-preserving — see `src/pegvm/vm.rs` `Instruction::RuleEnter`
arm and the new `cache_success` method.

Closes #52.

author: marbre
body:
The kpack-split host wheel METADATA today emits per-target extras as the bare bundle key, so a single find-links URL exposes two different conventions for the same SDK + PyTorch stack:

  pip install rocm[device-gfx1201]   # rocm-sdk-core
  pip install torch[gfx1201]         # kpack-split host wheel

This aligns the kpack splitter to emit the `device-<arch>` pattern used in rocm-sdk-core so both halves share one install command.

Apply the prefix uniformly: the per-target extras
(`device-gfx1201`, ...) and the aggregate (`device-all`) all start with `device-` after this commit and widens the regex in `_add_variant_markers_to_metadata` to match the new `[\w-]+` extra names, and strips the `device-` prefix before substituting the bare arch into the PEP 817 `"amd :: gfx_arch :: <arch>"` marker.

author: wavespestcontrolfl
body:
## Summary

Closes the photo-system loop end-to-end: techs upload photos via the new field UI (#351), and now customers can actually see them on the track page.

Two stacked bugs in `track-public.js#buildSummary`:

1. **Wrong column.** `SELECT s3_url` — but `tech-track.js` writes only to `service_photos.s3_key`. `s3_url` is a legacy column that's null in practice, so `.filter(Boolean)` erased every row. Result: customer track page returned `photos: []` for every completed visit, even ones with photos attached.
2. **Stale soft-join.** The lookup matched `service_records` by `(customer_id, service_date, service_type)` — the same cross-visit collision pattern PR #340 fixed in the tech upload route. Migration `20260427000007` added a direct `scheduled_service_id` FK; tech-track.js uses it; this route was the last consumer still on the soft-join.

## Architecture

- `service_records` lookup now uses `where({ scheduled_service_id: service.id })` — same canonical path as `tech-track.js#211-214`. Customer view and tech upload now resolve to the same row across same-day double visits.
- Photos are read-time presigned via `PhotoService.getViewUrl(s3_key, 900)` — 15-minute TTL, matches the `resolveTechPhotoUrl` cadence used for the tech avatar two lines above. Never persisted as presigned URLs.
- Per-photo presign failures filter that one photo out rather than erroring the whole summary — same defensive shape as the surrounding try/catch.
- All inside the existing token-scoped boundary (`track_view_token` lookup at line 165). No new public route, no AGENTS.md allow-list change.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open a track URL for a completed visit that has photos uploaded → confirm photos render as 2-col thumbnails on TrackPage.
- [ ] Open a track URL for a completed visit with NO photos → confirm `photos: []` and TrackPage degrades cleanly.
- [ ] Wait 16 minutes on the same page → photo URLs should 403 (TTL expired). Refresh → new presigned URLs should render.
- [ ] Same-day double visit (e.g., morning pest + afternoon lawn for same customer): each track URL should now show only its own photos, not the other visit's. (Pre-fix it could grab whichever record matched the soft-join first.)
- [ ] No regression on `serviceReportToken` and `invoiceToken` for the same buildSummary call — they're unchanged.

## Out of scope (deferred)

- `missed_photo` detector — now genuinely unblocked across all surfaces (tech upload + customer view both work).
- Schema cleanup: drop the now-unused `service_photos.s3_url` column. Separate PR — keeping data-shape changes off the read-path fix.

## Summary

- **Bounded-parallel feature execution**: replaces sequential feature loop in e2e-deep driver with a Semaphore-gated `Promise.allSettled` pool (`FEATURE_CONCURRENCY=2`), cutting per-service wall-clock time roughly in half
- **Feature-type filtering on trigger API**: extends the `/api/probes/:id/trigger` endpoint to accept `featureTypes` filter, threading it through HTTP handler → scheduler → invoker → ProbeContext → driver — enabling targeted probe runs against specific feature types
- **Config tuning**: bumps `max_concurrency` 2→4 and `timeout_ms` 300s→180s in e2e-deep.yml to match the faster execution model

## Key changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `e2e-deep.ts` | Semaphore class, `FEATURE_CONCURRENCY`, parallel pool, feature-type filter, canonical `isD5FeatureType` import |
| `probes.ts` | `featureTypes` validation, `slugsProvided` envelope semantics |
| `types/index.ts` | `featureTypes?: string[]` on `ProbeContext` |
| `scheduler.ts` | `featureTypes` on `TriggerOptions.filter` |
| `probe-invoker.ts` | `featureTypes` on `InvokerTriggerOptions.filter` + `ExecuteOneOpts`, threaded to ProbeContext |
| `e2e-parity.ts` | Replaced redundant `ALL_KNOWN_FEATURES` with canonical `isD5FeatureType` |
| `e2e-deep.yml` | `max_concurrency: 4`, `timeout_ms: 180000` |
| Tests | 15 new tests (8 driver + 7 HTTP) covering parallelism, filtering, Semaphore, graceful degradation |

## Test plan

- [x] 1320 showcase-ops tests pass (including 15 new)
- [x] Typecheck clean
- [x] Build clean
- [x] CR loop converged: 2 fix rounds + 2 confirmation rounds, 0 bucket (a) findings
- [ ] CI green

Thrift "[official](https://github.com/ahawkins/docker-thrift/issues/12)" images has been [deprecated](https://github.com/docker-library/docs/pull/1732) and then [removed](https://github.com/docker-library/official-images/pull/11079) from the repository. This pull request aims to:

* Make it truly official, as in powered by the Apache Thrift monorepo
* Introduce some automation for library generation, along with build checks

author: jgowdy-godaddy
body:
## Summary

Four distinct flake patterns showed up across recent PRs (#197, #204, #205, #186). Three are the same root cause — runner resource exhaustion. The fourth is a real test bug.

### Resource exhaustion (3 of 4 flakes)

- **rust-lld SIGBUS in `llvm::parallelFor`** during link of test binaries (#204).
- **"No space left on device"** mid-build on rust-tests rerun (#204).
- **"Hosted runner lost communication with the server"** after ~50 min on lint (#186).

All three are the same shape: debug-mode test binaries in this workspace statically link the AWS SDK + OpenSSL + Postgres/MySQL/SQLite + aws-lc-rs, peaking ~3-5 GB resident per link. The workspace `target/` + sccache + vendored OpenSSL/aws-lc-sys outputs together exceed the 14 GB free on a stock `ubuntu-latest` runner.

Two mitigations:
1. **Cap link concurrency on the heavy jobs** — set `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2` and `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` on `lint`, `integration-tests`, and `interop-tests`, matching the pattern that fixed `rust-tests` in `47740e7`.
2. **Free ~15 GB before the cargo work** — `scripts/ci-free-disk-space.sh` removes Android SDK + GHC + Boost + Swift + Chrome + Edge from the hosted runner image (none of these jobs use them). Wired into `lint`, `rust-tests`, `integration-tests`, `interop-tests`.

### Go hook tests (1 of 4 flakes)

`TestMetricsHookSurvivesManyOperations` and friends were asserting event counts after `waitFor(2*time.Second, ...)`. Hook delivery is async via a tokio worker (`asherah-ffi/src/hooks.rs`), and on a loaded CI runner the worker can take well over 2 s to drain. The failure mode was distinctive: the high-volume test got 87 events for an expected ≥200, meaning ~half the events were still in the worker's queue when the test gave up.

Two fixes in `asherah-go/hooks_test.go`:
- Bump per-test waitFor deadlines to 30 s via a `hookWaitDeadline` constant. Tests still return as soon as the predicate succeeds, so local runs are unchanged.
- Replace the threshold-based `waitFor(>= 200)` in `TestMetricsHookSurvivesManyOperations` with a new `waitForSteady` helper that polls until the count is stable for 500 ms (i.e. the worker has drained), then asserts. The threshold form races the worker even with a longer timeout.

## Test plan

- [x] `scripts/test.sh --lint` clean locally.
- [x] All 7 previously-flaky Go hook tests pass locally in 1.9 s with the new helpers.
- [x] `yq` validates the modified `ci.yml`.
- [ ] CI green (the test of the test, basically — confirm the new disk-cleanup + concurrency caps don't introduce regressions).

## Out of scope

If flakes still appear after this PR, the next step is moving heavy jobs to `ubuntu-latest-large` (4× CPU, 16 GB → ~64 GB disk) or self-hosted runners. Tracked but not in this PR.

body:
# Which issue does this PR close?

N/A

# Rationale for this change

This PR replaces `shuffle_bench` with a Parquet-driven runner modeled after [DataFusion Comet's `shuffle_bench`](https://github.com/apache/datafusion-comet/blob/main/native/shuffle/src/bin/shuffle_bench.rs). 
The CLI surface is intentionally kept close to Comet's so the same `--input` / `--partitions` / `--hash-columns` / `--memory-limit` arguments work against both binaries.

# What changes are included in this PR?

New benchmark.

# How to reproduce

Example:

```sh
cargo build --release --bin shuffle_bench

# Sort writer
./target/release/shuffle_bench \
  --input /path/to/tpch/sf100/lineitem \
  --writer sort --partitioning hash \
  --partitions 200 --hash-columns 0,3 \
  --memory-limit 8589934592 \
  --limit 1000000 --warmup 1 --iterations 3

# Hash writer
./target/release/shuffle_bench \
  --input /path/to/tpch/sf100/lineitem \
  --writer hash --partitioning hash \
  --partitions 200 --hash-columns 0,3 \
  --memory-limit 8589934592 \
  --limit 1000000 --warmup 1 --iterations 3
```

# Are there any user-facing changes?

The CLI surface of `shuffle_bench` changes (different flags, switched from `structopt` to `clap`). This binary is a developer profiling tool, not a public API. Anyone scripting against the previous synthetic flags (`--rows`, `--input-partitions`, `--hash-only`, `--sort-only`, etc.) will need to migrate to the new `--input` / `--writer` form.

No library or wire-format changes.

author: calxus
body:
## what

- Make the S3 planfile store authenticate via the active Atmos auth identity instead of always falling back to the AWS SDK default credential chain.
- Add an `IdentityAwareBackend` interface to `pkg/ci/artifact` so the registry can inject an `AuthContextResolver` (mirroring the existing `pkg/store` pattern).
- Refactor the S3 backend to defer client initialization when an identity is configured and resolve credentials lazily via the injected resolver.
- Wire `ci.createPlanfileStore` to propagate `info.Identity` (the resolved `--identity` / `ATMOS_IDENTITY` value) and a resolver built from `info.AuthManager`.
- Add unit tests covering registry resolver injection, S3 lazy init paths, and `attachIdentity` precedence.

## why

- `atmos terraform plan` was succeeding in CI (the Terraform subprocess inherits the prepared environment) but the subsequent S3 planfile upload failed with IMDS errors because the upload runs in the parent atmos process, which had no awareness of the active identity.
- Common CI setups assume GitHub OIDC + IAM role assumption is enough — the parent process has no ambient AWS credentials to fall back on, so the failure surfaced as a confusing AWS-side error rather than an Atmos config issue.
- The fix reuses the same identity resolver pattern already used by SSM / Azure Key Vault / GSM stores, so AWS-store auth wiring stays consistent across the codebase.
- When no identity is in scope, behavior is unchanged: the default credential chain is still used, so existing setups that relied on ambient credentials are unaffected.

## references

- closes #2369
- Mirrors the identity-aware store pattern in [`pkg/store/aws_ssm_param_store.go`](https://github.com/cloudposse/atmos/blob/main/pkg/store/aws_ssm_param_store.go) and [`pkg/store/authbridge/resolver.go`](https://github.com/cloudposse/atmos/blob/main/pkg/store/authbridge/resolver.go).

author: copilot
body:
Two issues addressed: tooltips appearing on the wrong monitor when the app is dragged to a secondary display positioned left of primary (negative x coordinates), and missing Save/Load buttons for Training Configuration.

## Tooltip multi-monitor positioning

`max(8, x)` clamping was snapping all negative x coordinates to `8` — the far-left edge of the primary monitor. Fix computes the virtual left edge of the widget's own monitor and clamps within that coordinate space:

```python
# Before — breaks for monitors with negative x origin
x = max(8, min(x, sw - tw - 8))

# After — monitor-aware clamping
mon_x = wx - (wx % sw) if sw else 0   # left edge of widget's monitor
x = max(mon_x + 8, min(x, mon_x + sw - tw - 8))
```

## Training Configuration Save / Load

- **💾 Save Config** / **📂 Load Config** button row added between the Queue controls and Start/Stop buttons
- Saves all settings to a JSON file: Project Name, Image Size, Epochs, Batch Size, Workers, Task Type, YOLO Model, all Advanced Training Options, and Class Names (in order)
- Default save filename: `ystraining-{project-name}-{YYYYMMDD-HHMM}.json` (spaces → `-`, lowercase)
- Both dialogs default to `~/Documents`; directory is shared via `_train_cfg_last_dir` — whichever dialog was used last sets the starting directory for both
- JSON is flat (advanced params not nested) for human readability/editability
- `task_type` added to `_get_current_job_config()` so it round-trips correctly through save/load

author: habdelra
body:
**Draft.** Brings back the desync detector by reverting commit `604364e6af` (which itself reverted #4521). We suspected that #4521 might have contributed to broken tests on main shortly after it landed, and reverted it out of an abundance of caution while we sorted out the signal. This PR brings the detector back so we can carry on the CS-10860 work.

Companion to #4541 (A: keep V8-captured exceptions on revoke). Together they cover the bug class:

- **A** changes *what's in* the error doc — V8-captured stack lands in `additionalErrors`.
- **B (this PR)** changes *when* the error doc gets created — the detector polls `[data-prerender-status]` after `model.status='ready'` and writes `data-prerender-status="unusable"` directly via Document API when the DOM is wedged, short-circuiting the 90s `cardRenderTimeout`.

## What's restored

- `packages/host/app/utils/render-desync-detector.ts` — the detector itself, including the backoff-poll grace window (hops at 50/200/500/1000/2000 ms, total ~3.75s) and the runtime knob `globalThis.__boxelDomDesyncSettleHopsMs` for live tuning.
- `packages/host/app/routes/render.ts` — wires `runDomDesyncCheck` into `#settleModelAfterRender`.
- `packages/realm-server/tests/prerendering-test.ts` — `desync-repro.gts` fixture + the integration test.
- `packages/software-factory/playwright.config.ts` and `.claude/skills/indexing-diagnostics/SKILL.md` — config and operator docs.

## Conflict resolution notes

The original #4521 also touched `packages/realm-server/prerender/{page-pool,render-runner}.ts`. Those files have since been further evolved by #4524 (runtime-exception-capture) and #4531 (shim-async-retry), in non-conflicting ways but with different surrounding context. The merge took **HEAD** on those — the post-#4524 versions are strict supersets of what #4521 contributed (the `stackFrames` field already exists, the `#formatConsoleErrorStack` helper now uses `stackHeaderForConsoleErrorEntry` which subsumes the original literal-header logic).

## Plan for this draft

Open as a draft and let CI run with the original grace value. Two reasons to start there rather than pre-emptively bumping:

1. The earlier failure profile may have changed. The SF harness preserves cloned modules cache now (#4528), main has gone through several merges since the revert, and the failure shape might no longer reproduce.
2. We need the empirical data to pick the right grace. If CI fails the same way as before, bump `DEFAULT_SETTLE_HOPS_MS` to something like `[100, 400, 1000, 3000, 7000]` (~11.5s) and re-run. If a smaller subset of tests fail, even narrower targeting is possible.

The runtime knob `globalThis.__boxelDomDesyncSettleHopsMs` is exposed precisely for this kind of iteration — we can also bump per-test if we identify a small set that's load-sensitive.

## Out of draft criteria

- [x] CI green (or grace tuned to make it green without disabling the detector for any production path)
- [ ] Whitepaper render URL hits the detector (verify via Chrome MCP visit + check error doc has `Render binding desync` title)

author: fkgozali
body:
Summary:
This test file contains a single `it.skip` test guarded by the comment "Enable once synchronous C++ state updates are re-introduced." That feature was deleted entirely (not just disabled) since 2025-07-15, with the reason: *"The current design of enableSynchronousStateUpdates is not correct and breaks `<Modal />` on Android. let's delete it.

Findings: A scan of `packages/react-native/src/private/featureflags`, `scripts/featureflags`, and `ReactCommon/react/featureflags` returns no replacement flag for synchronous C++ state updates. The `enableSynchronousStateUpdates` flag was removed from every layer (JS config, C++, Android Kotlin/JNI, iOS overrides, MC schemas) and the guarded code path in `EventQueue.cpp` was deleted as well.

Empirical confirmation: Removed the `it.skip` and ran the test 10x via stress runs. All 10 runs failed deterministically. The test is asserting the *presence* of the bug — i.e., that an intermediate state mutation leaks through when a UI-thread commit pulls transactions from an in-flight JS commit. Without the synchronous-state-updates codepath, that leak no longer occurs, so the test's expected log never matches the actual output:

  Expected: [Update ScrollView, Update intermediate-state-should-not-be-visible, Update view]
  Actual:   [Update view, Update ScrollView]

The test cannot be un-skipped (the bug it documents is no longer reproducible), and rewriting the assertion would defeat the purpose of the test. Deleting it.

author: koftwentytwo
body:
Closes #17.

## Problem

Each streaming provider's SSE parser had a `try { JSON.parse } catch { /* skip */ }` block that swallowed any well-formed event whose shape it didn't explicitly recognize — including upstream `error` events. A streaming call that errored mid-flight returned empty text with status 200, indistinguishable from a successful empty completion.

## Fix

Per-provider error event detection inside the SSE parser:
| Provider | Event shape detected |
|---|---|
| Anthropic | \`event.type === \"error\"\` → captures msg + type |
| OpenAI | \`event.error\` object → captures msg + type |
| Google | \`event.error\` object → captures msg + status |
| Ollama | \`event.error\` (string OR object — both shapes seen in the wild) |

Captured into a closure variable rather than thrown directly because `streamRequest`'s `onChunk` wraps consumer throws to keep the stream alive. After `streamRequest` resolves, providers throw the captured error — which means **partial pre-error tokens never surface as a successful CompletionResponse**.

Also extended each provider's streaming-fallback catch to re-throw \`<Provider> streaming error\` and \`TimeoutError\` instead of falling through to the non-streaming `httpFn` path. Without this fix the streaming error was silently retried via the non-streaming API, defeating the whole point.

## Tests

10 new tests in \`test/providers/streaming-errors.test.ts\`, two per provider plus a common-contract test:
- Mid-stream error event causes rejection with the upstream message
- Pre-error tokens NOT silently included as a successful result
- Error message includes provider name + error type for triage
- Ollama: covers both bare-string and object error shapes

## Coverage windfall

The streaming-errors tests exercised previously-untested code paths in all four providers, lifting global coverage:

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Lines | 82.19% | **90.93%** |
| Statements | 81.56% | 89.77% |
| Functions | 91.56% | 96.38% |
| Branches | 69.60% | 77.54% |

This delivers the global-coverage jump that audit issue #41 was scoped for, in this PR. Thresholds ratcheted: vitest lines 82→90, statements 81→89, functions 91→96, branches 69→77; \`.munitor.yml\` min_instruction 82→90.

## Test plan
- [x] \`npm run check\` passes locally (477 tests, 90.93% lines, all gates green)
- [ ] CI pr-checks workflow passes
- [ ] In Books vault: trigger a real Anthropic call with very low \`maxTokens\` to provoke an early error → review note shows \"Anthropic streaming error [...]:\" instead of \"0 words generated\"
